reviews.text:
Gardens by the Bay is truly an amazing place and definitely a must-visit attraction in Singapore. The entire area is beautifully designed, extremely clean, and very well maintained, making it a wonderful experience for visitors of all ages.

The Flower Dome and Cloud Forest offer a unique opportunity to see plants and flowers from different parts of the world. During our visit, we also experienced the Tulip Feast, where we saw many beautiful varieties of tulips in full bloom. The colorful display was absolutely stunning and added a vibrant touch to the overall experience. The indoor waterfall inside the Cloud Forest is especially impressive and creates a refreshing atmosphere. The Supertree Grove is another major highlight, and the night light show there feels absolutely magical with the music and colorful lights.

The whole place is spacious and easy to explore, although there is a lot to walk around, so it can feel a little tiring after some time. Still, the beautiful views and attractions make the walking completely worth it.

There are many perfect photo spots throughout the gardens, especially during the evening when the night view looks stunning. Souvenir shops are also available if you would like to buy gifts or memories from your visit.

Overall, it’s a peaceful and beautiful place to relax, enjoy nature, and experience one of Singapore’s most iconic attractions. Highly recommended, especially for first-time visitors.

reviews.text:
Gardens by the Bay is truly a highlight of Singapore and absolutely not to be missed. I’d highly recommend getting a combo ticket for the Cloud Forest and Flower Dome—plan for about 2-3 hours to cover both.

The Cloud Forest is spectacular, almost Jurassic Park-like in parts, and enjoyable for both kids and adults. There’s misting at specific times, so it’s worth checking those in advance. A great way to explore is to head to the top level first and then make your way down, stopping at the different exhibits along the way.
The Flower Dome is equally beautiful, showcasing flowers and plants from around the world, with plenty of photo-worthy corners throughout. There’s also a nice gift shop with garden and flower-themed souvenirs.

I also got a separate ticket for the OCBC Skyway and it was 100% worth it. I went up right at 7:45 PM during the light and sound show and got to watch it from the top—an incredible experience. You can stay up for about 15 minutes, and while there’s an elevator, lines to go can get long.

For food, the Jurassic-themed food court nearby is a good option for dinner. Overall, it felt like a well-spent ~$60 to explore all three places. I’d suggest going after 3 PM and spending the entire evening there to fully enjoy the whole area.

reviews.text:
Merlion is one of the most iconic landmarks in Singapore and a must-visit destination for tourists visiting the city. Located at Marina Bay, the famous half-lion and half-fish statue represents Singapore’s history as a fishing village and its nickname, “Lion City.” The area offers a beautiful waterfront atmosphere with stunning views of Marina Bay Sands and the city skyline.

The location is very clean, organized, and perfect for taking photos, especially during sunset and nighttime when the city lights create an amazing view. Many visitors enjoy walking around the bay area, relaxing by the waterfront, and experiencing the lively atmosphere with nearby attractions, restaurants, and shopping areas.

The Merlion Park is also easily accessible by public transport and is a great spot for both first-time visitors and families. While it can become crowded during peak tourist hours, the overall experience is still enjoyable and worth visiting when in Singapore.

Overall, the Merlion is more than just a photo spot — it is a symbol of Singapore’s culture, tourism, and modern city charm. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Singapore.

reviews.text:
I noticed that a number of these reviews are not meant for the Expo and Convention Centre. I attended a conference here last week so the following is my take.

It is impressive. The design, the hospitality, the amenities, the scent, you name it. And it is huge.

The toilets are well-maintained and the staff are helpful. The electronic displays are always updated, you cannot get lost finding the floor or even the room that you need to be in.

Once you are there, just have a moment to look around. Many of the things around you, even the small ones that may go unnoticed, are meant to be part of the pleasant experience of the visitor.

reviews.text:
Our recent stay at Marina Bay Sands was a fantastic experience overall. We had a beautiful room with a balcony overlooking the gardens, which gave us the perfect view of the nightly light show. It was such a great way to end each evening.

The staff on the hotel side truly bend over backwards to make your stay enjoyable. They are constantly checking to make sure you have everything you need and always do so with warmth and professionalism.  The amenities in the room and the gifts were really special.

As expected, this is an incredibly popular and iconic hotel, which does mean there are quite a few procedures in place to manage access to the facilities. Non-hotel guests are mostly unable to access the pool and restaurants, which is understandable, but we did find the rooftop bar experience a little over the top. Even as hotel guests, we needed a wrist stamp, wristband, and had to hand over our credit card for the duration of our visit.

The infinity pool really is as amazing as it looks online. However, it’s worth noting that there are no umbrellas, and the cabanas are both difficult to secure and surprisingly hot due to the lack of airflow. One fantastic touch was the complimentary sunscreen available at the pool, which saved us as we hadn’t brought any.

The hotel is attached to a casino, and it definitely carries that atmosphere throughout parts of the property. That said, the location is exceptional. It's directly connected to a high-end shopping mall, a great food court, and with easy access to the gardens and surrounding attractions.

Overall, despite a few small frustrations with the bar, it’s an impressive hotel experience and absolutely worth staying at least once for the experience.

This is a must-see hotel, but keep in mind that it is not a business hotel and is crowded with tourists. Especially in the mornings, you may experience longer waiting times.

The infinity pool is exclusively for hotel guests, so to enjoy this experience, you must stay at the hotel.

For room selection, the city view is preferable if you are above mid-level floors. Lower city-facing rooms may have their view partially blocked by the shopping mall.

The Gardens by the Bay view is also beautiful—you can watch the Supertree light show and enjoy the sea view. However, it is a more static and calm scenery. Personally, I prefer the high-floor city view, where you can also watch the Merlion light show, which feels more dynamic and lively.

reviews.text:
Lau Pa Sat: A must-visit for the lively night vibe!

I visited at 9 PM on a Friday, and it was absolutely crowded! The energy outside on Satay Street was incredible, with everyone enjoying grilled food in the open air. Inside the historic building, there are plenty of food stalls to choose from.

The Drinks:
One thing to watch out for is that there are very few drink stalls, so the lines are very long. I bought an Iced Mango Peach ($2.80), but I wouldn't recommend it. It was extremely sweet and didn't contain any fresh fruit—it tasted mostly like syrup. I suggest skipping the "juices" here if you want something fresh.

The Food & Service:
I tried the Thunder Tea Rice ($6.20). It was okay, though it didn't quite fit my personal taste. After eating, the service is efficient; you can either clear your own tray or wait for the staff who come by frequently to collect them.

The Verdict:
It is very crowded and noisy with loud music, but it’s a "must-visit" to experience the local Singaporean vibe. Just be prepared for the crowds!

reviews.text:
🏬 Suntec City – 4.5 stars

Suntec City is one of those malls in Singapore that feels huge but still easy to walk around. There’s a good mix of shopping, restaurants, cafés, and even office spaces, so it’s always lively but not overwhelming.

What I like is the variety — you can find everything from affordable eats to nicer dining spots, plus fashion, lifestyle stores, and specialty coffee places. It’s very convenient if you’re spending the whole day in the area.

The layout is quite spacious, and it connects well to nearby attractions and MRT, which makes it practical for both locals and tourists. It’s not the most luxurious mall in Singapore, but it’s reliable, comfortable, and has everything you need in one place.

Overall, a solid shopping and dining destination. Great for casual hangouts, meetings, or just walking around and exploring. ✨

A complex of Fountain of Wealth, Convention & Exhibition Centre, Shopping Mall & 5 Towers of Business Centres.

"Fountain of Wealth
(The heart of Suntec City)
Visit the heart of Suntec City - the stunning Fountain of Wealth, a symbol of wealth and life. Recognised in 1998 by the Guinness Book of World Records as the World's Largest Fountain, the bronze ring of the fountain is designed based on the Hindu Mandala (or "universe") and is a symbolic representation of the oneness in spirit and unity, representing the quality and harmony of all races and religions. Soak in the positive “qi” energy at the fountain by encircling the fountain clockwise three times, stretching out your right hand over the water, as you make a silent wish and let the wonders unfold."

We visited Maxwell Food Centre at around 8:00 AM on a Monday, so it was still relatively quiet with very few queues. Unfortunately, the famous chicken rice stall was closed, which was a bit disappointing. This was actually my second visit, and I still haven't had the chance to try it!

Thankfully, there are plenty of other stalls serving chicken rice, so we simply picked one without a line and it didn't disappoint. In fact, that's the beauty of Maxwell Food Centre. There are so many food options to choose from, and everything we tried was delicious. The drinks were great too, and the prices are very affordable. Those in the pictures are only some of those we found really delicious.

Whether you're craving local favorites or just looking for a good meal, Maxwell Food Centre never disappoints. If you're in Singapore, make sure to stop by for delicious food at budget-friendly prices. Just keep in mind that if you're hoping to try the famous chicken rice, it's worth checking the stall's opening hours before you go!

places.address: 665 Buffalo Road Zhujiao Centre, Tekka, Market, Singapore 210665

reviews.text:
Tucked within the vibrant heart of Tekka Food Centre, 蒸好味 Steamed Fish Cuisine is a quiet ode to the beauty of honest, well-executed cooking.

What sets this humble gem apart is its unwavering commitment to freshness — each fish is live-caught for the day, delivering a delicate sweetness that simply cannot be replicated. Gently steamed to perfection, the flesh remains tender and succulent, elevated only by a refined touch of ginger and scallion that enhances rather than overpowers. Every bite speaks of clarity, balance, and respect for the ingredient.

Equally noteworthy is their steamed egg — a silky, comforting masterpiece crafted from real eggs cracked fresh on the spot, not pre-mixed liquid substitutes. The result is a custard-like texture that is impossibly smooth, rich, and deeply satisfying.

In a setting as bustling as Tekka, this stall stands out not through extravagance, but through precision, sincerity, and an unwavering dedication to quality. A true hidden indulgence for those who appreciate the quiet luxury of simplicity done exceptionally well.

reviews.text:
🟠 City Square Mall
180 Kitchener Road
Singapore 208539

🟣 Location =  🟣 the mall is located at the junction of Serangoon Road and Kitchener Road.

🟣 It is directly connected to the Farrer Park MRT station via B1 level passage-way.
______________________________________________
⬛️  Historical Context: The mall actually sits on the former site of the New World Amusement Park, which was a famous landmark in the Jalan Besar area for decades.

⬛️  When I was a child in the early 1970s, my late Peranakan father used to bring me to New World to jalan jalan.
________________________________________________
🟠 The mall had undergone a SGD50 million massive revamp from September 2023 to early 2026.

🟠  The revamp added 26,000 sq ft of space, featuring a new 24,000 sq ft "Gastro Square" Level 4 dining area, new playgrounds, and classy luxurious interior upgrades.

🟨 The perimeters ( outside stretch of the mall)
*************************************************
🟨  There is a small verdant green park at the back of the mall, where a decomissioned MRT train cabin sits. ▪︎It is a hub for educational purposes.

🟨 There is also a small Merry-Go-Round & a Tea Cup Spinning Ride, reminiscent of the rides I used to enjoy in the 1970s.

🟩 For the interior of the mall itself
************************************
➡️ Below Info ➡️  is from the lift directory panel.

🟩L1 = City Green

🟩 B1 = Underpass to MRT, Taxi Stand, Pick-Up & Drop-Off, Green Square/ NTUC Fairprice/ Q&M Medical & Dental

🟩 B2=  ATM / Customer Service Counter/ Don Donki

🟩 B3=  Car Park + Food Square + Food Republic

🟩 B4= Car Park

⬛️ L9 To L6 = Schools & Offices  + Singapore Sustainability Academy (SSA)

⬛️ L5 = Discovery Square & Golden Village Cinema

⬛️ L4=  Gastro Square & CONNECT @ City Square Mall ( 🔴5 social service agencies)

⬛️ L 3 =  MST Golf Super Store

⬛️ L2 =  Decathlon & Uniqlo
________________________________________
🔴 Important info:
*******************
🔴 Level 4 features a CONNECT at City Square Mall, a dedicated community space comprising 5 ( five) social service agencies, affiliated with NCSS ( ▪︎National Council of Social Services), which itself is a statutory board under MSF.

🔴 MSF = Ministry of Social and Family Development.

🔴 The five agencies on Level 4 are
**************************************
● Counselling and Care Centre
● Kampong Kapor Community Services
● Singapore Children’s Society
● The Salvation Army

● Eagles Mediation & Counselling Centre ➡️ at B2 level

➖️ Dated 24 March 2026/ Tuesday.

The directory includes a well-stocked supermarket, numerous fashion boutiques, electronics retailers, and a wide selection of dining options ranging from quick bites to sit-down restaurants. The layout is generally logical, though it can take some time to navigate due to the sheer size of the complex. It serves as an excellent one-stop destination for both daily necessities and specialty items. Facilities like restrooms and parking are well-maintained and accessible. Given the extensive range of shops and services available under one roof, it is a highly practical choice for weekend errands or casual browsing. However, because of its comprehensive nature, it tends to attract large crowds, especially during peak hours and weekends. Overall, it provides a highly efficient and reliable shopping experience for visitors looking to complete multiple tasks in a single trip.

reviews.text:
Lucky Plaza: A Vibrant Piece of Singapore History

If you want to experience a different side of Orchard Road, Lucky Plaza is the place to be. While surrounded by ultra-modern, high-end luxury malls, Lucky Plaza holds its own as a bustling, soul-filled "vertical bazaar" that has stood the test of time.

History & ArchitectureCompleted in 1981 (with the shopping podium opening as early as 1977), it was developed by the legendary Far East Organization. At the time of its debut, it was a pioneer of modern retail:

It was one of the first malls in the world to be fully air-conditioned.

It featured the first "glass bubble lift" in Southeast Asia, which was a massive attraction in the late 70s and 80s.

The building was constructed on the former site of "Motor Row," where Champion Motors once stood.

Property Details
Unlike many newer developments on 99-year leases, Lucky Plaza is a Freehold property. This rare tenure is part of why the building has remained such a resilient and valuable landmark in the heart of District 9. The 30-storey complex is a mixed-use development, with the first six floors dedicated to retail and the upper floors housing 88 residential apartments.

The Vibe Today
Today, it is famously known as a cultural hub, especially for the Filipino community. It’s the best spot in town for authentic Filipino food (don't miss the lechon or halo-halo!), affordable electronics, perfumes, and currency exchange.

Pro-tip: It gets incredibly crowded on Sundays, which creates a festive, high-energy atmosphere. If you prefer a quieter walk-through to admire the retro architecture, try visiting on a weekday morning!

reviews.text:
I learned a lot about Singapore’s history through the museum’s interactive multimedia exhibits and high-quality visuals, which made the experience feel immersive and engaging. From its early days as a fishing village to its rise as a global metropolis, you really get a sense of the hard work and vision that shaped Singapore into what it is today.

What I especially appreciated was how values-driven the museum felt. During our visit, there was an activity where Singaporeans were encouraged to write heartfelt letters to expatriates, and there were also several exhibits showing what life was like for expats working in Singapore and the kinds of jobs they held. Older generations were also given space to share their stories with younger visitors, which added a meaningful intergenerational element to the experience.

Everything felt centered on connection, empathy, and understanding, and that was the theme I loved most about the museum.

The building itself is also beautiful, with plenty of photo spots throughout, so it’s easy to take nice pictures to share with friends.

The only caveat is that the Singapore Odyssea exhibition is a little pricey, so we ended up visiting the free option, Once Upon a Tide, instead. Even so, it was still well worth seeing.

A great stop if you’re looking for something educational, meaningful, and family-friendly.

reviews.text:
Well known hawker centre that once upon a time catered mostly to tourists.

But locals are now crowding the place because of the good food and the variety and because the Singapore Tourism Board has successfully clamped down some seafood stalls touting and scamming patrons, especially tourists, with exorbitant prices.

This is one hawker centre where you will find people from all over the world savouring local street food of all races in Singapore which originated from China, India,  Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand,  etc and even the US.

Beer by the jugs are served here.

Most stalls are closed for lunch. But it is usually quite difficult to get a table during dinner time, especially on weekends. Sharing table is the norm.  So be willing to do so.

Queuing at some stalls to collect your own order is also the norm.

This hawker centre, including the free toilets, are very clean and airy. There are basins all over for patrons to wash their hands before and after meals
meals.

Pay when you order. In cash or via your phone transfer.

There is an adjoining carpark. A huge one. But it can still be hard to find a parking space during dinner time.

The Newton MRT is very near by.

Sultan Mosque in Singapore is an iconic landmark and a must-visit for anyone interested in culture and architecture. The mosque’s golden domes and intricate details are truly breathtaking, reflecting rich Islamic heritage. The surrounding area, Kampong Glam, is vibrant with colorful streets, local shops, and cafes, making the visit even more enjoyable.

The mosque is well-maintained, peaceful, and welcoming to visitors. Non-Muslims are allowed to visit outside prayer times, and there are informative displays that provide insight into its history and significance. Photography is allowed in designated areas, allowing you to capture its beauty.

Overall, Sultan Mosque is not only a place of worship but also a cultural gem in Singapore, offering a deep sense of history and artistry. Highly recommended for travelers and culture enthusiasts alike.

reviews.text:
Sultan Mosque, located in the heart of Arab Street, is one of Singapore’s most iconic and beautiful mosques.
Its large golden dome and white exterior stand out beautifully, and the contrast with the colorful shophouses around it makes it very photogenic.

Visitors are required to remove their shoes before entering the mosque.
If your legs are exposed, such as when wearing shorts or a skirt, a covering skirt is provided free of charge at the entrance, so you can visit without worry.

When I visited, the staff at the reception was Japanese and kindly assisted us in Japanese, which was very reassuring.
They also explained the rules and background of the mosque in a friendly and easy-to-understand way, making it very welcoming to visitors.

Inside, the atmosphere is calm and serene, quite different from the lively streets outside.
It is a peaceful place worth visiting while exploring Arab Street.

They also explained the rules and background of the mosque in a friendly and easy-to-understand way, making it very welcoming to visitors.

Inside, the atmosphere is calm and serene, quite different from the lively streets outside.
It is a peaceful place worth visiting while exploring Arab Street.

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (4/5)
Mustafa Centre is one of the most famous shopping malls in Singapore, and for a good reason. It’s open 24/7, making it incredibly convenient for anyone to shop at any time of the day or night.

• Best Prices: Almost all goods are sold at very reasonable and competitive prices.
• One-Stop Shop: From electronics and jewelry to groceries and souvenirs, you can find everything here. It’s the go-to spot for foreigners and migrant workers to buy gifts and essentials for their families back home before vacation.
Important Tip for Shoppers:
I highly recommend checking the expiry dates on all food and consumable items before you buy. Try to ensure they have at least one year of validity.
My Experience: I’ve had issues multiple times where I bought items in bulk, but since the expiry date was too close, I couldn't finish them in time. This is a big waste of money, so please double-check your basket before heading to the cashier!

Mustafa Centre is one of the most unique shopping experiences in Singapore. Located in the heart of Little India, this massive multi-level store literally has everything — from electronics and perfumes to groceries, souvenirs, jewelry, clothing, and even travel essentials.
What makes it even more impressive is that it’s open 24 hours a day. Whether you need something late at night or just enjoy browsing without crowds during off-peak hours, it’s incredibly convenient.
The store can feel a bit overwhelming at first because it’s packed floor-to-ceiling with products and narrow aisles, but that’s part of its charm. Prices are competitive, and you can often find great deals, especially on chocolates, cosmetics, and electronics.
If you’re staying in the Little India area or nearby, it’s definitely worth a visit — even if just to see how massive and diverse the selection is. A true Singapore experience for shoppers.

I ate here regularly on a short visit to Singapore mainly because of positive reviews and also it was a walkable distance from my hotel. I enjoyed a variety of dishes in the hawker centre both breakfasts and dinners at  different vendors.
Tiong Bahru Market is an old school, popular, hawker centre with a deserved good reputation. Hosting a wide range of hawker stalls on the first floor with ample seating it is a fairly comfortable venue in hot and sticky Singapore with decent fans to cool the dining areas.
Although only one of the many local hawker centres in Singapore, Tiong Bahru Market is worth a visit for its old school charm and range of delicious food served at the numerous hawker stalls.  I will undoubtedly eat there again on a future visit to Singapore.

Food options are solid across the board. You’ve got all the classics done well from chwee kueh to lor mee to chicken rice. Easy to just follow the queues and you won’t go wrong. Prices still very reasonable too.

Crowd is more local which gives it a nice authentic vibe. Only thing is many stalls close by mid afternoon, so come earlier.

Great spot for a proper hawker fix without the chaos. Parking available around as well but pretty limited.

reviews.text: This was our second visit to Ce La Vi since we had a great experience here during our last visit to Singapore 7 years ago. We opted for its Saturday set course Brunch.  We tried its snapper, chicken and beef ribs.  All three main course were properly prepared and presented.  The appetizers (except for the Foie Gras could be better if it was lightly grilled, a purely personal preference) and the deserts were equally well done.  The staff was friendly and the setting was priceless.  In addition, we get to stay at its Sky Lounge after our meal, but we didn’t have time. Added bonus, there was even a pretty good magician entertaining us and other guests while we waited for our food.  One thing to note: the guest will take a dedicated elevator to the top of the Marina Sand Hotel that is saturated right by the main entrance.  However, we were turned away because we were 5 minutes early from our reservation.  So, don’t arrive early.  If you are short on time when visiting Singapore, then make this your must stop for a decent meal and unforgettable views.

reviews.text:
It was a last-minute reservation after we watched Les Misérables, and it was a good thing they still had a slot for dinner at their restaurant. The staff and crew were very pleasant and accommodating. From the moment we entered CÉ LA VI, the two staff at the front desk were cheerful and welcoming.

Mannan was the staff member who took our order, and even though I asked several times if we could change seats, he really made an effort to accommodate us. He was also very kind and patient when we asked for food recommendations, and he explained everything clearly. He was very knowledgeable about the menu. He was also very courteous; he asked what we were celebrating and even took a lovely photo and video for us.

About the food: Everything was so good, and the portions were generous. I especially loved the Mushroom Truffle Korokke, and the Short Rib was so tender it melted in our mouths. For dessert, I really enjoyed the Dark Chocolate Fondant, and thank you as well for the complimentary cake! That was such a kind and generous gesture.

Environment: Initially, the table we were seated at was a bit noisy because the speaker was very near us, which is why I kept asking Mannan if we could change seats. Thankfully, when we moved, it was much better. The atmosphere became peaceful, and we got to enjoy the beautiful view of Singapore.

Overall: The whole experience was exemplary, and we’re so glad we chose CÉ LA VI to celebrate our anniversary. We will definitely come back again and bring our families next time.

Once our table was ready we were taken to our table, great location too, outside under the red canopy overlooking Singapore.
Our waiter Mannan was fantastic! He was extremely helpful and was able to recommend dishes. He was always at hand and made sure we were comfortable.
All the dishes we ordered were fantastic. They were all tasty, full of delicious flavour. As a little birthday treat for my husband they came over with a candle & cake and sang happy birthday to him. Which was very special.
We didn't feel rushed at all and after the meal we went to the bar to have more drinks and take lots of pictures of the views.
Such a stunning restaurant one I will cherish for a long time.

reviews.text:
We arrived at the hotel at approximately 9:30 AM. While we understood that the official check-in time is 3:00 PM, we requested an early check-in as we were traveling as a family of three, including an infant, and had just completed a long and exhausting flight.

Our request was denied on the grounds that the hotel was fully booked and that only an Executive Room was available. However, we were told that we would need to pay an additional SGD 280 per night for this room, which is a two-category upgrade from the room we had originally booked.

As an Accor Gold member, I was disappointed by this response, especially since the available room was not a suite. Furthermore, our reservation was made using Stay Plus, where the second night is complimentary. Therefore, if an upgrade charge was applicable, it should reasonably have been applied only to the paid night rather than both nights.

I explained that I did not require an upgrade and simply requested any available room where my family, particularly our infant, could freshen up and rest after the flight. This request was also denied.

During the interaction, the staff member appeared reluctant to show room availability information, which led me to question whether the hotel was genuinely sold out. Unfortunately, I was left with no practical alternative and felt compelled to pay the upgrade fee for both nights, even though the second night was complimentary under the Stay Plus benefit.

This was one of the most disappointing customer service experiences I have encountered during my travels. The handling of the situation lacked empathy and flexibility, particularly considering that we were traveling with a young child. I expected a much higher standard of hospitality from Swissotel.

reviews.text:
This Hindu temple looks good from the outside, but once you get inside (no shoes) it is even more impressive. There were several outer buildings that looked to be for various different gods, where I saw people worshipping in small groups. There were also multiple offerings and ceremonies going on at the same time at these individual areas.

But inside the main building it was full of captivating statues and paintings. Some of these statues ran along the tops of the walls up to the ceilings, and they were fascinating and beautiful. This temple was crowded, but it was still easy to get around. Free to enter, and most certainly worth a visit. Take your time walking through this place of worship.

Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple in the Little India central area is a very famous and powerful Amman temple. The temple has a strong divine energy and peaceful atmosphere. Sri Durgai Amma looks so beautiful, blessed, and graceful like a loving mother. When we worship here, we can truly feel her happiness and protection.
It feels like we can enter the temple only with Veeramakaliamman’s blessings and permission. Her divine presence is powerful and comforting. In this temple, we can also see Samayapuram Mariamman and Lord Vishwanathan with Visalakshi Amman.
A very sacred and powerful place for prayers and blessings. Amma’s blessings are always with us. 🙏✨

We visited Chinatown Singapore, and it was truly a vibrant and memorable experience.
This place is like a lively market filled with everything—from trendy clothes like Asian-style jeans to souvenirs and daily-use items, all in beautiful and vibrant colours. The entire area feels energetic and full of life.
What really stood out was how polite and kind the people were. The streets were clean and well-maintained, which made walking around even more enjoyable.
There’s also a lovely temple you can visit, adding a peaceful and cultural touch to the experience. And of course, the food is amazing! From delicious Chinese street food to ice creams and fresh juices, everything was well-prepared and enjoyable.
Overall, it’s a must-visit place—not just for shopping, but to truly experience the lively atmosphere and colourful vibe of Singapore.

Bras basah Complex is one of the oldest malls we have been going since young.

This is one of the places to go for art resources. We would usually go to the Art-Fren and popular here. But since that was the usual places, we decided to venture out abit this time..

There are different lifts for commercial and residential. If you are heading up to the shops, you can also take the escalator up. Its rather easily accessible to many vendors, so you can shop around from one to another.

One more thing to note, carpark is slightly lower than normal. There are visual signs of vehicles hitting the beam within the carpark itself. So if you do have a vehicle higher than 1.8m, we would suggest to avoid coming and parking here.

Check out our images for the ways around this complex. And hope you guys don't get lost..

Cheers!

reviews.text:
Bras Basah Complex feels like a surviving time capsule from Singapore in the 1980s and 1990s. Walking through the corridors brought back memories of old-school bookshops, watch repair stores, art supply shops, music stores, printing services, and hobby retailers that used to be much more common in Singapore. It is honestly quite surprising - and refreshing - that this place is still around despite all the redevelopment happening elsewhere

The building itself has a very nostalgic charm with its open-air design, older architecture, and quieter atmosphere compared to modern malls. It may not be flashy, but that is part of the appeal. There is something enjoyable about slowly wandering around and discovering long-established independent shops that have clearly been operating for decades

reviews.text:
The soup looks quite light in color at first, but don’t be fooled by its appearance. The peppery taste is actually quite strong and gives a warm, comforting kick from the very first sip. The stewed pork ribs are extremely soft and tender, falling off the bone easily and soaking up all the rich flavors of the soup.

What makes it even better is the balance of taste. The spice is noticeable but not overwhelming, and it blends well with the deep, savory broth. Every spoonful feels warm and satisfying, making the soup very enjoyable to eat.

Even though we had already eaten earlier in the day, the taste of this soup was so good that it made us want to keep eating. It felt hearty and comforting, and it gave us a sense of warmth and energy after the meal.

Overall, it is a very satisfying soup that is both flavorful and comforting. It is the kind of dish that makes you feel full in a good way and leaves a lasting impression.

reviews.text:
Seah Im Food Centre is a fantastic spot right beside the HarbourFront bus interchange and MRT. It’s well-ventilated and generally very clean for a busy hawker center.

If you aren't sure where to start, the three stalls facing the main road are top-tier (non-halal):
• Chai Kee Braised Duck (财记卤鸭): Tender meat and great sauce.
• Shi Cheng Prawn Noodles (狮城虾面): Rich, flavorful broth.
• Queen Coffee: Excellent brews to pair with your meal.

On the row facing the bus interchange, Good Luck Fishball Noodles is also a solid choice—definitely worth a try. There is also a huge variety of Malay stalls here, offering everything from Ayam Penyet to Mee Rebus.
Great location, plenty of variety, and a clean environment!

places.name: Mediway Medical Centre
places.address: 20 Upper Circular Rd, #B1-26/29 The Riverwalk, Singapore 058416

reviews.text:
I went to Mediway Medical Centre on Saturday, 11 July 2026 for a health screening - the Deluxe package with add-on ECG and Xray.

Just want to say a big thank you for the efficient, organised, and professional service from the whole team.

Special shoutout to Mr Faruk, who did my blood test. He drew 3 big tubes of blood and it was completely painless, thumbs up for that !

Also want to thank Ms Nandini, who helped with my ECG and other tests. She was friendly, efficient, and clearly knew what she was doing 👍

The whole process was smooth from start to finish, no long waiting times, and the staff explained things clearly along the way. You can tell this is a well-run centre that genuinely cares about patient comfort.

Highly recommend Mediway Medical Centre for anyone looking to do a health screening. Will definitely be back for my next checkup.

Thanks again to the team ❤️

reviews.text:
It was my first time visiting Mediway Medical, and I genuinely only have positive things to share.
From the moment I arrived now I left, the entire experience was smooth and impressive. Despite the crowd, Aishah remained friendly, efficient, and well-organized. My family of four did the PR medical check, and we did not have to wait long at all.
The nurse who attended to us named Vigneswari was equally warm and patient. She explained everything clearly and guided us step-by-step on which stations to proceed to for the X-ray and blood test.
After we completed the whole process, the manager Steven personally checked in with us to ensure we had received the receipt via email and informed us that the report would be sent on the next working day. We truly appreciated this extra care.
The clinic’s location is also very convenient. I would recommend Mediway Medical to others.

places.name: Timbre+ One North
places.address: 73A Ayer Rajah Cres., JTC LaunchPad @ one-north, Singapore 139957

reviews.text:
Timbre+ One North is a great dining destination in Singapore's One North district, offering a vibrant atmosphere that appeals to a wide range of visitors. Whether you are meeting colleagues after work, catching up with friends, hosting a casual business discussion, or simply looking for a good meal, it provides a welcoming and comfortable setting.

One of its biggest strengths is the variety of food available. With options ranging from Indian and Chinese cuisine to continental dishes and local favourites, there is something to suit almost every taste and preference. This makes it an excellent choice for groups with diverse food interests.

The venue is clean, well organized, and efficiently managed, creating a pleasant dining experience even during busy periods. The lively yet relaxed environment makes it suitable for both working lunches and social gatherings.

Good food, reasonable prices, and a wide selection of cuisines make Timbre+ One North a place that offers excellent value for money and is well worth a visit when in the area.

reviews.text: Room felt luxurious and was very comfortable. Pool area was gorgeous and being tucked away at the rear of the hotel, is quite tranquil. There was also a dedicated lifeguard, which added piece of mind. The hotel has a direct link to neighbouring Tanglin Mall (convenient for any last minute shopping, pharmacy, restaurants etc.). I also used the 'business lounge' which has a couple of desk pods, plus a 'guest use' PC. This is offered on a first come first serve basis, but I was the only one there on the day I worked from there. The on-site buffet restaurant was a genuine stand-out, offering a premium and varied food and drink selection - I can recommendit for sure! The staff we interacted with in both the hotel and restaurant were all extremely professional and courteous.

★★★★★ Excellent Stay – Highly Recommended for Club Members
As a club member, my stay at JEN Tanglin Singapore was consistently impressive and well worth it. The hotel strikes a great balance between comfort, convenience, and thoughtful service.
The club benefits really elevate the experience. Check-in was smooth and efficient, and the lounge access was a definite highlight—quiet, well-maintained, and perfect for both relaxing and getting some work done. The food and beverage offerings were generous and well presented, especially during evening refreshments.
The rooms were clean, modern, and comfortable, with good soundproofing and all the essentials you’d expect. Housekeeping was attentive without being intrusive, which I really appreciated.
Location is another strong point. Being close to Orchard Road and public transport makes getting around Singapore easy, while the hookup to Tanglin Mall adds extra convenience for dining and shopping.
Most importantly, the staff were warm, professional, and genuinely attentive throughout my stay. As a club member, I felt recognized and well taken care of, which makes a big difference.
Overall, JEN Tanglin Singapore delivers excellent value and a consistently high standard of service. I would definitely return and highly recommend it—especially for fellow club members looking for a reliable, comfortable stay in Singapore.

We had a truly wonderful stay at Fairmont Singapore.

As an Accor member, I have stayed at many properties within the group, and this experience was truly outstanding. From check-in to check-out, every member of the staff was warm, friendly, and professional. The level of service was exceptional and made us feel genuinely cared for throughout our stay.

One gesture that particularly stood out was when my husband needed an additional power outlet for his CPAP machine. The hotel staff went above and beyond to assist us and made every effort to accommodate his needs. Their willingness to help was greatly appreciated.

Another thoughtful touch was returning to our room after dinner to find everything perfectly tidied and refreshed. Bottled water had even been placed beside the bed, making us feel especially comfortable and well looked after.

It is the attention to detail and genuine hospitality that made our stay so memorable. Thank you to the entire Fairmont Singapore team for providing such outstanding service and making us feel truly welcome.

We will definitely be returning in the future and highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting Singapore. Thank you, Fairmont Singapore, for an exceptional experience!

reviews.text:
During my stay in Singapore, I visited Chinatown Food Street almost every day.  It became one of my favorite places to eat and explore as a solo traveler.

There are so many food options available, from local Singaporean dishes to Chinese specialties, all at reasonable prices. The atmosphere is lively, especially in the evening, and it is a great place to experience Singapore’s food culture.

The location is easy to reach, clean, and surrounded by shops and interesting attractions. I always felt comfortable walking around and trying different foods each day.

I highly recommend Chinatown Food Street to anyone visiting Singapore, especially solo travelers looking for delicious food, a vibrant atmosphere, and an authentic local experience.

places.address: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Marina Bay Sands, Hotel, Level 57 Tower 1, Singapore 018956

reviews.text:
A truly memorable dining experience at LAVO Italian Restaurant & Rooftop Bar in Marina Bay Sands, Singapore. The atmosphere is exceptional, and the views are absolutely stunning—one of the best skyline experiences in the city.

A special mention to Sarah, who was incredibly helpful and attentive throughout the visit. Her warm service really elevated the entire experience and made everything feel smooth and welcoming.

There are also a few good vegetarian options available, which makes the menu more inclusive than expected. The pasta is a must-try—perfectly cooked and full of flavor, and something everyone should experience.

The combination of great food, excellent service, and that breathtaking view makes this a place everyone should visit at least once when in Singapore. Highly recommended for both the ambience and the overall vibe.

reviews.text:
We visited LAVO to celebrate our wedding anniversary, and it turned out to be a truly memorable evening.

The restaurant offers both indoor and outdoor seating, and knowing it was a special occasion for us, the team thoughtfully arranged a table outdoors overlooking the stunning Singapore CBD skyline at night. The breeze, view, and overall ambience made the experience especially enjoyable.

Service was phenomenal from start to finish. Our server (unfortunately, I can't recall his name) was attentive without ever being intrusive, checking in at just the right moments. A particularly thoughtful gesture stood out; when we realised a mocktail ordered for my wife contained an ingredient she couldn’t take due to her pregnancy, he immediately replaced it without hesitation and insisted we keep the original as well. That level of care was genuinely appreciated.

The food and drinks were top notch, and notably well-priced for the location and ambience, which made the overall experience even more satisfying.

To top it off, we were surprised with a complimentary dessert, complete with a “Happy Anniversary” message delicately written on marzipan; a simple but meaningful touch that made the evening feel even more special.

It was the perfect dinner for our wedding anniversary, and we would gladly return for another special occasion.

reviews.text:
I just had one of the most unforgettable dining experiences of my life at LAVO Italian Restaurant & Rooftop Bar at Marina Bay Sands, and I’m still floating on cloud nine. If there were more than seven stars to give, this place would earn them all. From the moment you step out onto the 57th floor, you’re transported to a sun-kissed Italian coastal dream with Singapore’s glittering skyline as the backdrop. Absolute magic. ￼
The views are nothing short of breathtaking. Perched high above the city with wraparound panoramic vistas, especially at night when the lights sparkle like diamonds across Marina Bay — it’s pure romance and wow-factor. The rooftop terrace vibe is sophisticated yet lively, with that perfect energy that makes you want to linger for hours. Whether you’re there for sunset or after dark, it’s one of the best rooftop experiences in Singapore. ￼
Now, onto the food — oh my goodness. I ordered the Spaghetti Tomato and Basil, and it was an absolute masterpiece. Fresh, vibrant, perfectly al dente pasta coated in a light, aromatic sauce that let the sweet tomatoes and fragrant basil shine. Simple ingredients elevated to perfection — it tasted like it was flown straight from Italy. And the mushroom pizza? Life-changing. Crispy, chewy crust with generous wild mushrooms, earthy flavors, and that melty cheese pull that dreams are made of. Every bite was heavenly — flavorful, well-balanced, and cooked to absolute perfection in their stone oven. ￼
The portions were generous, the ingredients top-tier, and everything felt fresh and thoughtfully prepared. Paired with the stunning setting, it was a sensory explosion. Service was warm, attentive, and made us feel like VIPs throughout.
LAVO isn’t just a meal — it’s an experience. Whether you’re celebrating a special occasion, impressing a date, or just treating yourself, this is the place. Hands down one of the best restaurants in Singapore. Book ahead, go hungry, and prepare to be blown away.
Thank you, LAVO — you’ve set the bar impossibly high. 7/7 stars, would return in a heartbeat! 🍝🍕🌆
Highly, highly recommend. Go now!

reviews.text:
Situated right next to the bustling Bugis Street and the famous Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple, Albert Centre is a must-explore hawker complex.

Chwee Kueh are little steamed rice cakes, light and smooth with preserved radish) on top. It makes it salty, sweet, and bursting with umami. Adding a bit of the sambal chili gives it a slow-burn kick that makes it addictive.

Kueh Pie Tee is a delightful Peranakan snack. The pastry shells are perfectly crisp, holding a juicy filling of shredded turnip. It’s a wonderful contrast of textures in a single bite, crunchy on the outside and savory-sweet on the inside.

Bak Chor Mee is Minced Meat Noodles. This bowl has a fantastic balance of vinegar and chili. The noodles are cooked al dente, and the variety of textures, from the soft minced meat to the earthy liver and savory braised mushrooms, make every bite interesting.

Hainanese Chicken Rice is my favorite. The chicken is incredibly silky and tender, paired with rice that is fragrant and perfectly oily without being greasy. The side of bok choy adds a nice crunch to the meal😍

reviews.text:
A very authentic local hawker centre right in the heart of Bugis. Plenty of food choices at affordable prices, from fishball noodles to yong tau foo and traditional desserts.
What I like most is the old-school atmosphere — not fancy, but full of character and local flavour. Some stalls have long queues, which is usually a good sign.😋
It can get crowded during peak hours, people & birds 🤭 but overall a great place to enjoy real Singapore food. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area.

Hope they put no entry to bird with nets charge.🤭

reviews.text:
One of those classic old school Singapore malls that still has a lot of personality. Peninsula Shopping Centre is especially great for sports gear, outdoor equipment, army surplus items, watches, music instruments, and hobby shops that you do not usually find in newer malls. Feels less commercialized and more like a place where enthusiasts actually shop.

The mall definitely shows its age, but that nostalgic charm is part of the experience. You can spend quite a while just wandering through the different floors discovering random hidden gems. Also conveniently connected to City Hall area, so it is easy to pop by even if you are just exploring town. A nice reminder of Singapore’s older retail scene before everything became ultra polished and identical.

Do note this is not Peninsula Plaza itself which is located across along North Bridge Road instead. This shopping mall is just beside the hotel along Funan Mall.

reviews.text:
ATLAS is without doubt one of the most impressive bars we have ever visited. From the moment you step inside, the scale and elegance of the room are breathtaking – soaring ceilings, the iconic gin tower and a glamorous Art Deco interior that immediately sets the tone for a memorable evening.

The cocktails were outstanding. We tried “Let’s Misbehave” and “Zaz Zuh Zaz” and both were beautifully balanced, creative and perfectly presented. The food was equally impressive – the prawns, scallops, prawn spaghetti and duck confit were all excellent, with generous portions and refined flavours that easily match the quality of the drinks.

​The Chinatown Heritage Centre is an absolute must-visit for anyone looking to understand the soul of Singapore. It offers a moving look at the sacrifices made by early pioneers to build the strong nation we see today.

​I’m grateful to the recommendations from Singapore Airlines and Changi Airport for highlighting this as a key cultural landmark.

​Immersive History: The history is detailed with incredible craftsmanship. You truly get a sense of "life back in the days" through the well-preserved exhibits.

​Comfortable Environment: The entire centre is clean and well-air-conditioned, making it a very comfortable place to spend a few hours exploring.
​
​It is absolutely worth the visit if you want to connect with Singapore’s heritage in a meaningful way.

The museum does an incredible job of bringing history to life, especially the stories of early Chinese immigrants in Singapore. Walking through the recreated living spaces really gave a powerful sense of what life was like back then.

The exhibits are well-designed, immersive, and easy to follow, making it both educational and engaging. I found myself slowing down to take in all the details.

The staff were friendly and helpful, and the overall experience felt very well curated.

It’s a must-visit if you’re in Chinatown and want a deeper understanding of Singapore’s cultural roots. Highly recommend!

reviews.text:
Level 33 provides a solid dining experience anchored by its breathtaking panoramic view of Marina Bay, which is the undeniable main attraction. The food is decent, with notable highlights including a rich and creamy burrata, perfectly balanced with sweet, acidic tomatoes, and an amazing mango-pineapple dessert tart. The well-crafted drinks are a plus, though some dishes, like the surprisingly lean Wagyu beef, don't fully meet expectations.

For the best visit, time your trip for late afternoon to capture the sunset, or secure an evening reservation to watch the city lights come alive. The venue is consistently popular, especially on weekends, so booking ahead is essential to enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and unforgettable vistas, which ultimately make the visit worthwhile.

reviews.text:
My recent stay at the Concorde Hotel Singapore was once again a very pleasant experience—this being my second time here, and certainly not my last.

One of the highlights of my stay was the exceptional comfort of the pillows. I had such a wonderful night’s sleep each day, which really made a difference after long days out in the city.

The hotel’s location is incredibly convenient, right in the heart of the city. Stepping out directly onto Orchard Road makes shopping, dining, and getting around so effortless.

The internet connection was also excellent—fast, reliable, and seamless throughout most of my stay and in all areas -- except in the gym.  It would be better if the same strong connection would  be made available there as well.

What truly sets this hotel apart, though, is the staff. They are consistently attentive, helpful, and thoughtful. On rainy afternoons, they kindly offered umbrellas without hesitation, and housekeeping was always prompt and accommodating whenever needed.

The overall atmosphere feels warm and welcoming—almost like a home away from home. A special shout out goes to the lovely Rita at Spices Cafe of the hotel, whose cheerful smile each morning when she is there before breakfast, made the experience even more delightful. Her friendly chats and genuine hospitality added a personal touch that I truly appreciated.

I will definitely be staying here again and would gladly recommend it to anyone looking for comfort, convenience, and excellent service in Singapore.

reviews.text:
Our experience with the wedding package at Concorde Hotel Singapore was unfortunately mixed and fell short of expectations for such an important occasion.

The main challenge was working with the assigned Wedding Coordinator, Barley. Communication was consistently slow and unresponsive, which created unnecessary stress during the planning process. Many of our requests or ideas were dismissed with references to “company policy,” rather than being approached with flexibility or a willingness to explore solutions. For example, even a simple request for pens for the signing of the marriage certificate was not handled helpfully. We also found some responses to be unprofessional in tone, including remarks such as “Normally understanding couple will understand…,” which came across as sarcastic and dismissive. This was disappointing, especially when couples are looking for reassurance and support during wedding preparations.

That said, we would like to acknowledge the positive efforts of Kenneth, Director of Catering, and Stephen, Banquet Manager. Both were professional, accommodating, and made genuine efforts to understand our ideas and concerns. The actual wedding banquet ceremony experience met our expectations and was delivered in line with what we had hoped for. Their service helped restore some confidence and showed the level of hospitality we had hoped for throughout the process.

Overall, while Kenneth and Stephen demonstrated professionalism and care, the coordination and planning experience significantly impacted our impression of the package. For couples considering this venue, we would strongly encourage clarifying expectations on communication, flexibility, and service standards from the outset.

I recently visited Coffee Addiction located at 13 Stamford Road #B2-25 Capitol Singapore and tried a few items from their menu.

I ordered the curry chicken with rice, but unfortunately the chicken was over too soft and the curry tasted rather bland. The flavor reminded me more of an Indian-style curry, but it lacked richness and depth.

I also tried the prawn noodle with shabu shabu. The prawns were fresh, which was a plus, but the broth was just average and the dish overall did not stand out.

Lastly, the siew mai was quite disappointing as it was dry and hard.

Overall, the cafe is still fine if you’re looking for a quick grab-and-go bite or just a cup of coffee. However, their food dishes could definitely use some improvement in flavor and quality.

reviews.text: I had a negative experience with the home delivery service. Both the salesman and cashier informed me that the delivery department would contact me one day in advance via phone call, followed by a WhatsApp message. However, I did not receive any call the day before the scheduled delivery. On the actual delivery day, I received a WhatsApp message from the delivery personnel, stating a delivery window of 11 AM to 2 PM. The message did not indicate that a reply was required. Approximately 20 minutes later, I received another message stating that since there was no reply, the goods would be returned to the origin. I attempted to call the driver, but the call went unanswered. When I contacted the delivery department, they repeatedly stated that this was a third-party delivery service and they were unable to intervene. They requested that I provide them with the text messages from the delivery service. After sending the messages, I did not receive any acknowledgment of receipt or updates on the progress, necessitating multiple follow-up calls from my end. I had to call the delivery department more than six times regarding this issue. The service was truly unsatisfactory.

I will definitely return for the Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup on another day.

reviews.text:
Hot Hideout is THE place I go to for my mala fix! It also so happens that I study here so the outlet at NUS makes it really easy to satisfy my cravings.

The one mala variant I always get here is the mala collagen soup. If you want dry mala, the one at Chinatown complex (iykyk), is way better. However, where this place beats every other mala place is the fact that they offer to deep fry certain ingredients like the luncheon meat, potato, lotus root etc.

Is it cheap? Most definitely not. As a big eater, and as a guy, I often spend $20 for my portion. A tip from me: if you’re dining by yourself or you and your friends are not sharing, don’t order the potato. It’s a good 300g+ and you’ll end up paying easily over $8 for a single potato - which is ridiculous imo.

Maximise your budget by getting meat, and if you want something deep fried, try the mantou buns. They pair beautifully with the peanut sauce 🤤

Another tip: come here on the weekends as there are barely any students around and you won’t need to queue.

Visited the iconic Long Bar, famous for the Singapore Sling.
The atmosphere inside is absolutely शानदार — truly one of a kind.
I really enjoyed the unique tradition of throwing peanut shells on the floor, which added to the fun and authenticity of the experience.
We ordered the Original Singapore Sling and the Raffles 1915 Gin Sling, both of which were excellent.
The bar was very busy, and unfortunately our drinks took more than 20 minutes to arrive. It seemed like the order might have been forgotten, but once the waiter noticed, he quickly took care of it.
Despite that small issue, the incredible ambiance completely made up for it.
Overall, a very satisfying experience and definitely worth visiting.

reviews.text:
YY Kafei Dian feels like stepping into old Singapore with just enough modern touches to keep things comfortable. The kaya toast here uses proper old-school buns — thick, fluffy, slightly crisp outside, and perfect with the rich kaya and butter combination. Soft eggs, traditional kopi and tea, and even the cakes bring back that nostalgic coffee shop experience that’s getting harder to find.

What I really liked was how they preserved the old-school ambiance while quietly modernising the operations. The place still feels very 80s/90s Singapore kopitiam, but with digital payments, order buzzers, and smoother service flow. It’s nostalgic without feeling outdated.

Simple food done properly. No overcomplication, no gimmicks — just solid traditional breakfast culture preserved well.

Overly rated & hyped up. A tourist trap!!!

Ordered a pork chop with rice & iced lemon tea. The meat was not too bad but hardly any sauce so rice was very dry. 🙄 The cup of iced lemon tea was the smallest cup ever! 😝😝

I went to get some chilli but didn't see the signage stating if need any cutleries or condiments to ask the serving staff. An old man in the cafe uniform who was seated at the back table raised his voice saying, Hello... I quickly apologised for my mistake but he continued raising his voice... I had to stopped him & told him, I already apologised & he doesn't have to create a scene.

I gave the service 3 🌟 cos the same person who took my order & payment was very polite. Do note this cafe only accept cash. The rest of the service staff seems like they were under pressure to quickly clear the table even though the cafe was barely full.

Honestly, not worth eating there as there are better eateries elsewhere. Even the cafe down the building is much better.

reviews.text: I highly recommend visiting Singapore City Gallery — it’s absolutely worth your time. The exhibitions are incredibly engaging and thoughtfully designed, with many interactive elements that allow visitors to actively participate rather than just observe. There are plenty of hands-on activities and immersive displays, making the whole experience both fun and informative. I was truly impressed by how much there was to see and do, and I left with a deeper appreciation for Singapore’s urban planning. Definitely a must-visit spot!

reviews.text:
Small Island Big Plans ❤️

Enjoyed the "In Our Time" mural by Lee Xin Lin
Totally awesome visual narrative because it depicts an intricate, vivid landscape of Singapore, blending historical landmarks with olden days memories and local culture references. We had fun spotting and identifying and discussing the references.

Later on further in the gallery, enjoyed the interactive board when we lookup our own postcodes. East side is best side!

Impressive also the panoramic cityscape drawing from memory by the autistic savant. Somebody help solve the mystery what is the landmark way further back. Even the on-site gallery guide wasn't sure.

We also love maps so studying the colonial maps and historical evolution of cartography made us wonder what it was like way back ancient years ago

As a history teacher, I found the Singapore City Gallery to be a masterclass in storytelling. It is deeply informative and educational, tracing the island’s evolution with incredible precision. What surprised me was how engaging and moving ALL the exhibits were, seeing the delicate balance between heritage preservation and future-ready planning. A must-visit for anyone who wants to understand the 'why' behind the skyline.

Don’t skip this! The Singapore City Gallery is a hidden gem for history buffs and urban explorers. It’s educational, engaging, and deeply moving to see how much thought goes into every square inch of this city. A highly informative experience that makes your city walks much more meaningful. A total must-visit!

reviews.text: Had a weekend lunch/brunch here. The restaurant itself is beautiful, being situated at a great location. However, I felt that for the price, the food was only so-so. The truffle fries were great, and I did enjoy the carbonara. But for the price, I feel that there shld be some authentic pancetta or guanciale used for the carbonara. The hot honey pepperoni pizza was decent. The sticky date pudding was also quite good. However I felt the shakshouka did not taste great — the bread was delicious, but the shakshouka sauce was underwhelming. While the food was decent, I do believe there are other cafes that offer better food at more reasonable prices. Moreover, the restaurant is arranged in a circle, and I found that waiters and waitresses rarely walked to the ‘back’ end of the circle where we were seated, which made ordering and getting water refills, etc take an extremely long time.

reviews.text:
The Apple Store at Marina Bay Sands is probably the place where you walk in without expectations but somehow ended up standing around like you were in a modern-day cathedral dedicated to beautiful design.

My tip? Don’t rush straight into the dome. Head downstairs first and take the escalator ride up. There’s something almost magical about the way the giant glass sphere slowly reveals itself. It’s like the building is saying, “Wait for it… wait for it…”

And then -The space opens up. The curves. The lines. The sunlight dancing through the glass. The stunning view of Marina Bay stretching into the blue skies. It’s one of those places where you suddenly forget its a store.

Watch the neat rows of Apple devices lined up like they were attending a very expensive family reunion. Macky screens shimmering. People excitedly setting up their new gadgets. Others bringing their Apple devices in for resuscitation and what not. Amid all the buzz, find a quiet corner and take a moment, there’s a surprising sense of peace here.

reviews.text:
The building looks like it’s from the future.

The customer service? Somehow still waiting to arrive.

This Apple Store is an architectural masterpiece floating on the bay, and it’s definitely worth seeing. It’s about a 15-minute walk from Raffles Place or around 5 minutes from Bayfront through Marina Bay Sands.

Now for the adventure…

I entered from the upper level where several staff in green shirts were gathered. Unfortunately, they seemed far more interested in chatting with each other than acknowledging customers. Not even eye contact.

So I went downstairs to find someone else. Same story.

Eventually, I returned to the entrance and asked two staff members for help, only to be told to ask someone inside. Ah yes… the classic Apple relay race begins.

Staff #1 → Staff #2 → Staff #3.

By the time I finally collected my purchase, I’d met half the team.

This isn’t my first visit, and honestly, every visit feels exactly the same. There are plenty of staff, yet somehow nobody actually helps you. Friendly is great, but standing around chatting while customers are hunting for assistance isn’t what I’d call customer service.

If you’re choosing between Apple Stores in Singapore, I’d personally head to Orchard instead. At least there, the relay race is shorter.

I had a very pleasant stay at Dorsett Changi Singapore. I chose this hotel because I had an early morning flight the next day, and it turned out to be an excellent choice.

The room was surprisingly spacious by Singapore standards, clean, comfortable, and well-maintained. The hotel is conveniently located right next to a shopping mall, making it easy to find food, do some shopping, or simply relax without having to travel far.

What stood out the most was the friendliness of the staff. They were warm, welcoming, and always ready to help. They even kindly helped take photos of me and my friend, which was a thoughtful gesture that made our stay even more memorable.

The check-in process was smooth and efficient, while check-out was incredibly easy - simply dropping the room key card into the designated box. The proximity to Changi Airport also made the journey stress-free and allowed me to avoid rushing for my early morning flight.

Overall, Dorsett Changi Singapore offers a great combination of comfort, convenience, and excellent service. I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable hotel near the airport.

reviews.text:
In order to get hot water to the sink and shower, I was told I need to turn on the hot water at the bathtub first, and leave it on, THEN also turn on the hot water to the sink/shower. This was the "solution" that I was expected to accept after troubleshooting the issue over the span of 3 nights. Not only is this wasteful, it was inconvenient to say the least. Just shower/bath in the bathtub? Keep in mind the cleaning supplies were conveniently secured to the shower stall, with none by the bathtub - so, I had to go in and out of the bathtub, without falling thankfully, to wash up. Showering inside the tub turned into an aerobic experience, where I had to "shower" sitting/squatting down to minimize water splashing everywhere. Furthermore, there were no follow-ups from the service staff to confirm proper issue resolution, nor did they ask about the stay at check-out (shows how much they care). Not that I crave for attention, but I thought I was paying for the "stars".

Breakfast gets the job done, TV is on the smaller side, gym is about the size of a guest room, rooftop bar has leaks/puddles around the area. Sound/noise insulation sounded pretty good, AC performed well, WiFi functional.

If you find this sort of experience acceptable for $200+ per night, then you're at the right place!

I guess they can get away with subpar accommodation for being in the city center. Probably not too hard to find better value for the money in the area.

reviews.text: 林记 mee hoon kuey is the best in Singapore. For 7 years, whenever I drop by, I'd just eat their MHK. I don't even eat other stuff from this stall. The stall is relatively quiet compared to the adjacent wanton mee. Their kuey is handmade and very thick and chewy. My mom could taste that the secret ingredient adding porridge to the flour to give it additional texture. The soup is very clean. Other top rated MHK in SG are often too salty, or they add starch to make their soup gravy-like. Not this one. The garlic flakes and prawns (if you order large) give the soup an aromatic and refreshing seafood flavour.

reviews.text:
Multiple visits and Nylon has never once missed.

No food menu, small standing-room plus some sitting space indoor and outdoor in Everton Park, roastery visible behind glass with the IMF roaster running. The whole setup makes clear that coffee is the only agenda here.

The bar runs a Mahlkönig CORE grinder into an xBloom precision brewer — consistent, technical, no shortcuts. Brewed at 1:17 across filters, which gives the cup exceptional clarity.

The bean rotation is genuinely impressive. I've had the Washed Ethiopia Banko Gotiti Heirloom — bright, lemonade-like, floral. The Washed Nicaragua Parainema — stone fruit and wild honey. And the Colombia La Laja Washed Geisha — one of the cleaner, more elegant cups I've had in Singapore. The menu rotates with the same seriousness as the brewing.

If you're new to specialty coffee, Nylon will reset your expectations. If you already know what you're looking for, you'll keep coming back. One of the best in the city, full stop.

reviews.text:
Nylon Coffee is not only recommended by the Singapore Tourism Board, but also suggested by experienced coffee professionals. What's unique is its location on the ground floor of a residential complex facing the central courtyard.

Inside, the shop possesses a lot of high-end coffee equipments such as the latest model La Marzocco Strada X 2grp with straight-in portafilters, EK43, and Ceado Titan grinders. The owner has also replaced the previously used Probat roaster (German-made renowned coffee bean roasters) with an Italian-made iMF roaster. According to the baristas, iMF can roast very light/light roasted beans more thoroughly, preventing the coffee beans from being undercooked in the center.

We ordered a Colombian pour-over and a white coffee. The Colombian coffee was refreshingly sweet and delicate, with no astringency whatsoever, which left a deep impression on us…

The shop was bustling with customers as soon as it opened in the morning. The owners were very friendly, interacting warmly with their customers. The owner, knowing we were from Taiwan, chatted with us and introduced us to other excellent local coffee shops (unfortunately, the Maxi Coffee was closed on the day).

We thought that Nylon is a highly professional, warm, and locally-flavored Singaporean coffee shop. It's definitely worth a special visit!

Worth the price! Great food, great vibes, and great service.

This homely cafe has a highly relaxing atmosphere that's great for catching up with friends or just hanging out by yourself.

The food and drinks are excellent. The Full Breakfast was delicious; a hearty meal with an elevated take on a typical english breakfast. Standout was the scrambled eggs which were perfectly silky, as well as the bacon and sausage which were very flavourful and not too oily. reviews.text:
Came to this place as part of a business team dinner on a weekday evening. Upon arrival have to say the scenery is pretty nice and the place looks quiet and peaceful, would think it's probably more apt to come here for a meal and chill on a weekend brunch after a hike or a jog around the area.
The place was really quiet throughout the night. Other than the main table of us for about 15 people, they only served another pair in another table. It just felt like we had the entire place to ourselves.
Since there were quite a lot of us, we ordered quite a bit. First we started off with a few bottles of wine then we ordered food.
The menu was supposed to be decent but there were quite a number of items which were unavailable, which was what I initially wanted to order, like the mushroom soup, seafood sambal pasta and the apple crumble, all the supposedly more appealing dishes for me in the menu.
Ordered the starters to share and individually ordered a main each. The starters were decent in general but not fantastic, however the fried mushroom dish stood out among the rest and those who tried liked it.
I got the crabmeat aglio olio and was quite disappointed with it. My friend ordered the same but it wasn't consistent. His had wetness to it and it was okay while mine was totally dry and I found it too dry for my liking. The crab also didn't look fresh there was a stench to it.
Had a try of other dishes and thought probably the best of the mains we got was the pan seared smoked duck.
Since there was only one dessert left on the menu, we ordered the chocolate lava cake and it was pretty decent.
Overall was very filling cause we over ordered, but we all felt the food had hits and misses so it's probably very average. Price wise the mains are quite reasonable it's all in the 20s range but some of the salads and starters are on the expensive end.

My husband and I recently celebrated our 12th anniversary at voco Orchard Singapore, and what truly made this stay memorable was the exceptional hospitality from the Club Lounge team.

From the moment we arrived before check-in, the team made us feel welcomed and cared for. While waiting for our room to be ready, everyone was warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly. The Club Lounge team was always observant, proactive, and welcoming. Small gestures, friendly conversations, and the effort taken to ensure guests were comfortable made a significant difference to our stay.

Thank you to the entire voco Orchard team for making our special occasion even more memorable. We look forward to returning in the future.

reviews.text: Malay Heritage Centre is housed in the former Istana Kampong Gelam, a palace which was gazetted as a National Monument of Singapore in 2015. The centre showcases the history, culture and contributions of the Malay community within the context of Singapore’s history and multi-cultural society. Officially opened by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in June 2005, the Malay Heritage Centre provides wonderful cultural exposure and learning opportunities for visitors of all ages and interests. Situated amidst the Istana Kampong Gelam, Gedung Kuning and the surrounding Kampong Gelam precinct, the Centre acts as a vital heritage institution for the Malay community in Singapore. The first Istana Kampong Gelam was a traditional timber structure built on stilts, and in honour of the Istana's original layout, visitors will commence their tour of the permanent galleries from the upper level and end their visit on the ground level. In the traditional layout, the upper level is called the panggung, which serves as the main living and sleeping quarters of the house, while the kolong at the ground level is typically used as storage, work or service areas, and even as a children's play area.

I have visited this place a few times before and decided to bring a visitor here for their first experience. The cafe was pleasantly quiet on a weekday afternoon.

Instead of ordering the Classic Bolo Bun again, we decided to try the Curry Potato Bolo Bun - marketed as the world’s first curry bolo bun - along with two iced Americanos.

Unlike the Classic Bolo Bun, which I enjoyed during my previous visit more than a year ago, the Curry Potato version fell short of expectations. Personally, I felt that curry potato fillings would pair better with a softer bun rather than a bolo bun, which perhaps explains why this concept remains relatively uncommon. As for the iced Americano, it tasted more diluted than expected.

reviews.original_text:
I have visited this place a few times before and decided to bring a visitor here for their first experience. The cafe was pleasantly quiet on a weekday afternoon.

Instead of ordering the Classic Bolo Bun again, we decided to try the Curry Potato Bolo Bun - marketed as the world’s first curry bolo bun - along with two iced Americanos.

Unlike the Classic Bolo Bun, which I enjoyed during my previous visit more than a year ago, the Curry Potato version fell short of expectations. Personally, I felt that curry potato fillings would pair better with a softer bun rather than a bolo bun, which perhaps explains why this concept remains relatively uncommon. As for the iced Americano, it tasted more diluted than expected.

The prices were also slightly on the higher side for what we ordered. It feels acceptable as an occasional indulgence, though probably not something sustainable on a regular basis.

That said, when the cafe is not crowded, the second-level seating area offers a rather relaxing atmosphere. Complimentary ice water is also available, which is a thoughtful touch.

reviews.text:
Stopped by Champion Polo Bun after hearing all the buzz and it definitely delivers if you are a fan of Hong Kong style bakery snacks done fresh.

The star of the show is obviously the polo bun. It arrives warm with that signature golden crust on top that is crisp, crumbly and lightly sweet. Bite into it and the inside is soft, fluffy and buttery, which creates that classic contrast that polo bun lovers are always chasing. The shop itself is small and casual, with a steady flow of people popping in for a quick snack or takeaway box. Seating can be a little tight during peak hours but the turnover is quick so it usually moves along. Love the three storey design and also including a very cosy third level as well.

Simple menu, well executed classics and very satisfying if you are craving a good polo bun in the Tanjong Pagar area. Definitely worth the stop.
