reviews.text: Perched on the 40th floor of the building and surrounded by others, the blocked view of Marina Bay and the Singapore Strait beyond was still quite spectacular. Outdoor dining is available but not recommended if heavy rain threatens. I imagine it would be nice in the evening but at lunch time, we preferred indoors! The large windows managed to filter any harsh sunlight and despite the bustle, it was a very relaxing meal. We had the Executive Lunch ($55 for 2 courses or $62  for 3). I orderd the cod for my main, which had that springy, slightly chewy texture i love. My companions had the pork, lamb and beef and all were not disappointed. Dessert was a satisfying sweet ending to the meal. Kudos to the attentive and efficient service staff who were constantly moving among the tables and making sure our glasses were never empty. From 12pm, the place quickly filled up and all tables were occupied so make reservations! Overall, a very pleasant experience across the menu selection, food quality, service and ambience. Will come back for dinner sometime!

reviews.text:
What an experience. I've recently had my wedding dinner held at Artemis just last week on the 3rd of May, and to put it simply it was the proverbial 5-star experience.

I am based overseas and was searching for the right venue for a wedding dinner, so I had to rely solely on online reviews and video journals to research various venues around Singapore. Right from the beginning when I first submitted my enquiry, (Events) Manager Kai and Adrian had been very proactive and informative with their responses. Kai, who was the main coordinator for this journey, deserves special praise for his patience and willingness to really listen and provide solutions for the client.

Based on online research, we found Artemis fulfilled several of our criteria with it's wonderful outdoor sky garden, chic sky bar and classy but intimate dining space. Needless to say, I still had some reservations initially before the actual food tasting and site visit. All it took was one visit during the food tasting session to quell all of my doubts.

Working with Artemis' partner florist and design company, both extremely professional and responsive, they've helped create an evening of quiet magic and perfect ambience, exactly how I've envisioned it.

1. We had our tea ceremony at their assigned room, which was comfortable and had a pleasant backdrop perfect for phototaking. We also really appreciated the beautiful tea set and cups that was provided, something I had not expected.

2. We then had our solemnization at the outdoor sky garden, luckily the unpredictable weather was co-operative and everything went perfectly. We had specifically wanted a venue where an 'ourdoor garden' style solemnization was possible, and Artemis was one of the few places that provided such an option, at level 40 no less. We also really liked the cute tiffany chairs, and partner florist Elin did a beautiful job with the floral decor.

3. The sky bar area was something that (based on everything I've researched) most wedding venues did not provide, so it is rather unique to Artemis I would say. It has spectacular views of MBS and the bay, and many of my guests would say it is a unique experience to enjoy such a stylish space to themselves for a wedding/family event.

4. The dining area, while not the largest, fit my 120 guests perfectly. The ambience was everything I had hoped for, cozy, intimate and romantic, and had enough clear room for a 'stage' area for games and dancing. The star of this space, however, had to be the breathtaking lv40 views of the city, which provided amazing backdrops for phototaking.  One of my biggest regret due to being too busy as the groom, was how I wasn't able to really take in the dusk views, which is something Artemis is known for.

5. The food was everything I had hoped, and almost all the guests I've spoken to gave 5-star reviews. Amongst our favourites were the Black Cod, Burrata starter and the mango sticky rice dessert, even the complimentary mocktail drew huge praise my wife! I will readily admit I'm not usually a fine dining kind of person, but I absolutely look forward to the next time I return to Artemis.

6. Service was good, professional and understated, all feedback was also taken onboard positively and reacted upon quickly. Supervisors and servers were both well trained and handled themselves with a lot of grace.

Lastly, I want to extend my heartfelt thanks once again to Kai, your fantastic support made this all possible and I always felt like no problem couldn't be solved throughout this journey!

places.address: 70 River Valley Rd, #01-05 Foothills Fort Canning, Singapore 179037

reviews.text:
Tiong Bahru Bakery - Fort Caninning Park

Rain or sun, you will enjoy your stay here, at the foothills of a beautiful park, surrounded by trees.

FRESHLY DELICIOUS:
The concept and atmosphere unique. They offer great selections of new and classic bakery items. As well as, great hot and iced beverage options.

CLASSICALLY NEW:
I ordered new and classic delicious bakery items.

SALMON:
If you appreciate a good and fresh salmon, may I recommend you try, Smocked Salmon & Cream Cheese Croissant - S$12.

I love a good natural salmon and they offered a great choice here. It tasted fresh and the combination of ingredients was delicious and unique. Be sure to ask them to toast it for you, as they offered it for me.

CHOCOLAT DEVOTION:
Next, if you love a good Chocolat pastry, may I suggest you try, Pain Au Chocolat - S$4.70. Just as delicious as it looks.

SMOOTH MATCHA:
Finally, if you’re a lover of all things Matcha, you should try their, ALL-NEW: Matcha Basque Cheesecake - S$9. This one I’d say was exquisite and very unique.

The texture, the flavor was nothing short of delicious. With each bite it was smooth, soft and rich. Try it out and your taste buds will be on cloud nine.

SEATING:
Good seating options too, both indoor and a large patio. I stayed here for few hours and enjoyed hearing great music through their BOSE speakers. I also enjoyed listening to loud thunder and rain outside, beating against the treetops.

OVERALL:
It’s a laid back and relaxing experience with super friendly and welcoming staff. If you need any assistance to place your order, they’re here to assist with a smile. I’m looking forward returning.

reviews.text:
An excellent dinner option with a great view. Our server Audrey was very polite and gave information about the dishes. The rest of the staff were professional, quick to attend to our needs, and very helpful when we wanted to transfer tables to the outdoor terrace for dessert. As it was our birthday month, our dessert came with a lit candle and a song from the staff. A free printed photo in a frame was our takeaway memento of excellent service.

The set for two was definitely worth it with great portion sizes. Starters were unique, very well prepared and plated. I would have been very happy to have the starters as a meal by itself. The pasta was well done. Flavors clean and the ingredients top tier. Ordered the extra Wagyu beef which came with a very healthy portion. A bit on the salty side, but the wine just paired perfectly.

Atmosphere wise was very cosy, lightly lit, but with a more modern choice of background music. A little bit on the louder side, but we had no issue speaking.

Would love to visit for their lunch set.

Our 7-Year Journey: The Good & The Bad at KKH

After 7 years and 3 miscarriages, we finally welcomed our miracle. Our journey had incredible highs and some difficult lows.

The Heroes: Expertise & Care
Dr. Liu Shu Ling (IVF): After years of "normal" results but no baby, Dr. Liu’s logical, step-by-step approach was a game-changer. She was patient with my wife’s past trauma and guided us through a successful IVF PGT-A journey. She is a true expert in recurrent miscarriage.

Dr. Angelina Chua (Delivery): Recommended by Dr. Liu, she was amazing. The C-section was smooth, the stitches were incredibly neat, and the anesthesia team managed the pain perfectly.

The Challenges: Areas for Improvement
Ward 82 Recovery: Following a C-section under Full GA, my wife needed rest. However, we felt pressured and judged by staff regarding breastfeeding and formula use. More empathy is needed for mothers in heavy post-op recovery.

Physiotherapy: We felt pushed into unnecessary treatments for "suspected" Torticollis. The approach felt forceful rather than supportive.

Jaundice Management: We were discharged despite a rising jaundice trend, only to "bounce back" to the NNJ ward a day later. KKH should recalibrate this—starting phototherapy earlier for "high-normal" cases would save exhausted parents from the stress of readmission.

Final Word,
The NNJ Ward staff were a silver lining—comforting and straightforward during a tiring time. Ultimately, we give all the credit to Dr. Liu and Dr. Angelina for finally make our dream come true and we can bringing our baby home in January.

Thank you, KKH, for the medical expertise that made us a family.

reviews.text:
I underwent an emergency cesarean section at KKH. The surgery went smoothly. Supported by the gentle comfort and professional skills of the medical staff, I safely gave birth to my baby daughter. I was admitted to the intensive care ward that night, where staff took meticulous care of my postpartum discharge. After moving to the general ward, most medical workers were warm and thoughtful. They helped feed and burp the baby, and patiently taught me breast massage methods to stimulate lactation. I soon mastered basic care skills. Most members of the medical team are professional, patient and kind, for which I am truly thankful.

Nevertheless, a female medical staff member wearing glasses behaved harshly and coldly. Her actions repeatedly upset me, leaving me filled with guilt toward my baby afterwards.

My husband tried feeding the baby for the first time. As new parents, he feared the baby might choke and nervously turned to medical staff for advice. Unexpectedly, she raised her voice and spoke in an impatient, blaming tone, repeatedly questioning whether we knew how to feed the baby and saying they would take charge instead. Without giving us a chance to explain, she took the baby straight to the nursery without a single word of explanation, and did not send the baby back for a long while. Much later, another staff member returned the baby. Seeing my husband looking flustered, I suppressed my discomfort and comforted him to relax.

Later during a routine check-up, the newborn suddenly burst into tears. Newborns cry mostly out of hunger or physical discomfort, so I planned to soothe her first before cooperating with the check. She stopped me abruptly, telling me not to hold the baby in case it developed bad habits. I could not bear to ignore the fragile crying infant. I told her I once thought the same way before becoming a mother, yet all I wanted was to calm my uneasy baby.

I comforted the baby and laid her back gently in the trolley. Yet she completely ignored my will and asked her colleague to push the baby to the nursery without my permission. The nursery was constantly filled with crying sounds. My baby had stayed there alone overnight due to my poor health condition. Though reluctant, I assumed it was only a temporary placement and the baby would come back right after the check, so I did not stop her immediately.

What disappointed me deeply was that she left right after the examination. I waited alone anxiously and felt wronged. It was not until a kind medical worker asked if I wanted my baby back that tears welled up in my eyes. I nodded quickly, and my baby finally returned to my side.

I cannot remember her name, staff ID or clear appearance, but her rude and unfeeling manner is deeply engraved in my mind. Every time I recall this experience, I blame myself bitterly for failing to protect my baby firmly and letting her be taken away. Even though she may have rich work experience, her lack of empathy and tough attitude are unacceptable.

I still trust the medical services of KKH and sincerely appreciate all the caring medical staff. Night-shift workers comforted me constantly and shared happiness when my blood pressure returned stable.

I hope I will never encounter such distressing incidents when giving birth to my second child. I wish all expectant mothers here could be treated gently. I remind myself and all mothers to follow inner feelings. Speak up bravely whenever feeling uncomfortable, and always protect ourselves and our lovely babies.

Time has passed since these incidents. My baby was born prematurely but grows healthy and well now. Whenever I gaze at her pure and cute face, those unpleasant memories haunt me and bring back my remorse. I share my personal experience with other parents staying at KKH, and I believe relevant medical workers will also see these words. I have never filed any complaint about what happened. I only hope every mother and infant can receive considerate and humane care during their hospital stay.

reviews.text:
KKH service has been extremely disappointing.

Admission staff, the level of empathy and basic courtesy has been lacking. As parents, we are already physically and emotionally exhausted caring for a sick child. We are not asking to be treated like royalty — we are simply asking to be treated with kindness, patience and respect.

Instead, when we try to explain our situation or ask for help, we are often cut off mid-sentence or spoken to in a dismissive manner. This only adds more stress and frustration to parents who are already going through a very difficult time.

Healthcare is not just about medical treatment. Compassion, empathy and communication are just as important when dealing with patients and their families.

It is deeply disappointing that when feedback is raised, the response often feels like the institution is quick to defend staff rather than acknowledge the experience of patients and their families.

Perhaps it is time for all frontline staff — especially those at admissions — to undergo proper service training or Certified Service Professional courses to improve how they interact with parents and patients. A little empathy, patience and understanding can make a huge difference.

Parents who come to the hospital are already worried and overwhelmed. The least we hope for is to be treated with respect, not dismissal.

Very disappointed with the experience.

reviews.text:
Mount Faber Peak, is a popular hilltop destination in Singapore. It is located at 109 Mount Faber Road, Singapore 099203.

Mount Faber, formerly Telok Blangah Hill, is a hill about 308 ft in height, located in the town of Bukit Merah in the Central Region of Singapore.

This placec overlooks the Telok Blangah area and the western parts of the Central Area of Singapore. The summit is accessible by Mount Faber Road or by Mount Faber Loop via Morse Road, but there are many footpaths or trails leading up the hill, like  Marang Trail, which leads from Marang Road at the Harbour Front MRT station (Exit D), and the Southern Ridges Park Connector, which connects from Telok Blangah Hill Park, Kent Ridge Park, and Henderson Waves.

It is a major tourist attraction, as it provides a panoramic view of Singapore's Downtown Core.
It's slope includes a tower that is part of the Singapore cable car system that connects to the Harbour Front and Sentosa. It is accessible from the HarbourFront MRT station.
This is the same cable car that me and family took for our joy ride and a look see from the Faber Peak, during our visit to S8ngapore in 2023.

In 1972, the government spent S$63,910 to renovate the bunkers and turn Mount Faber into a landscaped scenic spot, plus the construction of the S$2.94 million cable car system, just to link Mount Faber and Sentosa together.

The vegetation around Mount Faber is a secondary rainforest that is smaller and less dense than on Bukit Timah Hill.

Mount Faber is  separated from the adjacent slightly lower Telok Blangah Hill Park by Henderson Road.

Standing high above the sea levels, it offers panoramic views of the city skyline, the harbour, and Sentosa Island.

The site features dining options, event spaces, and the Bells of Happiness' area too.

To get to the Cable Car connection, just board from Harbour Front / Sentosa and alight directly at the Faber Peak station.
Or one can access it by car or taxi via Mount Faber Road.

Mount Faber Peak is one of Singapore’s most underrated destinations, combining stunning panoramic views, nature, dining and the iconic cable car experience all in one place

After making the climb through the lush greenery of Mount Faber Park, arriving at the peak feels like a reward in itself. The views are spectacular, stretching across the Southern Ridges, Sentosa, Keppel Harbour and the Singapore Strait. Watching the cable cars glide silently across the skyline adds a unique charm to the scenery and creates countless photo opportunities

Raffles Hospital - Singapore

It’s a very nice and modern hospital.

I came here for a minor check up. When I entered the lobby, it was nice and clean. They have a friendly, Valet-Like person in white clothes that can help you navigate through this hospital.

I took the escalator to the second floor and waited in que, to sign up to be in que. About 30 minutes later when I was ready to put my information on the iPad, a friendly and helpful nurse let me know I was in wrong Que line. 🤭🙈

She assisted me to the right room. The Que line didn’t exist here. I signed up and set down in comfortable chairs to wait to see a doctor.

Overall good service and I would come back, should I have any future medical needs.

I came to try the burgers as ‘I do love the taste of a good burger’ 🍔

I had the cheeseburger and the butter burger and each burger is $16.50. The price is not a consideration for me as I’ve eaten burgers that cost much more.  It’s whether the burger is good.

To taste then, there are good aspects of it but I am not a fan of their special sauce and unfortunately that is the dominant taste. It’s a tangy more bbq style sauce and I don’t find it that great. Pickles are nice and has a sweet taste to them. Buns are soft and nice but will of course soak up a bit of that sauce. Patties are ok, not that moist or juicy though and maybe a bit more done than I would like and there’s the taste of that sauce.

Even the butter burger had that taste which may be in the relish with it.

For me it would be better if they had maybe another sauce option for people to decide what they would want. I saw that they have an ofc cheese sauce and maybe they should offer that as an alternative or something else.

Good service from the chap at the counter. Can get a bit noisy. But those are secondary considerations. Won’t be back for these burgers based on my taste 🍔

I truly believe One Fattened Calf Burgers serves the best burgers in Singapore. From the first bite, you can immediately taste the quality and passion behind every ingredient. The beef patty was juicy, tender, and packed with flavour, while the buns were soft, buttery, and perfectly toasted. Every component came together beautifully without feeling overly heavy or greasy.

What impressed me most was how thoughtfully crafted the burgers were. The sauces enhanced the flavours instead of overpowering them, and the toppings were fresh and balanced. The fries were also crispy, addictive, and the perfect side companion. Portions were generous and incredibly satisfying.

Beyond the food, I am honestly so proud that this is a local Singapore brand. It easily stands alongside some of the best international burger joints I have tried, yet still carries its own unique identity and character. Singapore truly has amazing homegrown talent, and One Fattened Calf Burgers is proof of that.

The staff were friendly and welcoming, creating a relaxed and enjoyable dining experience. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a truly memorable burger experience in Singapore.

reviews.text:
I honestly have no idea why this place has so many 4-5 star reviews. ive seen it all over TikTok, which is why i decided to give it a try with my partner.

We dined in for two and were seated outside. The ambience was actually pretty nice, no complaints there. But the food prices were honestly outrageous considering the quality of the food served.

We ordered:
- Steak Frites $38
- Pasta $26
- Potato Gratini $16 ? cant remember lol

and wow… the steak was genuinely bad. It tasted rubbery and definitely didn’t feel fresh, most likely frozen. I asked for medium but it came closer to well done. The pasta was extremely bland with almost no flavour at all.

We also ordered the potato gratin, but it literally tasted like mushroom soup poured over sliced potatoes. Again, very bland.

Overall, I’d rate the food 1/5. Total bill came up to about $108, and honestly, we left after only a few bites because we just couldn’t finish the food (as seen in the photos).

To be fair, the owner was actually very friendly and kind. He noticed we barely touched the food and came over to ask about it. He even offered us two pastries, then later offered kunafa and tea from his other shop, but we politely declined.

Fun fact: the owner isn’t Malay like many people think. Zeekri actually owns 3 restaurants around Arab Street some of which us turkish restaurant. Maybe French cuisine just isn’t his strong point.

Service and hospitality were good, but unfortunately the food was really not it for me. Still confused how this place has over 1.2k reviews with such high ratings. Personally, I don’t see myself coming back again.

reviews.text: This is a truly grand and majestic casino right at the heart of Marina Bay, and you can feel that sense of scale and organisation the moment you step inside. It’s open 24 hours, which adds to the excitement, and entry for foreigners is free (locals pay a $100 entry fee), so it’s clearly designed to manage crowds while keeping things running smoothly. The place is massive, with an impressive range of games including roulette, sic bo, blackjack, baccarat, and a huge number of digital and physical tables and machines. There’s a noticeable emphasis on security, with cameras covering every inch of the floor, which gives the whole experience a very professional and transparent feel. The staff are excellent—polite, knowledgeable, and clearly confident in what they’re doing—and it shows in how efficiently everything operates. Free drinks are a nice touch, and members in particular are well looked after. Even if you’re just visiting to experience the atmosphere, it’s an impressive, well-run casino that feels polished without being intimidating.

Carnival Cinemas offers a good movie experience, especially if you're into Indian or regional films. The auditorium is quite spacious, which adds to the comfort during screenings. While the seating could use some upgrades for better comfort, it’s still a decent setup for the price you pay.

reviews.text:
Visited Bacha Coffee on a Sunday afternoon. I’m handicapped and requested to be seated while my partner queued. We joined the queue at around 3pm and were seated 30-40 mins later, so be prepared to wait. The space is quite tight, a little challenging moving around.

We ordered the Tasmanian salmon ($35) and gnocchetti with crab meat and clams ($32). Both were well executed. The salmon was moist and flaky, with asparagus adding a nice crunch, though the potatoes were a little dry. The gnocchetti was flavourful and comforting, with sweet crab meat and briny clams, love the sauce that ties everything together. Bread and butter were also served, which was filling.

Overall, good food, but the wait took quite some time…

places.name: Fatt Choy Eating House [發財餐馆]: Modern Singapore Comfort Food (Bugis - Haji Lane)

reviews.text:
Wandered into this spot

We did ordered their hkm once before many years ago

Glad we walked into their cosy space. Late afternoon and super humid so their aircon was a lifesaver

Met with friendly smiles from their Burmese workers. The service here is superb.

And to beat it off Mr Ko, does FOH and whips up a superb plate of Hokkien mee!!! He was explaining to us about the dish when serving it. I’m touched that a foreign worker will bother to learn so much about one of our local dish. The sambal they serve with it is good. And the dish had all the traditional ingredients; sliced three layer pork aka pork belly, sotong, prawns, chives and boy their pork lard is damn crispy. No trace of rancid oil in every bits of it at all!

Pork satay serving was substantial not ur usual flat kind, this one is almost chunky. But wish they would’ve warm up the sauce figured it would’ve elevated the mango salsa that accompanied it

Ordered their ngor hiang to finish off our second bottle of wine. Tasty and convenient bite size but would’ve preferred it with pork instead of chicken 😝😂

Will definitely be back to try more of their dishes and the stout looks very tempting

reviews.text:
Modern twist, you’re in luck. ✨ Fatt Choy Eating House at Haji Lane brings new life to traditionally delicious dishes, blending familiar local flavours with creative contemporary touches.

From the crispy Umami Shrimp Paste Chicken Karaage and rich Dry Aged Angus Beef Mapo Tofu, to the indulgent Roxy Crab Laksa topped with wild-caught crab and tobiko, every dish packs plenty of flavour. We also loved the Iberico Hainan Pork Satay, Xinjiang Lamb Skewer, Iberico Pork Ribs Bak Kut Teh, and their unique take on Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee wrapped in opeh leaf with scarlet prawn.

Save room for dessert — the Gula Melaka Tiramisu and Kaya Ice Cream with Churros are worth every calorie. 🍨

reviews.text:
Song Fa delivers truly authentic flavors with a clean, comforting taste that keeps me coming back. I’ve been here at least five times, and every visit has been consistently great, that kind of reliability is rare and impressive.

You can really taste the quality of the ingredients. The meat is tender, clearly using good cuts.

I dropped by last minute during peak dining hours yesterday, and the team still managed to get me a table quickly!!!

Service was excellent overall, with a special mention to Heah, who was friendly, knowledgeable about the menu, and made the whole experience even more pleasant. It’s genuinely nice to see a place doing so well while maintaining such high standards.

places.name: The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands

reviews.text:
Marina Bay Sands is truly an iconic landmark in Singapore and always delivers a world-class experience. The architecture is stunning, especially at night when the skyline lights up beautifully — it’s one of the most recognizable views in the city.

The SkyPark observation deck offers breathtaking panoramic views, and the infinity pool (for hotel guests) is simply unforgettable. The entire property feels luxurious, spacious, and very well maintained.

Dining at Marina Bay Sands is also a highlight. There is an impressive range of restaurants — from celebrity chef concepts to refined Asian and international cuisine. Whether you are looking for fine dining with a spectacular rooftop view or casual dining options, the quality and ambience are consistently excellent. It’s a great place for business meals, celebrations, or romantic dinners.

The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands provide a premium shopping experience with a wide selection of luxury brands, and service throughout the property is generally professional and attentive.

Overall, Marina Bay Sands is a must-visit destination in Singapore — perfect for a staycation, dining experience, or simply enjoying the incredible city skyline.

reviews.text:
Mansion7 is one of the best Chinese dining experiences I’ve had in Singapore—memorable food, exceptional value, and truly outstanding service.

Every dish was thoughtfully curated to suit our tastes, thanks to Alex, the restaurant manager, who has an incredible ability to understand his guests and recommend dishes we instantly fell in love with.

The abalone with crispy edges coated in salted egg yolk was a revelation—crispy and chewy at the same time. The prawns in mango sauce were bright, appetising, and beautifully balanced. The pork chop, served with tomato sauce and wine, was unbelievably tender. The Beijing Duck was a visual masterpiece, presented on a picturesque plate and expertly wrapped for us—no awkward DIY wrapping, just pure enjoyment. The shark’s fin soup was so flavourful! It had a generous portion of ingredients like mushrooms, fish maw and thick crab meat!

The finale was unforgettable: a durian puff with sesame crystal skin and Mao Shan Wang filling, dramatically revealed with dry ice. A true visual and sensory delight.

What truly touched me, beyond the food, was the service. Alex stayed attentive throughout the evening, respectfully giving us space during deep and meaningful conversations, and even stayed beyond closing time to ensure we were comfortable and happy.

This is white-glove service at its finest in the F&B industry. Mansion7 delivers not just a meal, but a complete, thoughtful dining experience. Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
My family had a wonderful experience dining at Yì. We were warmly greeted by the hosts and led through a beautifully curated walkway. The ambiance, environment and decor were immaculate. The staff were friendly, attentive and had a very positive attitude (I'll gladly pay service charge here). We decided to get 2 set meals and add on some ala carte dishes -- everything was a hit. The dishes were presented beautifully and we were pleasantly surprised by how every dish did not disappoint.

Big shoutout to Mei Ling for her service (we literally never saw the bottom of our tea cup). It was our first time dining at Yì and she helped to make the experience memorable from answering questions about the dishes, to the timing of service for each dish, to checking in on us throughout the meal to ensure the food is good, to organizing a little treat for celebrating my dad's birthday. We truly appreciate it and couldn't have asked for a better experience!

I'd recommend this place to others and would probably come back again ✨ (photos don't do this place justice bc we were too busy eating and enjoying ourselves that I just quickly snapped random shots to document what I ate).

reviews.text:
Little India is a vibrant and lively place, perfect for shopping and experiencing Indian culture in Singapore. Mustafa Centre is one of the biggest and most famous shopping malls here, where you can find almost everything at reasonable prices. There are many Indian restaurants and shops, and you will see a large Tamil community in this area.
There are beautiful North Indian and South Indian temples, giving the place a very spiritual and traditional feel. All kinds of Indian groceries, vegetables, spices, clothes, and accessories are easily available. While roaming around, you will find many people from India, which makes the place feel like home.
Overall, Little India is a must-visit for shopping, food, and cultural experience in Singapore.

reviews.text:
Rumifolks is one of the more chill and aesthetic café spots around the Haji Lane / Bali Lane area in Singapore, especially if you enjoy cozy café vibes, creative coffee drinks, and a relaxing place to lepak with friends or do some light work. The café was previously known as “Rumi The Poet’s Cup” before reopening nearby with a refreshed concept and brighter interior.

The atmosphere is probably the biggest attraction here — warm lighting, bookshelves, plants, artsy decorations, and a calm ambience that feels very fitting with the Haji Lane culture. Many visitors mention the friendly staff and comfortable environment for long conversations or just enjoying coffee slowly.

For drinks, their signature items like the Pandan Latte, Butterscotch Americano, Strawberry Matcha, and Salted Caramel Macchiato are among the popular choices. The coffee menu is more unique compared to many standard cafés nearby, especially if you like sweeter or flavoured specialty-style drinks.

Food-wise, the menu is more café-style comfort food rather than heavy meals. Croissant sandwiches, waffles, fries, cakes, and desserts are commonly recommended. Portion sizes are decent, though some reviewers feel the pricing is slightly on the premium café side.

Overall, Rumifolks is more about the full café experience — ambience, aesthetics, relaxing environment, and creative drinks — rather than purely hardcore specialty coffee. It’s a nice stop if you’re exploring Haji Lane or Kampong Glam and want a comfortable halal-friendly café to unwind. Suitable for couples, café hopping, casual meetings, or coffee hunting with friends.

The food and snacks are delicious, and every dish I ordered exceeded my expectations. The coffee is excellent too—great quality and very reasonably priced. Service was warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly, which made the experience even better.

The music is thoughtfully selected—not too loud, just enough to create a relaxing ambience that's perfect for conversations, reading, or simply unwinding. It's easy to see why this place is so popular.

What makes Rumifolks truly special is its genuine commitment to arts, poetry, culture, and the creative community. It's inspiring to see a café that not only serves great food and coffee but also creates opportunities for cultural exchange, artistic expression, and live performances. Spaces like this are becoming increasingly rare, and I really admire their vision of bringing people together through creativity and meaningful experiences.

Whether you're an artist, performer, poet, musician, or simply someone looking for a peaceful place to relax and be inspired, Rumifolks is a place worth visiting.

I highly recommend Rumifolks to anyone looking for great food, excellent coffee, wonderful service, and a unique space where culture, arts, and community come together. I'll definitely be coming back whenever I'm in the area!

reviews.text: My wife was warded here after a brain op. I lodged together with her for about 5 days. Unlike the lackluster reviews of others here, we experienced the best of everything, from customer service, admin, ward nurses, porters, housekeeping, and food services. Everything was top notch service. Smiles all around, sometimes we forget this is a hospital, felt like a 6-star hotel service.  Room and facilities work as advertised and intended. Honestly the human factor just covers any hardware flaws you might encounter. I left the best part to the last. The food menu, OMG., opulence, exquisite, heavenly, MasterChef quality. I know everyone's only talking about the lobster laksa. Yes that's good too. But I must specifically point out the beef rendang. I have always like beef rendang but Mt E's rendition is the best by far. I have never tasted a beef rendang more tender and juicy than theirs. My saddest fleeting thought was that I will never get to eat this again unless I am hospitalized. Touch wood. As they say, there are some things worth dying for.... Mt E's beef rendang comes really close.

reviews.text:
I recently stayed at Mount Elizabeth Novena Hospital for 5 days last week in Ward 11, and I would like to express my sincere appreciation to the nursing team there.

All of the nurses were incredibly attentive, professional, and caring throughout my stay. Recovering from surgery was not easy, and although I did not have much appetite after the operation, I was pleasantly surprised by the wide variety of food choices available from light and simple meals to dishes that felt like hotel quality cuisine.

Unfortunately, I cannot remember every nurse’s name, but the kindness and compassion they showed left a very deep impression on me. However, there is one nurse I especially want to mention and thank — Gaite Michelle Anglea. Her attentiveness, warmth, and genuine care made me feel safe and reassured during a difficult time as a patient.

Thank you to Ward 11 and the entire team for the excellent care and support.

reviews.text:
I booked a Pilates class through ClassPass and made every effort to arrive on time. Unfortunately, due to traffic and the building entrance being under maintenance, I had difficulty locating the correct entrance and had to find the back entrance to access the studio. As a result, I arrived approximately two minutes late.

While I was already frustrated about being denied entry despite arriving only two minutes late, what was far more unacceptable was the attitude and conduct of your front desk staff!

After I explained the situation and asked whether I would still be charged a no-show fee despite already arriving at the studio, the female staff member responded coldly and without any empathy: “Yes, you will be charged no-show fees.”

Throughout the interaction, her tone was dismissive, impatient, and unnecessarily rude. There was absolutely no attempt to communicate professionally or show even basic customer courtesy. I understand policies may exist, but there is a major difference between enforcing a policy and treating customers with complete disregard.

I would like this complaint regarding the staff member’s conduct to be taken seriously. Unfortunately, I did not get her name, but she was the female front desk staff assisting customers on May 9 between approximately 1:50–1:55 PM.

Overall, this was an extremely unpleasant customer experience:

I lost both my ClassPass credits and transportation costs despite physically arriving at the studio.
I was denied entry over a two-minute delay caused partly by the building maintenance situation.
Most importantly, I was treated with a shocking lack of professionalism and empathy by your staff.
I would appreciate hearing about the outcome or follow-up actions taken regarding this complaint, as I believe this level of customer service is unacceptable and should be properly addressed.

reviews.text:
Dining Experience @ Sona's Grill.
.
The Dahi Puri (SGD $11) has a beautiful satisfying crunchy tender creamy texture, bursting with bright milky savoury starchy sweet sour tangy zesty spice herbal flavour.
.
The Tandoori Kukurmutta Tikka (SGD $17) or Tandoori Mushroom Tikka are bouncy and springy in texture, juicy and bursting with vegetal earthy savoury sweet spice flavour.
.
The Murgh Malai Tikka (SGD $19) or Chicken Malai Tikka is tender and juicy and moist, bright with smoky meaty savoury milky sweet nutty flavour.
.
The Anda Bhurji (SGD $16) or Egg Bhurji is fluffy crunchy tender in texture, with enticing eggy savoury salty vegetal earthy sweet herbal spice flavour.
.
The Murgh Makhani (SGD $22) or Butter Chicken has a creamy thick smooth curry, with tender juicy bouncy chicken meat, carrying smoky meaty savoury milky sweet spice flavour.
.
The Baingan Ka Bharta (SGD $17) or Mashed Eggplant Curry has a thick gloopy chunky texture, with mellow vegetal earthy salty sweet spice flavour.
.
The Naan Garlic (SGD $6 Per Piece) has a fluffy chewy texture, with nice bready savoury spice flavour.
.
The Paratha Pudina (SGD $6 Per Piece) has a crisp firm crunchy texture, with bright bready minty herbal savoury flavour.
.
The Paratha Aloo (SGD $10) has a crisp firm soft texture, with mellow bready starchy savoury salty spice flavour.

reviews.text:
Got the Butter Chicken, garlic naan, mango lassi. I think it was around 39$ after all charges.

Taste wise, it was amazing. I could taste the grill in the chicken gravy, very garlicky, the naan had fresh garlic over it and it was very good, chicken was extremely tender and flavourful.

However! The prices are portions are insane! It's tiny! For $22 for a small bowl, maybe 7 pieces of chicken. 1 naan for 4-6$. I thought that I couldn't finish it when I saw the price, thought it was to share with multiple people, but consider me "relieved" when I saw it come out. The saving grace is the taste, because the price lowered my enjoyment.

reviews.text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Excellent learning experience with strong industry relevance

SMU Academy provides a well-structured and professionally run learning environment. From onboarding to programme briefings, everything has been smooth, organised, and clearly designed for working professionals.

What impressed me most is how industry-relevant the content is. The modules are practical, up-to-date, and focused on real application instead of just theory. The facilitators are experienced practitioners who encourage discussion, critical thinking, and sharing of perspectives — making each session engaging and meaningful.

Administrative support has been responsive, and the networking opportunities are a big bonus, bringing together participants from different industries to exchange ideas.

Overall, SMU Academy delivers a high-quality learning experience that truly adds value for mid-career professionals and business leaders looking to upskill and stay ahead. Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
Singapore Management University (SMU) is a top-notch institution that's making waves in Asia! Established in 2000, it's a public university located in the heart of Singapore, offering a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs.

*Key Highlights:*

- *Rankings*: SMU is ranked #3 in Singapore and #1016 globally, with top rankings in fields like Investment Banking, Real Estate, and Accounting.
- *Research*: The university is known for its high-impact research, with faculty members collaborating with international researchers and partners in the business community.
- *Campus*: SMU's city campus is modern and well-equipped, providing students with a vibrant learning environment.
- *Programs*: SMU offers bachelors, masters, and PhD programs in various fields, including Business, Economics, Law, and Computing.¹ ²
*Student Life:*
- *Student Body*: Over 12,000 students from diverse backgrounds.
- *Facilities*: State-of-the-art library, sports facilities, and administrative services.
*Admissions:*
- *Tuition Fees*: SGD 11,500 for local students and SGD 24,600 for international students.
- *Scholarships*: Available for deserving students.
Overall, SMU is a great choice for students looking for a world-class education in a vibrant city-state. Would you like more info on SMU's programs or admissions?

reviews.text:
Bai Nian Yong Tau Foo at Albert Food Centre is one of my go-to comfort food stalls. I tried both the dry kuay and the soup bee hoon — the dry version comes with rice noodles in a tasty sauce, while the soup has a light, clean broth that feels so comforting. The Yong Tau Foo pieces taste fresh and handmade, especially the prawn paste and stuffed bitter gourd.

On top of that, their crispy chicken wings were juicy and well-marinated, and the golden wantons had the perfect crunch. Simple, hearty, and satisfying meal

The place feels really comfortable and relaxing, and the coffee smells amazing and tastes very pure. The barista was also very friendly. After talking to them, I found out that their coffee beans are specially imported from Japan, and they have different flavor options to choose from.

Of course! I also tried their matcha. Since matcha is everywhere..but their matcha honestly surprised me because it tasted very different from the ones I’ve had before. It was smooth, lightly sweet, and very easy to drink, with no bitter or rough feeling at all.

Really recommend this café if you’re around!

reviews.text:
Every dish we ordered was tasty and full of flavour. I have to commend the warm hospitality shown by everyone there. It genuinely felt more like visiting a family friend’s home than dining at a restaurant.

The Kizhi Parotta was excellent, and the signature Kanthari Chicken Paal Curry was outstanding. The Nool Parotta was perfectly crispy, while the Kizhi Parotta was beautifully soaked in the curry, making every bite incredibly satisfying.

One thing I appreciated was that they informed us upfront, even before we ordered, that the food would take about 25 minutes to arrive. They delivered it right on time, which set expectations well and showed great professionalism.

The $1 cutting chai is absolutely worth trying. Served in authentic glass cups, it adds a nice touch to the overall vibe. It’s slightly on the sweeter side, but still very enjoyable.

Overall, this is an affordable restaurant serving high-quality food with genuinely warm and welcoming hospitality. A lovely family-run place that I can definitely see myself visiting often.

reviews.text:
Finally visited this spot I’ve had saved for ages, hidden inside Golden Mile Tower.

The place is small and cozy, and it also doubles as a vintage clothing and accessories shop, which makes it feel a little different from usual cafe. There are a few seats along the side where we can sit down and enjoy matcha.

I came on a weekday afternoon, but it was still pretty crowded. The wait was totally worth it though. I ordered the Banana Pudding Matcha, and it was super thick and creamy, basically like having dessert in a cup. It’s topped with cream, banana slices, lotus biscoff, and bits of cake, which made every sip extra indulgent and satisfying. No wonder this drink sells out so quickly!! I felt really lucky to catch it in time hehehehe

Such a cool little hidden gem overall. Definitely coming back to try their Strawberries Matcha next time!!!

This is my go-to spot for an authentic Izakaya experience. I visit this place regularly.

Food:
SKEWERS (YAKITORI): The grilled skewers are exceptional. Each piece is perfectly seasoned. It is easily the highlight of the menu.

NOMIHODAI: The free-flow drink option is very well-priced and offers a great selection.

reviews.text:
I had a disappointing experience with this clinic regarding their health screening service. If the grade can be lower than zero star, I definitely agreed.

While my own report was ready earlier, my wife has been waiting for more than 2 weeks and still has not received her health screening report. We have tried following up multiple times via WhatsApp, but the responses have been slow, unclear, or sometimes not received at all. It feels like our messages are just being ignored.

We have never experienced such a long delay with other clinics before. What is more frustrating is the lack of proper communication and transparency. Even when looking at Google reviews, the clinic often replies asking patients to contact them directly, but based on our experience, this does not seem to lead to any real follow-up or resolution.

In addition, the overall process feels very manual and outdated. There seems to be a lack of proper system or automation to track and update patients on their report status, which may be contributing to the delays and poor communication.

Health reports are important, and patients should not have to keep chasing for updates. We hope the clinic can improve their turnaround time, communication, and consider adopting better systems to manage patient reports more efficiently.

reviews.text:
Marina Bay in Singapore is a stunning example of modern urban planning and architectural brilliance. Located at the heart of Singapore's downtown, it is a vibrant hub that perfectly encapsulates the city-state's blend of innovation, luxury, and cultural diversity.

One of the most iconic features of Marina Bay is the Marina Bay Sands, a massive integrated resort that dominates the skyline with its three towering structures connected by a unique rooftop SkyPark. The SkyPark offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city, especially at sunset when the skyline is bathed in a golden glow. The infinity pool at the top is also a must-visit, offering a surreal experience of swimming with the city at your feet.

The area around Marina Bay is equally impressive. The Marina Bay Promenade is a beautifully designed waterfront walk that provides scenic views of the bay and is a perfect spot for an evening stroll. The Merlion Park, featuring Singapore's iconic Merlion statue, is another highlight, drawing tourists and locals alike for photo opportunities and to enjoy the atmosphere.

For those interested in culture and the arts, the ArtScience Museum, with its lotus-inspired design, offers a range of exhibitions that blend art, science, and technology. The Marina Bay Sands itself houses numerous high-end shops, restaurants, and a world-class casino, catering to every kind of luxury experience.

The Gardens by the Bay, located just a short walk away, is a futuristic garden space with towering Supertree structures that light up beautifully at night. The Cloud Forest and Flower Dome within the gardens are also spectacular, offering a unique blend of nature and technology.

Transportation in and around Marina Bay is seamless, with excellent connectivity via the MRT and buses. The area is also pedestrian-friendly, making it easy to explore on foot.

Overall, Marina Bay is a must-visit destination in Singapore, offering a mix of luxury, culture, and breathtaking views that make it one of the most memorable places in the city. Whether you're there for shopping, dining, sightseeing, or just soaking in the vibrant atmosphere, Marina Bay has something for everyone.

reviews.text:
At Singapore General Hospital. The area appears to be well-signed with information in multiple languages. The presence of a registration counter suggests a structured process for patients. Inside, there are waiting areas and indications for different types of scans like CT and MRI. However, these are just observations based on the visuals. Currently, after a week where my parents bring my brother here for his additional upcoming appointments for his return to visit to the Diagnostic Radiology department at Block 2 of Singapore General Hospital, Gastroenterology & Hepatology, with Dr. Steven Mesenas. Also, he has additional upcoming appointments that after a five-day period, which is on Monday, May 19, 2025, at SGH. The CT Enterography procedure, such as fasting for 4 hours beforehand and following a low-residue diet the day before, my brother indicated, "Signs of Crohn's disease and iron deficiency anemia." This information, along with the upcoming CT Enterography, suggests he is undergoing tests and treatment for these conditions. The test was performed on November 5, 2024. The levels > 100-200 may indicate the presence of intestinal inflammation. The managing physician should correlate the patient's clinical status with this test result and determine if further laboratory, radiological, and endoscopic tests are needed. The test was performed using Quantum Blue Calprotectin Extended Buhlmann.

Review posted on Thu, 15/05/2025
4 days ago

__

Edited: Mon, 19/05/2025

Currently, since earlier over the past five days, when my parents have brought my brother here once again undergo for additional checkup, it seems my brother Raymond has had additional appointments and a CT Enterography procedure at SGH, specifically within the Gastroenterology & Hepatology department and the Diagnostic Radiology, with Dr. Steven Mesenas, Clinic M, department located in BLK 3 L1 (Yellow Zone). This day he be able to self-collecting his consultation and services medications there. In addition, the doctor has prescribed him for Ferrous Gluconate Compound Cap (180 QTY), which is used in the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia. OMEprazole 20mg Cap (91 QTY) is used to treat certain conditions where there is too much acid in the stomach after done seeing his latest Gastroenterology & Hepatology test result.

The final tax invoice indicates that the CT Enterography procedure costs $1,974.75, which was covered by the MINDEF CMPB (PRE-ENLISTEE) scheme.

reviews.text: Next January would be a year I first stepped into SGH on our 15 years of stay in Singapore, all this while we have heard about this biggest hospital in Singapore with worldwide fame, okay the Urology department's public toilet needs a little renovation. Jokes apart, our destination was the Urology department, I was the patient who is a fear monger to the power of infinity, joke was least on my mind! Then I met my prescribed doctor, in fact his assistant or junior, whatever. I was in dilemma not knowing the system, the name says doctor is male, I am talking to a female. I saw one gentleman continuously moving to & fro from one room to the adjoining, I asked if he is Dr.Henry Ho, he finally was kind enough to look at the screen and speak to me. He didn't rebuke me for being suspicious about his doctor title, but his broad smile & comforting words eased me in such a manner that those few words spoken & his gestures would forever remain etched in my heart & memory! I met him one more time thereafter, the scheduled third meet did not happen, he redirected me to his junior colleague! May be he was busy with serious patients given I wasn’t diagnosed with anything serious! But I firmly believe he is not only excellent in his job but knows the way to a patient's heart, how to ease scared patients in discomfort! Definitely a medical college may not teach this in details, it comes from within! I believe he has as beautiful a heart as seen through a patient’s eyes in that brief encounter, besides the varied degrees & chairs he holds. I wholehearted recommend Dr.Henry Ho for your related issues! I wish him health, happiness, success throughout his life! By the way, SGH houses excellent food arenas at subsidised prices, you may try!

reviews.text:
This restaurant is best known for its briyani, the true signature dish of the house. The rice was soft, light, and fragrant, while the meat, well-marinated, delivered rich and balanced flavors. The accompanying sauce was also well executed, although it felt slightly too salty for my taste.

The service stands out for its speed and the friendliness of the staff, making the overall welcome pleasant. However, the cleanliness of the dining area in the street food center leaves room for improvement, and additional staff dedicated to cleaning would probably be beneficial.

In the end, despite the quality of the briyani, the overall experience did not fully live up to expectations.

reviews.text:
Solid boutique hotel with a clean, modern, well-designed interior. Definitely on the smaller side (at least for their lower priced rooms). I was solo traveling and had enough space. But if I had been traveling with my partner, their double room would not have been large enough for multiple suitcases without having to put them right in the middle of the floor/tripping hazard.

But the room was very clean, aesthetically pleasing, comfortable bed, and nice shower with good pressure. A good place to come back, relax, and sleep after a day exploring the city. The hotel is right across from a bar, so there is some of that noise (I advise earplugs if you’re a light sleeper) or ask to stay in the interior side of the hotel. The higher rooms are their more expensive rooms, too, which could potentially cut down on the noise.

The location is AMAZING! 10/10 on location. Right in the heart of Chinatown with quick walks to two great hawker stall centers: Chinatown Complex and Maxwell Center, with both the Chinatown MRT and Maxwell MRT very close to walk to (use Singapore’s MRT system – it’s great: inexpensive, convenient, takes you all over the city).

Would give this hotel a 4.5 if I could. It is reasonably priced compared to a lot of other options in Singapore and feels newer and very well-maintained.

You can tell that a lot of thought has been put into keeping everything neat and aesthetically pleasing. The overall atmosphere is relaxing and perfect if you’re looking for a simple yet comfortable place to stay.

The only minor downside is that the toilet is quite small, which might feel a bit tight for some guests. Aside from that, everything else was great. Overall, I’d still highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a well-kept boutique hotel with a nice, modern vibe.

Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
I visited a loved one at Outram Community Hospital and was very impressed by the overall environment and care provided. The hospital is clean, modern, and thoughtfully designed, creating a calm and welcoming space for both patients and visitors. Carpark is also well organized with sufficient parking lots.

What stood out most was the professionalism and warmth of the staff — from nurses to therapists to admin personnel. Everyone was patient, respectful, and genuinely caring in how they interacted with the patients. It gave me a lot of reassurance seeing my loved one so well looked after.

Facilities were well-maintained given its newly opened as well and visiting hours were managed smoothly. There are also great amenities - Koufu food court, POSB ATM, AXS machine, starbucks, Koi, and a pharmacy. Pretty decent for a community hospital.

A great example of community healthcare done right unlike some others i have visited. Thank you to the team at Outram Community Hospital for your dedication and compassion.

Bugis Market @ Bugis Street is a vibrant and bustling spot packed with a huge selection of shops.
It’s very popular with both tourists and locals.
You’ll find fruit stalls, souvenirs, street food, mobile phone services, chocolates, sweets, T-shirts, trinkets, beauty services, bags, pharmacy and plenty more.
It’s always busy and crowded, but over the years, the place feels cleaner and less stuffy, with better air circulation now.
Worth a visit to browse around and soak in the lively atmosphere.

reviews.text:
Pocket Rocket is a splendid reminder that true hospitality has very little to do with extravagance and everything to do with the people behind the bar.

The venue embraces its dive bar identity with confidence—unpretentious, full of character, and effortlessly welcoming. It strikes a rare balance between relaxed charm and genuine warmth, making it somewhere you find yourself returning to without hesitation.

A particular mention must go to Ganesh, whose hospitality is nothing short of exemplary. Attentive without ever being intrusive, personable without feeling rehearsed, he has a remarkable ability to make every guest feel genuinely welcome. It is, quite simply, hospitality at its finest.

If you’re after polished cocktails, authentic conversation and an atmosphere that values substance over spectacle, Pocket Rocket is well worth a visit. A proper hidden gem. Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
One of my favorite neighborhood spots in Singapore.

Pocket Rocket is about as casual as it gets—in the best possible way.  Nestled among the shophouses on Keong Saik Road, it’s the kind of place that’s perfect for bringing out-of-town guests for a taste of local flavor, or winding down after a long day in the CBD.

The team genuinely cares about the people who walk through the door, remembers your name, plays great music (with the occasional nostalgic 2000s emo/punk throwback 🎸), and creates the kind of atmosphere where it’s just as comfortable to come with friends as it is to rock up solo and strike up a conversation.

Don’t come expecting luxury or pristine amenities — that’s not the point.  Come for a cold beer, good company, and a team that works hard to make everyone feel welcome.

A rare gem.

places.name: Coffee Hive (Altez) | Wide Range of Local Delights | Traditional Local Coffee

reviews.text:
Stopped by here for a late lunch. I had the Kopi O Kosong and Mee Siam. The place was relatively quiet when I went, which was nice for a relaxed meal. The staff was genuinely friendly, and the lady boss even came by to ask how the food was – you can really tell they're putting in the effort to get things right as a new shop. The Kopi O Kosong was robust and flavourful, exactly how a good Kopi O Kosong should be, and the Mee Siam had that perfect balance of tartness and sweetness without being too heavy.

If I had to nitpick, a few minor things could be polished, which is expected for any new place, but the attention to detail and their food recommendations really shone through. It's clear they care about what they serve. If you're in the area (Icon Village / Altez), I'd say give them a shot – new spots need support, and the team here is genuinely trying their best. I'll definitely be back soon. Worth a visit for sure!

reviews.text:
Had such a lovely dining experience here! Every dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented.

The Beef Tartare was one of my favourites, hand-chopped and perfectly seasoned with pickled shallots and mustard, paired with crisp toasted brioche for the perfect bite. The K.P.T Cocktail was a fun starter, crispy tart shells filled with creamy prawn cocktail salad, light yet flavourful.

For mains, the Hua Diao Brine Poulet really surprised me! The poached chicken was unbelievably tender and juicy, complemented by a smooth carrot purée that tied everything together. The Flame-Grilled Scallops were plump and smoky, each bite bursting with natural sweetness.

Desserts were a perfect ending, the Burnt Cheesecake with a hint of dark rum was rich and indulgent, while the Bread Pudding felt warm, homey, and comforting.

Their cocktails were another highlight! I especially loved Amy, a sweet and refreshing mix that instantly won me over. Grace was just as delightful, balanced and elegant.

Overall, an amazing spot for great food, drinks, and a cozy, refined atmosphere. Would definitely come back to try more!

reviews.text: Chinatown MRT station is recognized as one of the busiest stations in Singapore and is a significant point of interest for tourists. It offers diverse dining options, from local eateries to vibrant street vendors. Visitors can easily explore nearby attractions such as Little India, Chinatown Complex, Chinatown Point, the Chinatown Street Market, and the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, all within a short distance. Positioned at the intersection of Eu Tong Sen Street, New Bridge Road, and Upper Cross Street, this station provides essential rail connections to the bustling Chinatown district, where the harmonious blend of modern architecture and distinct Chinese cultural elements creates a unique urban landscape.

Chinatown Singapore.
This is a must visit location in Singapore especially during the Chinese New Year festival.
There are many stores popped up along the streets during the this period and in the evening the whole Chinatown will be so busy with the locals doing the usual New Year shopping.
It's so colorful and foods are on every street.
The wet market at basement of Chinatown complex is one of the busiest market in Singapore.
Many Dim Sum restaurant here in chinatown.
The tooth relic temple in Chinatown is the new landmark and you will never miss the temple when you are in Chinatown.

reviews.text:
If you wanted to visit Gardens by the Bay, Marina Bay Sands, ArtScience Museum and the Helix Bridge, this is NOT the MRT station to go. Instead, Bayfront MRT Station (CE1/DT16) should be the designated station. Don't worry, luckily this is an interchange station and Bayfront Station is just 1 station away. You just need to head to the Circle Line (CCL), going towards CE1 direction.

This is a huge interchange station, from one line to another takes a few minutes walk. I like that the station is spacious, clean and less crowded, but the elevator speed is really fast, you really need to pay attention when getting onto the elevator.

reviews.text:
Chuan Seng Kway Chap is one of those always long-queue stalls at Albert Centre Food Centre, Bugis.

Skip the standard one pax platter, go straight for a pick & mix instead.

Paid S$15.70 for a decent spread of large fatty intestines/大肠头, small powder intestines粉肠, pig stomach/猪肚, fish cake, & egg, plus a bowl of kway/flat noodles.

The offal is the highligh - clean, no gamey smell, nice chewy bite but still tender, & well soaked in that savoury, slightly herbal braised gravy.

The kway is silky smooth & breaks apart easily with a spoon, super easy to eat (my kind of texture).

Gravy looks dark but flavour is well balanced - not too salty, not too bland.

Only thing is the chili not really my type.

Despite seeing quite a few reviews mentioning a “bossy” or “rude” auntie, my experience here was actually very pleasant.

When I went back to get extra noodles, auntie even checked if I wanted to top up my chilli, which I thought was a really nice touch.

The kway chap itself was excellent — the noodles were silky, comforting, and served piping hot. Portions were very generous (this was a portion for 5 pax), and the intestines were impressively clean with no unpleasant smell at all.

Overall, a satisfying and hearty meal. Would definitely come back again!

reviews.text:
Found this newly opened cafe tucked in an alley near the mosque.

The decor of the place is very interesting, reminding me of a Junk journal. Alongside anime posters, there are concert tickets, art prints, cutouts of packaging and stickers adorning the walls, and it is gives a lot of personality as you can tell all of the posters are from a personal collection curated over years. It was fun looking around the walls and pointing out franchises we recognise.

We had the apple/carrot juice and burata cheese pizza. The juice was fresh and not too sweet, and the 10inch size pizza is good to share for 2 people. Despite not having any sauce added, the pizza was really tasty as the pizza dough was really good on its own! Do note you do need to wait a bit for the pizza though.

reviews.text:
5 stars for Koffee Kollective at Tanjong Pagar! Honestly one of the best little coffee finds in Singapore, a charming, cozy coffee house tucked away in the corner at #02-51, Tanjong Pagar Food Market.

What I love most is that it feels so personal and heartfelt. The founders are lovely, and you can really tell they put a lot of care into what they do. It is the kind of small local business that makes you want to come back, not just for the drinks, but also for the warm service and good vibes.

Their drink options are great too. Whether you want a classic kopi, an espresso-based coffee, an iced latte, or something more fun and creative, there is something for everyone. They also have matcha options, hojicha, Milo-style drinks, and special flavours like strawberry matcha, dirty matcha, honey oat latte, and even more indulgent choices like banana pudding matcha. Perfect for coffee lovers, matcha fans, or anyone who just wants a nice drink to brighten the day.

They also have another outlet in Bedok, so do check them out there too.

Please come support Koffee Kollective if you are around Tanjong Pagar! It is a hidden gem, run by lovely people, with solid drinks and lots of heart. Highly recommended.
reviews.original_text:
5 stars for Koffee Kollective at Tanjong Pagar! Honestly one of the best little coffee finds in Singapore, a charming, cozy coffee house tucked away in the corner at #02-51, Tanjong Pagar Food Market.

What I love most is that it feels so personal and heartfelt. The founders are lovely, and you can really tell they put a lot of care into what they do. It is the kind of small local business that makes you want to come back, not just for the drinks, but also for the warm service and good vibes.

Their drink options are great too. Whether you want a classic kopi, an espresso-based coffee, an iced latte, or something more fun and creative, there is something for everyone. They also have matcha options, hojicha, Milo-style drinks, and special flavours like strawberry matcha, dirty matcha, honey oat latte, and even more indulgent choices like banana pudding matcha. Perfect for coffee lovers, matcha fans, or anyone who just wants a nice drink to brighten the day.

They also have another outlet in Bedok, so do check them out there too.

Please come support Koffee Kollective if you are around Tanjong Pagar! It is a hidden gem, run by lovely people, with solid drinks and lots of heart. Highly recommended.

reviews.text:
personally i feel that their quality, quantity and price point is really hard to beat compared to the myriad of matcha brands around the area. plus you get to use your cdc voucher!!

/niko neko matcha/

/niko neko houjicha/
• akane - dark roast with soy milk chocolate taste profile and intense roastiness.

/regular or large size/
• specialty coffee - hot is 8oz, iced is 12oz
• matcha & houjicha - regular is 12oz, large is 16oz
*info gathered from their website

they're located around a corner area, facing a traffic light below~

reviews.text:
Fun experience shopping for a Chinese style dress. I came across this shop while exploring the Chinatown. They have Chinese style tops, dresses, etc that are in cotton (not as common as shiny polyester ones). They were sold out of the styles that I wanted but were able to suggest alternatives based on my preferences. I got this navy blue short dress, which my boyfriend really liked. When he saw me in it, his face literally lit up! The shop doesnot have a fitting room but they will choose that size that fits. I usually wear US 2 but was suggested that a size L would fit, which actually fit me pretty snugly😂
The dress has a bit of stretch and is comfortable and cool to wear. The shop closes around 6 PM, so make sure that you get there so that you’ll have enough time to choose (I arrived as they were closing the shop so I felt bad that I was being indecisive. They were really nice and helpful despite that).

reviews.text:
A Unique co-sharing concept where Dose Coffee is sharing the space with Bibi: Modern Bibimbap. I went in the morning for my caffeine fix - clean, pleasant, and cozy interior and rather quiet in the morning which was a plus point in CBD. However it's packed during lunch, so do take note!

Aesthetics aside, Dose serves awesome coffee! Especially if you prefer a stronger dose of caffeine, I highly recommend the "Magic". Not all coffee places serve this option so I'm really happy that they have it here.

And as I was there for a while, the next drink I had was the Iced Matcha Latte, smooth and velvety with a beautifully balanced taste profile. Thumbs up to the barista Annie for all the wonderful drinks!

I bought the prepaid card as well for my future drinks; already planning to try the Aeroccano next, seems interesting!

And I will remember to take photos of my drinks next time :)

reviews.text:
Our stay at Shangri-La Singapore was overall a lovely experience, especially as a family traveling with kids. The hotel is very well set up for families, and it truly shows in the thoughtful facilities and attentive service from the staff throughout our stay.

One of the highlights was definitely the Asian breakfast buffet. The selection is generous and well-executed, with plenty of local flavors to enjoy. However, if you’re staying longer than three days, you might notice that the menu doesn’t vary much, which can make it feel a bit repetitive over time.

That said, the other restaurants within the hotel are excellent and maintain a high standard, offering good alternatives when you want a change from the buffet.

For families, Buds by Shangri-La is a fantastic play area—our kids absolutely loved it. Just keep in mind that access isn’t included in all room bookings, and you’ll need to reserve sessions in advance during your stay.

Another great feature is Splash Zone Shangri-La, which adds a lot of fun for children. However, being outdoors, it can be affected by the tropical weather, and I do wish it opened a bit earlier than 9 AM to make the most of the day.

Overall, despite a few minor points, our stay was very enjoyable. The staff were warm, helpful, and consistently supportive, which made the experience even more memorable.

reviews.text:
We came here for the Western dishes, and each main course came with access to an all-you-can-eat salad bar.

Our main dishes were delicious, but what really impressed us was the extensive salad bar. There was a wide variety of side dishes to choose from, along with a fun DIY dessert station. We also appreciated the condiment and sauce stations, which allowed us to customize our meals with different flavours.

One thing that puzzled us was the nasi lemak at the salad bar. It came with sambal chili, but it felt incomplete without essentials like ikan bilis. As a result, the rice didn’t pair particularly well with the other items available at the salad bar.

Overall, it was a very satisfying lunch with plenty of variety and good value. The only limitation was the 90-minute dining time, but it was still more than enough for us to enjoy the meal at a comfortable pace.

reviews.text:
TANGS at Tang Plaza is one of the oldest surviving and longest running  department stores in Singapore, and the main Orchard Road store feels like it has been around forever. I’ve been seeing it since I was little, so there’s definitely a sense of nostalgia attached to it.

One of my favourite restaurants, Sinpopo, is located inside the department store. However, the fourth floor, which used to house places like Dancing Fish and Justin’s Gastro Café-Bar, has since been repurposed. The basement has now been transformed into a large food hall featuring the Hawker Street food court and various other restaurants and eateries.

I really hope TANGS continues to thrive, as it remains such an iconic part of Orchard Road. Since they own the freehold land the building sits on, I’m optimistic that the business will continue for decades to come.

What I appreciate most is that the coffee is still consistently solid, the food is as good as I remember, and the place still has that easygoing charm that makes you want to hang around a bit longer than planned.

So many places change, chase trends. Common Man has just quietly kept its quality over the years.

Always a good meal, always a good coffee and somehow it still feels like coming back to a familiar spot. ☕

reviews.text:
I recently dined at PS.Cafe at Raffles City and had a pleasant overall experience. The ambience was as expected—stylish, relaxed, and perfect for a casual catch-up or a quiet meal in the city.

For mains, I ordered the king prawn aglio olio. The prawns were fresh and reasonably juicy, and the pasta was cooked al dente. The garlic and olive oil combination was fragrant, though I felt it could have had a bit more depth or spice to elevate the flavors further.

The Caesar salad was disappointing. The dressing  seemed odd, but the ingredients tasted fresh.

Dessert was the highlight of the meal—the marshmallow brownie with vanilla ice cream. The brownie was rich, warm, and gooey, paired perfectly with the cold, creamy ice cream. The toasted marshmallow added a nice sweetness and texture contrast, making it a satisfying end to the meal.

Service was attentive and efficient, though the restaurant can get quite busy during peak hours. Overall, a reliable spot for comforting Western dishes in a chic setting.

We reached the outlet at 8pm and were informed that this promotional price was only applicable for the first 2 hours. Any subsequent hours would be charged at $28++ per hour.

The rooms were clean, the sound system was great, and the song selection was good.
Just felt disappointed with the pricing arrangement, as it came across as misleading.

places.name: NamNam Raffles City
places.address: 252 North Bridge Road #B1-47, Raffles City Shopping Centre, Singapore 179103

reviews.text:
13/1/26 at 11:20am - To my great surprise, I was customer #2 today🤔

As a creature of habit, Nam Nam has been my lunch venue for almost EVERY visit to Raffles City in the past 10 years. But after today, I will NOT be returning here for lunch ever again. Because prices are now higher, portions are smaller and food quality is down.

👎 no more lunch sets of a bowl of noodle with protein, side dish & drink. Now I pay more for the bowl of noodle.
👎 today my hot lotus tea is $5.50😱 which is unbelievable for a hot drink with some flavour.
👎 the soup standard has slipped throughout the years. Today’s version was weakest. It’s just a bowl of brownish liquid that looks like soup but the robust flavours of the version I loved at first slurp from years ago are gone. For good.
👎 the beef slices came clumped together and the texture was not appetising. I don’t believe the higher price was justified for a REGULAR portion that didn’t even fill me up properly. There was a serving of basil leaves and bean sprouts but these looked like visual distractions to make up for the lack of a free side dish 🙄
👍 service staff was cordial and attentive but their readiness to serve means nothing when there are only one or two diners. By 12pm, the only people who came in were a handful of tourists. Then some office workers came but the scenes of long queues and packed restaurants are no more.

Today’s lunch here cost $23 but I was still hungry and had to buy a bun from a bakery, which meant total spent was about $26.

For that amount, the next time I come to Raffles City, I will find a new lunch venue that gives me more value. Bye bye Nam Nam 👋 it’s not me, it’s you!

reviews.text: Been a fan of Nam Nam since its opening but I honestly haven’t had it in the last few years since the menu change and there isn’t crab noodles or seafood pork noodles anymore. Still tastes decent but I have to say it’s unlike before. Still find it tastier in the past. Pho used to be served with a small plate of herbs (mint leaves, basil, bean sprouts, chilli and lime wedge) but seems like they don’t anymore — you have to request for it and even then they don’t give you everything. There is a limit of 45mins eating time (to ease the queue), though it’s not strictly enforced but it’s quite stressful. I can’t enjoy to the fullest because I feel like I’m being watched when I’m done with my food and they want me to leave. I would say there are greater Vietnamese options out there but if you do have some cravings and Nam Nam is close by, give it a go.

reviews.text: Fusion western restaurant that infuses  local flavors into standard western cruisine framework. I have had their pasta in the past, and the Cincalok steak, and have returned for the steak this time around. I consider their rendition a successful and adventurous mix, such that I would be back for theiress conventional steak, to say the least. The cincalok is an unexpectedly exciting partner to their decently done steak, sauce and all. There is no mistake for if you are after a higher tier pristine steak experience, this may not be it. For anything else, this has been on my mind for awhile, for that strong unami kick is unforgettable. It can get a little too salty though, considering the use of cincalok is a matter of dealing with an item of very high salt content in its native form. Present as well is the lemon grass chicken which is crispy and drench in the aforementioned sauce and respectably satisfies my crave for protein. The soup of the day is Spicy Sour soup and is also done properly with the appropriate amount of thickening. The execution of the dishes does well to continue my faith in this fusion menu, which has taken care and consideration for use of Asian/Singaporean flavor profile to thoughtfully pair with their western counterpart. This shine through amongst the many others which may fall short, sometimes by an appalling margin.
