Went around 11pm, still the same old taste.. to put it simply in words, first look doesn’t feel appetising, but it’s the few spoonful of rice, meat, veggie, and most importantly curry and lor zhap.. 5start rating would be too high for taste, but a 4.3-4.4 star is definitely good enough.

Normal service and atmosphere. Won’t complain becos nostalgia comes at a cost.

Really good restaurant, and just like all the reels and videos, they really drowned it with the curry sauce. While it can be off putting for some people, the individuals item was actually really delicious and makes you wanting more. The portion is big but we finished fairly quick
Very appetising scissor cut curry rice. Paid $4.80 for 1 meat, 2 Vegetables. It's not very spicy, portion is just nice for me. Simple eating place. Very fast in serving. Thanks!

I recently visited Coffee Addiction located at 13 Stamford Road #B2-25 Capitol Singapore and tried a few items from their menu.

I ordered the curry chicken with rice, but unfortunately the chicken was over too soft and the curry tasted rather bland. The flavor reminded me more of an Indian-style curry, but it lacked richness and depth.

I also tried the prawn noodle with shabu shabu. The prawns were fresh, which was a plus, but the broth was just average and the dish overall did not stand out.

Lastly, the siew mai was quite disappointing as it was dry and hard.

Overall, the cafe is still fine if you’re looking for a quick grab-and-go bite or just a cup of coffee. However, their food dishes could definitely use some improvement in flavor and quality.
World Cup 2026 screening. Free and easy seating at Capitol’s Outdoor Plaza . 9am-10pm matches only. Big screen.

Located at B2-48-50,
Grace TCM specializes in woman’s health and wellness. Doing facial, massage, TCM postpartum care and Tuina therapy

My father’s feet specialized in foot massage and body massage, TCM Tuina and many more.
What a fantastic department store. You can everything under one roof. And beautifully displayed. A shoppers paradise.

OG at Bugis is a well-stocked department store offering a wide range of products, from clothing and cosmetics to household essentials and travel goods. The store has a traditional department store feel, with organized sections making it easy to browse.

It’s especially known for its good selection of fashion, including formal and casual wear, along with branded cosmetics and skincare products. The home and kitchen section also has a decent variety of useful household items. Prices are reasonable, and there are often promotions and discounts available.

The staff are generally helpful, and the store is well-maintained, making it a convenient shopping stop in the Bugis area.

I had a negative experience with the home delivery service. Both the salesman and cashier informed me that the delivery department would contact me one day in advance via phone call, followed by a WhatsApp message. However, I did not receive any call the day before the scheduled delivery. On the actual delivery day, I received a WhatsApp message from the delivery personnel, stating a delivery window of 11 AM to 2 PM. The message did not indicate that a reply was required. Approximately 20 minutes later, I received another message stating that since there was no reply, the goods would be returned to the origin. I attempted to call the driver, but the call went unanswered. When I contacted the delivery department, they repeatedly stated that this was a third-party delivery service and they were unable to intervene. They requested that I provide them with the text messages from the delivery service. After sending the messages, I did not receive any acknowledgment of receipt or updates on the progress, necessitating multiple follow-up calls from my end. I had to call the delivery department more than six times regarding this issue. The service was truly unsatisfactory.

This mall, situated between Bendeemer and Lavender, is a middle-sized mall with a big food court in the middle. There is Thai food, Japanese cuisine, and two bakeries if my memory serves me right. There is also an atrium which has book sales or carnivals every now and then. Although people say its a quiet mall, it gets noisy during lunch hours

It has variety of stalls and many different companies
It has 2 towers which tower 1 and tower 2. Those are for companies
The mall is having the most famous restaurants, supermarkets and coffee shops
Azqore software company is in 8th floor in tower 2
McDonald’s headquarter is also there in tower 2
Parking 🅿️ facilities are there
Thai shops are there
It’s also called as Little Thailand
Cold storage supermarket is there
McDonald ℹ restaurant is there in first floor
Subway restaurant is there

Super green vegetable restaurant is there
EPIKEBAB is newly opened one

Heavy rain yesterday. Look at the video attached newly.

Kopi and tarts also there

Lift facilities are there to enter the towers
Access card are required
Wash room facilities are there in the first floor
POSB ATM is there in the first floor
Hao Lai ke restaurant is there

Last time I visited the Paris baguette which is located opposite of cold storage
Thai Supermarket has everything I need, awesome vegan options at folks collective restaurant and vegan ice cream at The Pack store. Lv 3 has open Annex to chill and enjoy the breeze near ARK Court!

Location is superb. Room was spacious, clean and well equipped (with everything I needed for my stay). Bed, pillows and climate control were comfortable. Bathroom was of high hygienic standard and everything worked just fine. Housekeeping was top. Front desk staff were friendly, professional and highly attentive. Breakfast was a bit 'boring'.

Royal Plaza on Scotts is an exceptional hotel that delivers comfort, convenience, and warm hospitality right in the heart of Singapore. From the moment you arrive, the staff greet you with genuine friendliness, making you feel welcomed and well taken care of throughout your stay. The hotel’s vibrant lobby, modern design, and inviting atmosphere set the tone for a memorable experience.
The rooms are spacious, spotless, and thoughtfully designed, offering plush bedding, excellent amenities, and a relaxing environment after a long day in the city. One of the standout features is the complimentary minibar and high‑speed Wi‑Fi, which adds great value and convenience for both business and leisure travelers.Its location is unbeatable — just steps away from Orchard Road, with easy access to shopping, dining, and transportation. Whether you’re exploring the city or attending meetings, everything feels effortlessly within reach.
The breakfast buffet is another highlight, offering a wide variety of delicious options, from international dishes to local favorites. The service team is attentive, efficient, and always ready to assist with a smile.Overall, Royal Plaza on Scotts delivers a perfect blend of luxury, comfort, and hospitality. It’s a hotel that consistently exceeds expectations and makes every stay truly enjoyable.

Had a wonderful stay at Royal Plaza on Scotts. The hotel is lovely, with extremely clean and spacious rooms that make the stay feel very comfortable and relaxing. The staff were exceptionally friendly and welcoming throughout.
The buffet was another highlight  a really good spread with delicious food and plenty of variety. The location is also ideal, especially for shopping lovers, with many malls and shopping spots within walking distance. Overall, a very convenient and enjoyable stay in Singapore.

Many stalls were closed when I reached there today @ 3.50pm ( 9 May 2026, Saturday ) . It’s a medium size hawker centre. Many drinks stalls . I went there specifically for the famous Ivy’s Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup but my own fault that I didn’t check their operation hours and they were closed at 3pm.

As not many stalls were open at the time I was I there so not many choices. I went for the fish soup and it was good 👍🏻.

Also tried the famous rojak . It was good 👍🏻 too.

The tables were clean.

The food centre is well ventilated with many fans installed overhead. So it was windy and comfortable eating there. Flies appear around 6+pm though. Not sure why.

There were many customers at 4pm. More customers when I left the food centre at 7pm. Many workers in technicians uniforms came in for their dinner 🍽️ .

I will definitely return for the Hainanese Herbal Mutton Soup on another day.

Hawkers centre is very clean. Floor is almost spotless. Tables are cleared and cleaned. Not many stalls opened on a Sat night. Had the seafood soup. Didnt enjoy it as it had a bad fishy after taste.

The fruit rojak was good and priced reasonably. Drinks aunty was very friendly.

The place was not hot as there were fans and it was well ventilated.

Good hawker centre right next to MRT station with plenty of good choices at reasonable prices.

There’s a segregation of Malay Indian stalls and a non-halal local side.

Favourites are Jubilant chicken rice!
Many other stalls like roasts, BCM fishball noodles are highly rated.

Also a Japanese ramen with high ratings!

Good coffee too!

I found prices are generally lower here than other hawkers in the city.

Only gripe is the amount of smokers who stood or sit around the hawker centre to smoke. Sometimes the smoke comes right to the seated eating areas.

Leisure Park Kallang is a laid-back shopping center with just the right amount of traffic—not too crowded, making it comfortable to explore.
It offers a bit of everything: a kids’ arcade, tuition centers, a bowling alley, a food court, and numerous restaurants and cafés.
Overall, it’s a good place to visit if you prefer a quieter, more relaxed atmosphere away from the usual mall crowds.

This mall, especially when viewed against the backdrop of its more prominent neighbors, is relatively underwhelming.

While it boasts a good selection of restaurants and food options, the overall shopping experience feels somewhat haphazard in my opinion. It's certainly not the first mall that comes to mind when you're looking to do some serious shopping.

Given that the primary patrons of the Kallang/Stadium area are typically athletes, sports enthusiasts, or concert-goers, I can only envision them visiting this mall predominantly for its food offerings.

Very near MRT, the shops here always opened and closed forever more like pop up stores as business has been bad with weak traffic after the open air carpark has closed for the temp swimming competition but when it is over since late 2025, the structure seems to be left there rotting. The level 1 food court is nice, very big supermarket at B1 Sheng Song. Open and shelter carpark lots available. Many eateries with Burger King as the only fast food and a KTV outlet beside it. Level 2 is very boring apart from a bowling allery. Nothing much for tourists to shop or see.

Walking distance to Kallang Wave Mall.

The cheese otah is damn good, get it deep fried. We like the dry version the best! They can deep fry the mantou, lotus root and potato into chips.

We had the collagen mala soup. It was very drinkable and not so ‘qiang’ or spicy.

Flavourful Thai milk tea as well.

Finally understand the hype since it’s my first time here!

📍A Hot Hideout

Ngl, this Mala Xiang Guo broke my healthy dieting spell. 😅

I was delighted to see the lotus roots that I ordered transformed into crispy, crunchy snacks. I also tried the fried potato which was so addictive!

AHH mlxg is good for diners who can take level up spicy mala and 重口味 strong flavours. My siao la is two chillis up for me. 🥵 They also serve fried mantou which is interesting. The food is not cheap but worth a try.

#tiramisoooo #tramisoooojiaks #jiakjiakjiak #ahothideout #malaxiangguo

Hot Hideout is THE place I go to for my mala fix! It also so happens that I study here so the outlet at NUS makes it really easy to satisfy my cravings.

The one mala variant I always get here is the mala collagen soup. If you want dry mala, the one at Chinatown complex (iykyk), is way better. However, where this place beats every other mala place is the fact that they offer to deep fry certain ingredients like the luncheon meat, potato, lotus root etc.

Is it cheap? Most definitely not. As a big eater, and as a guy, I often spend $20 for my portion. A tip from me: if you’re dining by yourself or you and your friends are not sharing, don’t order the potato. It’s a good 300g+ and you’ll end up paying easily over $8 for a single potato - which is ridiculous imo.

Maximise your budget by getting meat, and if you want something deep fried, try the mantou buns. They pair beautifully with the peanut sauce 🤤

Another tip: come here on the weekends as there are barely any students around and you won’t need to queue.

Visited the iconic Long Bar, famous for the Singapore Sling.
The atmosphere inside is absolutely शानदार — truly one of a kind.
I really enjoyed the unique tradition of throwing peanut shells on the floor, which added to the fun and authenticity of the experience.
We ordered the Original Singapore Sling and the Raffles 1915 Gin Sling, both of which were excellent.
The bar was very busy, and unfortunately our drinks took more than 20 minutes to arrive. It seemed like the order might have been forgotten, but once the waiter noticed, he quickly took care of it.
Despite that small issue, the incredible ambiance completely made up for it.
Overall, a very satisfying experience and definitely worth visiting.

Birth place of the Singapore Sling, a visit here is a must experience for a stay in Singapore!
Midweek there was a very short wait to get in, sat at the bar have a great view of the cocktails being made - including the fascinating hand-cranked cocktail shaker.
Bar staff very friendly, good to have a chat with them between drinks.
Good range of the menu, but obviously their signature Singapore Sling is recommended - may be over S$40 but worth it for being here. Tradition of throwing the peanut shells onto the floor is novel but also adds to it, definitely unique!

What an iconic place! The Long Bar is home to the original Singapore Sling and would highly recommend popping in for a drink.

The hotel itself is absolutely gorgeous, and getting to sip on a cocktail in the place it was conceptualized was a highlight of my trip to Singapore.

The bar offers bowls of peanuts to snack on, and you’ll find peanut shells scattered across the floor, which adds to the delightful atmosphere

The lines to get in can get long, so arrive early to snag a spot at the bar!

YY Kafei Dian feels like stepping into old Singapore with just enough modern touches to keep things comfortable. The kaya toast here uses proper old-school buns — thick, fluffy, slightly crisp outside, and perfect with the rich kaya and butter combination. Soft eggs, traditional kopi and tea, and even the cakes bring back that nostalgic coffee shop experience that’s getting harder to find.

What I really liked was how they preserved the old-school ambiance while quietly modernising the operations. The place still feels very 80s/90s Singapore kopitiam, but with digital payments, order buzzers, and smoother service flow. It’s nostalgic without feeling outdated.

Simple food done properly. No overcomplication, no gimmicks — just solid traditional breakfast culture preserved well.

Delicious, thick, soft, Kaya Toast Bun! Plenty of kaya spread in this thing, matched with coffee makes for an awesome kopitiam breakfast! Place can get crowded at even strange times of the day. Queue can get lengthy so be prepared for that. Tables can remain uncleaned at times due to the visitor volume, but staff are very quick to help! Would stop by again if less crowded!

Overly rated & hyped up. A tourist trap!!!

Ordered a pork chop with rice & iced lemon tea. The meat was not too bad but hardly any sauce so rice was very dry. 🙄 The cup of iced lemon tea was the smallest cup ever! 😝😝

I went to get some chilli but didn't see the signage stating if need any cutleries or condiments to ask the serving staff. An old man in the cafe uniform who was seated at the back table raised his voice saying, Hello... I quickly apologised for my mistake but he continued raising his voice... I had to stopped him & told him, I already apologised & he doesn't have to create a scene.

I gave the service 3 🌟 cos the same person who took my order & payment was very polite. Do note this cafe only accept cash. The rest of the service staff seems like they were under pressure to quickly clear the table even though the cafe was barely full.

Honestly, not worth eating there as there are better eateries elsewhere. Even the cafe down the building is much better.

I highly recommend visiting Singapore City Gallery — it’s absolutely worth your time. The exhibitions are incredibly engaging and thoughtfully designed, with many interactive elements that allow visitors to actively participate rather than just observe. There are plenty of hands-on activities and immersive displays, making the whole experience both fun and informative. I was truly impressed by how much there was to see and do, and I left with a deeper appreciation for Singapore’s urban planning. Definitely a must-visit spot!

Small Island Big Plans ❤️

Enjoyed the "In Our Time" mural by Lee Xin Lin
Totally awesome visual narrative because it depicts an intricate, vivid landscape of Singapore, blending historical landmarks with olden days memories and local culture references. We had fun spotting and identifying and discussing the references.

Later on further in the gallery, enjoyed the interactive board when we lookup our own postcodes. East side is best side!

Impressive also the panoramic cityscape drawing from memory by the autistic savant. Somebody help solve the mystery what is the landmark way further back. Even the on-site gallery guide wasn't sure.

We also love maps so studying the colonial maps and historical evolution of cartography made us wonder what it was like way back ancient years ago

As a history teacher, I found the Singapore City Gallery to be a masterclass in storytelling. It is deeply informative and educational, tracing the island’s evolution with incredible precision. What surprised me was how engaging and moving ALL the exhibits were, seeing the delicate balance between heritage preservation and future-ready planning. A must-visit for anyone who wants to understand the 'why' behind the skyline.

Don’t skip this! The Singapore City Gallery is a hidden gem for history buffs and urban explorers. It’s educational, engaging, and deeply moving to see how much thought goes into every square inch of this city. A highly informative experience that makes your city walks much more meaningful. A total must-visit!

Had a weekend lunch/brunch here. The restaurant itself is beautiful, being situated at a great location. However, I felt that for the price, the food was only so-so. The truffle fries were great, and I did enjoy the carbonara. But for the price, I feel that there shld be some authentic pancetta or guanciale used for the carbonara. The hot honey pepperoni pizza was decent. The sticky date pudding was also quite good. However I felt the shakshouka did not taste great — the bread was delicious, but the shakshouka sauce was underwhelming. While the food was decent, I do believe there are other cafes that offer better food at more reasonable prices. Moreover, the restaurant is arranged in a circle, and I found that waiters and waitresses rarely walked to the ‘back’ end of the circle where we were seated, which made ordering and getting water refills, etc take an extremely long time.

+I have frequented several P.S. Cafe locations, and this particular establishment stands out as a personal favorite. In my opinion, it surpasses the Damseyhill location, which is widely recognized by tourists.

+You can enjoy a splendid view of Marina Bay Sands and Merlion Park from this venue.

+The truffle fries were exceptionally crispy and remarkably non-greasy. I highly recommend trying them.

-Please note that securing a desirable table without a prior reservation may be challenging.

-While the prices are on the higher side, the overall experience justifies the cost.

This waterfront bay view restaurant stands nicely if you make a reservation in time. Dinner is extremely busy, however the staff is extremely warm and kind. We ordered: 1) the super food salad 2) truffle fries (has a lot of crispy fries, bold Parmesan flavor and plenty of food) and 3) seafood carbonara (has better than average seafood and plenty of pasta). The salad has a good mix of acidity and sweetness (a good mix of blueberries and broccoli and spinach) plus quinoa. 4) passionfruit cooler gives you plenty of passionfruit flavor with soda.

Service was excellent! I made an appointment for 3pm but arrived 30 minutes early. Instead of asking me to wait, the staff kindly registered me immediately without any issues. The entire process was smooth and efficient, and all the staff were very friendly and helpful throughout.

Dr. Chan, the female doctor, was especially kind and professional as well. Thank you all for your warm hospitality and excellent service.

This was for a new work permit medical check-up, and I was pleasantly surprised that the medical report was ready within just two days. Everything was completed in less than 30 minutes. Highly recommended!

I had an ultrasound scan done at this clinic and was genuinely impressed with the experience. I managed to get a same-day appointment,  results were provided very quickly. The pricing was also very reasonable.

I was very happy with the specialist who performed the ultrasound. she was very careful, and made me feel comfortable throughout the procedure.

I would highly recommend this clinic to anyone who prefers to avoid long waiting times at other imaging centres.

I came to ATA Medical for my yellow fever jab before my trip to South America. The charges were reasonable and cheaper than TTSH travel clinic. The location was convenient and I was administered with the jab right after registration with the counter staff. They allow online appointment booking and ensure that the patients don’t wait for long. The staff and nurses sweet polite and professional, it was a very pleasant visit.

Stopped by Golden Village at Suntec City to purchase a pair of movie vouchers for a corporate giveaway and the experience was smooth and hassle free. The staff were helpful in explaining the voucher options and the transaction was completed quickly without any issues.

The cinema compound itself was clean, well maintained, and conveniently located within Suntec, making it easy to access. It is also spacious with decent waiting and seating area. Queue system is efficient too.
Super fresh and great caramel coated popcorn . Even though it's $9.50 for one box of popcorn but I have not eaten popcorn for a long long time. I'll slowly enjoy each piece

My second time watching a gold class movie here, and I must say that the service and quality has been superb. Also tried their mains for the first time - clams and mushroom pasta and laksa pasta, both were good! Unable to take photos as the movie was screening. Staffs were also polite and professional

The Apple Store at Marina Bay Sands is probably the place where you walk in without expectations but somehow ended up standing around like you were in a modern-day cathedral dedicated to beautiful design.

My tip? Don’t rush straight into the dome. Head downstairs first and take the escalator ride up. There’s something almost magical about the way the giant glass sphere slowly reveals itself. It’s like the building is saying, “Wait for it… wait for it…”

And then -The space opens up. The curves. The lines. The sunlight dancing through the glass. The stunning view of Marina Bay stretching into the blue skies. It’s one of those places where you suddenly forget its a store.

Watch the neat rows of Apple devices lined up like they were attending a very expensive family reunion. Macky screens shimmering. People excitedly setting up their new gadgets. Others bringing their Apple devices in for resuscitation and what not. Amid all the buzz, find a quiet corner and take a moment, there’s a surprising sense of peace here.

The building looks like it’s from the future.

The customer service? Somehow still waiting to arrive.

This Apple Store is an architectural masterpiece floating on the bay, and it’s definitely worth seeing. It’s about a 15-minute walk from Raffles Place or around 5 minutes from Bayfront through Marina Bay Sands.

Now for the adventure…

I entered from the upper level where several staff in green shirts were gathered. Unfortunately, they seemed far more interested in chatting with each other than acknowledging customers. Not even eye contact.

So I went downstairs to find someone else. Same story.

Eventually, I returned to the entrance and asked two staff members for help, only to be told to ask someone inside. Ah yes… the classic Apple relay race begins.

Staff #1 → Staff #2 → Staff #3.

By the time I finally collected my purchase, I’d met half the team.

This isn’t my first visit, and honestly, every visit feels exactly the same. There are plenty of staff, yet somehow nobody actually helps you. Friendly is great, but standing around chatting while customers are hunting for assistance isn’t what I’d call customer service.

If you’re choosing between Apple Stores in Singapore, I’d personally head to Orchard instead. At least there, the relay race is shorter.

easily the most special and impressive Apple Store I have ever visited. It looks like a bubble floating on the sea, with a stunning background of the Singapore Skyline made of skyscraper. The whole exterior design is very futuristic, while the interior design is similar to typical Apple Store. Still, the lighting inside is beautifully designed. You can enter the store via a bridge, it feels like I am boarding on a spaceship.There is also a basement level, connecting to the Marina Bay Sands.

Chinatown Singapore is a great place to visit, full of character and culture. There are many shops and restaurants to explore, offering a wide variety of food and souvenirs. The old Chinese heritage buildings are beautiful and well-preserved, adding to the charm of the area. A perfect place to spend time exploring and soaking in the atmosphere.

Visited Chinatown Complex in Singapore during Chinese New Year and the vibe was amazing 🎎✨
The whole place was beautifully decorated with lights and festive items, which made the experience even more special.
Food options are plenty, but very few vegetarian choices are available, so that can be a bit difficult for veg visitors.
Still, the atmosphere, crowd, and cultural feel make it a must-visit place in Singapore.
Great place to explore, eat, and enjoy the festive mood.

Exploring the vibrant streets of Chinatown — a perfect blend of culture, colors, and flavors. From bustling markets and traditional architecture to mouth-watering street food, every corner tells a story. A must-visit spot for anyone who loves authentic experiences and lively vibes!

We had our quick snack here. We ordered the original Kaya toast bread with coffee. Taking video is not allowed as per employee and we cannot request ice for the coffee too. You cannot ask also for creamer or sugar for coffee because they want to preserve their own recipe. So what ever was given, just eat and taste the originally prepared to you.

We came to try the Kaya toast and ordered both the peanut butter set and the regular Kaya set. It's a good option if you like sweet and savory combinations. They offer hard-boiled or soft-boiled options for the eggs served alongside; we chose hard-boiled, but it wasn't really hard-boiled. Still, we liked it and recommend it.

Jan 2026 update - this place is a tourist trap. If you are a tourist and want to get good kaya toast and eggs, go to the Yakun outlet at One Raffles Place basement instead.

Mid Sep 2025 update - teh gao gah dai not thick and not sweet. Made me an unhappy customer. Minus one star.

Early Sep 2025 - I'm a fan of yakun eggs, but this outlet gave me one broken yolk and the eggs were not as warm as the other outlets. Also had to wait longer than usual despite no queue. Teh gao gah dai was more sweet than thick, but passable. Unlike other outlets, they don't remember me even though I've been here thrice in 2 weeks. Also no tissue available - other outlets great service, pass me tissue when they see me right after I order despite super long queue (one Raffles plc). Great service makes a lot of difference, hope this outlet can improve. Also weird that main door is kept closed, and the only entrance is by the side, narrow and hard to navigate in esp when there is a queue. Fans in the eatery also blow hair in all directions. Overall really not near my top few fav yakun outlets at all.

I had a very pleasant stay at Dorsett Changi Singapore. I chose this hotel because I had an early morning flight the next day, and it turned out to be an excellent choice.

The room was surprisingly spacious by Singapore standards, clean, comfortable, and well-maintained. The hotel is conveniently located right next to a shopping mall, making it easy to find food, do some shopping, or simply relax without having to travel far.

What stood out the most was the friendliness of the staff. They were warm, welcoming, and always ready to help. They even kindly helped take photos of me and my friend, which was a thoughtful gesture that made our stay even more memorable.

The check-in process was smooth and efficient, while check-out was incredibly easy - simply dropping the room key card into the designated box. The proximity to Changi Airport also made the journey stress-free and allowed me to avoid rushing for my early morning flight.

Overall, Dorsett Changi Singapore offers a great combination of comfort, convenience, and excellent service. I would definitely stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a comfortable hotel near the airport.

Great hotel with a strategic location. The views from my room were great. There is a laundry in the 7th floor you can use, it cost 8sgd for a washing cycle and 8sgd for a dryer cycle. There is a patio/terrace on the same floor with great views but there’re no chairs or bench to sit so you just it’s not very good to hang out in there. There are vending machines for orange juice, water, instant noodles and starbuck coffee in the lobby.

The room is small but it was in good shape and had amazing views.

Great location.  Found out it has its own exit (no. 4) from Outram underground station on our last day! Short walk to Chinatown and the Maxwell Hawker market.
Comfy bed, great shower and aircon but the room was rather tired and could have done with a deeper clean.  Overall, a nice stay with super friendly staff. Oh and easy to use washing machines and dryers on the 7th floor.  Great for travellers!

I highly recommend this hotel for your next trip to Singapore. Everything at the hotel was really good.
1. The staff were very helpful and friendly from the moment we walked in. They tried every way to get us checked in early at no cost and even brought up all our luggage to the room.
2. The room was very nice. Very clean and spacious. The bathroom was huge as well.
3. Breakfast/ swimming pool & hotel location were all good.

Again, highly recommend this hotel. Even though it might be more expensive than the other one but it is worth it.

In order to get hot water to the sink and shower, I was told I need to turn on the hot water at the bathtub first, and leave it on, THEN also turn on the hot water to the sink/shower. This was the "solution" that I was expected to accept after troubleshooting the issue over the span of 3 nights. Not only is this wasteful, it was inconvenient to say the least. Just shower/bath in the bathtub? Keep in mind the cleaning supplies were conveniently secured to the shower stall, with none by the bathtub - so, I had to go in and out of the bathtub, without falling thankfully, to wash up. Showering inside the tub turned into an aerobic experience, where I had to "shower" sitting/squatting down to minimize water splashing everywhere. Furthermore, there were no follow-ups from the service staff to confirm proper issue resolution, nor did they ask about the stay at check-out (shows how much they care). Not that I crave for attention, but I thought I was paying for the "stars".

Breakfast gets the job done, TV is on the smaller side, gym is about the size of a guest room, rooftop bar has leaks/puddles around the area. Sound/noise insulation sounded pretty good, AC performed well, WiFi functional.

If you find this sort of experience acceptable for $200+ per night, then you're at the right place!

I guess they can get away with subpar accommodation for being in the city center. Probably not too hard to find better value for the money in the area.

Our stay at Carlton City Hotel Singapore was wonderful from start to finish. The hotel is modern, comfortable, and perfectly located, but what truly made our experience stand out was the service. A special thank you to Jenna at reception. She welcomed us with genuine warmth, helped us settle in smoothly, and made every interaction feel effortless. Her professionalism and kindness set the tone for our entire stay.

Carlton City is a great choice for anyone visiting Singapore, and the staff make it even better. We would happily return.

The Food court here is kept quite clean , pretty airy and located just above the market. Can access by lift or staircase. I like the chicken noodle fried that comes with soup. The small portion is SGD4, add one egg is SGD4.7
Hubby took the fried prawn Mee at SGD5, which is salty for me. Drinks although long Q at the Ah Teik, but taste is so so. Sweet bun is not bad with Kaya n condensed milk

林记 mee hoon kuey is the best in Singapore. For 7 years, whenever I drop by, I'd just eat their MHK. I don't even eat other stuff from this stall. The stall is relatively quiet compared to the adjacent wanton mee. Their kuey is handmade and very thick and chewy. My mom could taste that the secret ingredient adding porridge to the flour to give it additional texture. The soup is very clean. Other top rated MHK in SG are often too salty, or they add starch to make their soup gravy-like. Not this one. The garlic flakes and prawns (if you order large) give the soup an aromatic and refreshing seafood flavour.

A very authentic food ctr. It's been here at least since the 80s i believed.

Many stalls offered well priced and nice local foods. So happy that it's not dominated by overseas / Chinese F&B, retaining it's local food scene.

The chicken rice stall I've dined at got very delicious soy chicken. The dumpling soup is surprisingly tasty too.

Came on a Sunday, 40% stalls were closed but good enough for us.  Plus it's not as crowded... clean space, and airy....

Multiple visits and Nylon has never once missed.

No food menu, small standing-room plus some sitting space indoor and outdoor in Everton Park, roastery visible behind glass with the IMF roaster running. The whole setup makes clear that coffee is the only agenda here.

The bar runs a Mahlkönig CORE grinder into an xBloom precision brewer — consistent, technical, no shortcuts. Brewed at 1:17 across filters, which gives the cup exceptional clarity.

The bean rotation is genuinely impressive. I've had the Washed Ethiopia Banko Gotiti Heirloom — bright, lemonade-like, floral. The Washed Nicaragua Parainema — stone fruit and wild honey. And the Colombia La Laja Washed Geisha — one of the cleaner, more elegant cups I've had in Singapore. The menu rotates with the same seriousness as the brewing.

If you're new to specialty coffee, Nylon will reset your expectations. If you already know what you're looking for, you'll keep coming back. One of the best in the city, full stop.

One of the best coffee in town. The coffee is amazing! They really go an extra mile to ensure every cuppa is of quality. Their barista would serve you and share the best way to consume it.

We had an ice white and another with oat milk. Love it 🥰 the coffee blends so well with milk but not losing the aroma.

Prices are humble, like their warm service. They even offer a small discount for folks over 60, allowing everyone able to enjoy a nice cuppa.

I will definitely come back soon.

Nylon Coffee is not only recommended by the Singapore Tourism Board, but also suggested by experienced coffee professionals. What's unique is its location on the ground floor of a residential complex facing the central courtyard.

Inside, the shop possesses a lot of high-end coffee equipments such as the latest model La Marzocco Strada X 2grp with straight-in portafilters, EK43, and Ceado Titan grinders. The owner has also replaced the previously used Probat roaster (German-made renowned coffee bean roasters) with an Italian-made iMF roaster. According to the baristas, iMF can roast very light/light roasted beans more thoroughly, preventing the coffee beans from being undercooked in the center.

We ordered a Colombian pour-over and a white coffee. The Colombian coffee was refreshingly sweet and delicate, with no astringency whatsoever, which left a deep impression on us…

The shop was bustling with customers as soon as it opened in the morning. The owners were very friendly, interacting warmly with their customers. The owner, knowing we were from Taiwan, chatted with us and introduced us to other excellent local coffee shops (unfortunately, the Maxi Coffee was closed on the day).

We thought that Nylon is a highly professional, warm, and locally-flavored Singaporean coffee shop. It's definitely worth a special visit!

Loved the ambience, atmosphere and food at this modern Australian Cafe / restaurant. They have different menu as per time, breakfast, brunch, evening snacks and dinner.
They have indoor and outdoor seating and vibe is really nice. The drinks menu is huge with some good cocktails.
The staff is courteous and service is fast. The food was fresh and delicious.
Special mention for the loaded nachos, Agliolio Pasta, Blueberry Mojito and Strawberry lemonade.
Highly recommend and will be back for sure.

Worth the price! Great food, great vibes, and great service.

This homely cafe has a highly relaxing atmosphere that's great for catching up with friends or just hanging out by yourself.

The food and drinks are excellent. The Full Breakfast was delicious; a hearty meal with an elevated take on a typical english breakfast. Standout was the scrambled eggs which were perfectly silky, as well as the bacon and sausage which were very flavourful and not too oily. Surprisingly the meal isn't as "heavy" as it looks - it's filling but doesn't make you feel bloated; A welcome departure from typical breakfast meals of this sort.

The avocado gula melaka smoothie was great too. Extremely fresh and not too sweet.

Service here is great too! Staff are super friendly and go out of their way to ensure a positive dining experience.

Best to make a reservation if you're coming on a weekend.

Visited on 31 Jan 2026. Food was great as usual and we commend the service. When we feedback that we could not find the flesh in the shell for the seafood aglio oglio, the staff re-cooked and re-served a whole new warm plate of food. We were impressed, because we are sure they do not have to do so. Worth returning for both food and services. 👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼

Lovely ambience and attentive staff! I thoroughly enjoyed the dining experience here with my family today.
We ordered a few different dishes and every one of them tasted surprisingly good! We unanimously agreed that the Gruyére Cheese Zucchini Croquette was the tastiest - crunchy on the outside and filled with cheese and veg inside - yumz!
I ordered the oven-roasted chicken leg. The meat was moist and succulent - though I would have preferred little more gravy.
Vegetarian friends don't have to get hungry here as there are many options and the dishes taste awesomely good too!

Enjoyed the À La Carte French Buffet at Vineyard @ HortPark. The food was freshly prepared and served to the table, with the grilled ribeye, mushroom soup and mussels being our favourites. Service was friendly and attentive, and the peaceful garden setting made the dining experience even more relaxing. The only downside is that the buffet menu is quite limited. If there were more variety, it would make the experience even better. Overall, a great place for quality food and a relaxing meal. Would definitely visit again!
But very kind of them to celebrate my hubby Birthday. Thank you to all the staffs in vineyard.

I stopped by Vineyard at HortPark for lunch and really enjoyed the buffet spread. There was a good variety of French dishes, and it was easy to find enough to suit my appetite. The service also stood out, especially Clarence, who was attentive throughout and made the visit feel well taken care of. I left satisfied and would happily come back.

Yubari Melon soft serve was excellent. Tried the curry sauce with McNuggets, it's decent but the Garlic Chili Sauce is the show stopper. Had the Chicken McCrispy, I like it better than Malaysia's Ayam Goreng McD. Staff are not attentive to the cash payment counter, I had to wait to be attended to on 2 occasions. First staff gave me a number to get my food served but the second one didn't.

Ordered the Bundled meal.  McSpicy and  Triple cheeseburger.  $16/- for two specific bundled meals.   Somehow the McSpicy is much smaller than usual,  and has the words “Promo” printed on box.  Its misleading because it gave impression of the same Mcspicy burger but it’s not.

ARC Macs outlet used to be very popular,  but no longer though its was a Sunday night.

The McCafe counter with Barista was scrapped,  and the current layout is very monotonous and squarish.  It’s a change but not better.

14 May 2026 Thurs. I am not eating your breakfast anymore. Yesterday evening, I ordered a cold latte with syrup. It arrived with no syrup. I had to go to the counter to get. And the staff didn't apologize, just gave me a cup with syrup. This early morning 5.30am, your male staff delivered my hotcakes missing another whipped butter & syrup. And he quickly looked down when approaching our table. Weird reaction. I thanked him for the delivery & he didn't even say a word & no smile. This is 5.30am & I as a customer had to make the effort to smile instead of him. I had to go to the counter to call many times for inside staff to come out. When finally, the female staff appeared, no smile. I showed her the receipt with 2 whipped butter & syrup stated & asked for them. She didn't apologize. Just gave me the whipped butter & went inside to get the syrup. The staff here need to go to Bangkok & Taiwan for training. The sides of the muffin were hard.

27 March 2026 Friday morning. Expensive & Very bad. The bread is so hard. Can't eat it. Have to throw away. What's wrong with the staff? Deteriorated from a few months ago. And yesterday, the Chicken Tomato burger was so poorly made & didn't look like chicken meat & fries were cold & hard. McDonald's in Taiwan & Bangkok way better. Staff here need to go to Taiwan to learn. Taiwanese staff are excellent & fast & the burgers & fries are properly done everytime.

First experience with the MRT in Singapore. Once we finally found the entrance it was quite easy to navigate. Many small restraunts in this Bugis station, even a 7-11 where I got a SLURPEE. Loved using the MRT. Very clean and safe.

Singapore’s MRT system is clean, efficient, and extremely reliable. Trains arrive frequently, stations are well maintained, and signage is clear, making it easy for both locals and tourists to navigate the city.

The network covers most parts of Singapore, with convenient connections between lines and seamless transfers to buses. Stations are generally equipped with lifts, escalators, and clear announcements, making travel accessible and comfortable.

Overall, the MRT is one of the best public transport systems in the world—fast, affordable, and stress-free. It’s the easiest way to get around Singapore.

Bugis MRT station is very different now it has becomes the interchange for the Downtown Line.

It also have many more facilities and better connected.

Crowded, but serves its purpose well.

Took my parents here for brunch on a Sunday. We had the hotdog on French toast, the fried chicken and the chilli crab spaghetti.
Food was pretty good. They enjoyed it.
Place was not crowded so it was a very pleasant atmosphere. Lots of parking spaces available too. Service staff were really friendly and kind. She suggested we take a table away from the window as it would get hotter and the aircon was not very strong that day.

The restaurant was right near the Hort Park office — cozy ambience, nice decor, and super friendly staff 😊
We had brunch withthe chicken scrambled eggs, garlic toast was crispy & fragrant, chicken strips were tasty, eggs were fluffy, and roasted potatoes 🥔 were perfect. Sauted prawn was savory & fresh seafood taste. We also received complimentary black coffee ☕ & ice water too. Chill spot for a relaxed brunch.

Came to this place as part of a business team dinner on a weekday evening. Upon arrival have to say the scenery is pretty nice and the place looks quiet and peaceful, would think it's probably more apt to come here for a meal and chill on a weekend brunch after a hike or a jog around the area.
The place was really quiet throughout the night. Other than the main table of us for about 15 people, they only served another pair in another table. It just felt like we had the entire place to ourselves.
Since there were quite a lot of us, we ordered quite a bit. First we started off with a few bottles of wine then we ordered food.
The menu was supposed to be decent but there were quite a number of items which were unavailable, which was what I initially wanted to order, like the mushroom soup, seafood sambal pasta and the apple crumble, all the supposedly more appealing dishes for me in the menu.
Ordered the starters to share and individually ordered a main each. The starters were decent in general but not fantastic, however the fried mushroom dish stood out among the rest and those who tried liked it.
I got the crabmeat aglio olio and was quite disappointed with it. My friend ordered the same but it wasn't consistent. His had wetness to it and it was okay while mine was totally dry and I found it too dry for my liking. The crab also didn't look fresh there was a stench to it.
Had a try of other dishes and thought probably the best of the mains we got was the pan seared smoked duck.
Since there was only one dessert left on the menu, we ordered the chocolate lava cake and it was pretty decent.
Overall was very filling cause we over ordered, but we all felt the food had hits and misses so it's probably very average. Price wise the mains are quite reasonable it's all in the 20s range but some of the salads and starters are on the expensive end.

My husband and I recently celebrated our 12th anniversary at voco Orchard Singapore, and what truly made this stay memorable was the exceptional hospitality from the Club Lounge team.

From the moment we arrived before check-in, the team made us feel welcomed and cared for. While waiting for our room to be ready, everyone was warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly. Throughout our stay, whether during afternoon tea, evening cocktails, or breakfast, the service was consistently excellent.

A special thank you to Ali, Chona, Josephine, Michelle, Justine and JX. Each of you contributed to making our experience comfortable and enjoyable. Your attentiveness, professionalism, and sincere hospitality did not go unnoticed. It wasn’t just good service—it felt personal and heartfelt.

The Club Lounge team was always observant, proactive, and welcoming. Small gestures, friendly conversations, and the effort taken to ensure guests were comfortable made a significant difference to our stay.

The room itself was comfortable, clean, and provided a relaxing environment for our anniversary celebration. However, what truly stood out was the people. Great facilities can be found in many hotels, but genuine hospitality is what creates lasting memories.

Thank you to the entire voco Orchard team for making our special occasion even more memorable. We look forward to returning in the future.

We chose the Voco Orchard for our wedding event.
Our wedding event was „smaller“ event with only 50 people and we were very glad that they have a location just fitting for this amount of people.
Ofcourse there are bigger rooms for bigger events aswell.
The whole process went very professional.
The preparations went very well thanks to the help of Ms Sunshine Garcia and Mr Ashok.
The team around Mr Ashok and the waiters are all nice and were attentive to our guests needs.
The banquet felt more like fine dining with a 7 course lunch menu and we surprised all of our guests with the variety and quality of the meals.
No one went home hungry.
The price is very reasonable and definitely not overpriced.
We can highly recommend the Voco Orchard to everyone. Not only as a hotel with a good service and beautiful rooms. But also as an wedding location for your special day.
Thank you very much !

3-night stay at Voco Singapore. Stayed in a King room which was very spacious. Amenities included a built-in filtered water tap, coffee pod machine, slippers. Room was comfortable and modern with USB outlets. Bathroom was a bit dated but everything worked fine. Breakfast was superb with 3 live stations for egg, soup noodles and Indian delights. Great range of dishes, some of which were rotated daily. The Italian restaurant on the rooftop has a lovely ambience. Hotel also has happy hour drinks daily from 5-7pm. Plenty of dining choices in the vicinity, including a huge food court in nearby Shaw House. Hotel is located 5 mins walk from the main shopping strip and Orchard station. Staff throughout the hotel were very courteous and friendly. We were grateful for the 1hr extension given for checkout. Highly recommend this hotel.

The MRT is a fantastic transport system. Really easy to use and work out which line is required for each of your destinations. To pay, all is required is a credit card and simply tap in at the start and tap out at your destination. The cost is absolutely minimal, the trains themselves are immaculate and are very frequent. Each stop or interchange there is at most only a couple of minutes to wait. All parts of Singapore are accessible, those are that aren't, for example the Singapore Zoo, there is a very conectable bus. Fun and simple to use, follow all the codes of conduct which are very catchy.

Easy MRT station to reach Little India. Very convenient if you want to explore the markets, temples and food streets nearby. Can get crowded during weekends but overall clean, safe and well connected to other MRT lines.

Little India MRT was very convenient and easy to navigate. The station is clean and well organised like most places in Singapore. Also felt a bit like home seeing Indian shops and people around. Connectivity from here is very good, so travelling becomes hassle-free. Overall smooth experience.

Esplanade Mall has transformed into a cultural centre, where  local and foreign artists showcased their talent and performance. when I was there during a weekend, there was actually a Chinese cultural festival. There was an artist performing Hokkien opera and she was teased in a very colourful and beautiful traditional Opera costume. She was singing a tune of Hokkien opera which was very captivating.

Around the mall they are multiple restaurants. There is a Peranakan restaurant on the second level and next to it as labyrinth Michelin star Restuarant. On the same level, there’s also a restaurant  serving local favourites such as chicken chop , Nasi lemak which seem pretty interesting and our try on my next round.
Food options are mainly expensive. Good place for shows.nice view
The mall is exceptionally clean. Maintaining such high standards of cleanliness with heavy foot traffic is commendable.

Visited the Malay Heritage experience during the opening weekend (2 May 2026), and it honestly felt worth the long wait after the renovation. The refreshed space looks beautiful & the exhibits really bring Malay culture and history to life. Personally, I still feel there’s something lacking … perhaps the content side is still developing … but it’s still nice to see the place vibrant again after being closed for so long.😅

First visit to this little heritage museum which appears to be part of a permanent exhibition. Well organized and all displayed clearly with corresponding context and storytelling. One can easily move from one section to another and learn about the history of the Malay communities here while also appreciating some of the related arts and culture. The wayang exhibit (shadow puppets) was particularly entertaining as it was an interactive display that caught the attention of almost every guest there. Free admission for all. Only steps away from historic Masjid Sultan.

Malay Heritage Centre is housed in the former Istana Kampong Gelam, a palace which was gazetted as a National Monument of Singapore in 2015. The centre showcases the history, culture and contributions of the Malay community within the context of Singapore’s history and multi-cultural society. Officially opened by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in June 2005, the Malay Heritage Centre provides wonderful cultural exposure and learning opportunities for visitors of all ages and interests. Situated amidst the Istana Kampong Gelam, Gedung Kuning and the surrounding Kampong Gelam precinct, the Centre acts as a vital heritage institution for the Malay community in Singapore. The first Istana Kampong Gelam was a traditional timber structure built on stilts, and in honour of the Istana's original layout, visitors will commence their tour of the permanent galleries from the upper level and end their visit on the ground level. In the traditional layout, the upper level is called the panggung, which serves as the main living and sleeping quarters of the house, while the kolong at the ground level is typically used as storage, work or service areas, and even as a children's play area.

Curry Bun - this was the best bun I’ve eaten!!

It was the perfect balance of sweet, spicy and flaky!!
The bun itself is sweet (but just the right amount), and the potato filling was just perfectly moulded into the bun. The filling was spicy, but the good kind, and they didn’t compromise on the filling.

The bun is best eaten hot, and I would go back for more!!! Best start to my trip.

I went around 1pm, so the classic buns were sold out.

I have visited this place a few times before and decided to bring a visitor here for their first experience. The cafe was pleasantly quiet on a weekday afternoon.

Instead of ordering the Classic Bolo Bun again, we decided to try the Curry Potato Bolo Bun - marketed as the world’s first curry bolo bun - along with two iced Americanos.

Unlike the Classic Bolo Bun, which I enjoyed during my previous visit more than a year ago, the Curry Potato version fell short of expectations. Personally, I felt that curry potato fillings would pair better with a softer bun rather than a bolo bun, which perhaps explains why this concept remains relatively uncommon. As for the iced Americano, it tasted more diluted than expected.

The prices were also slightly on the higher side for what we ordered. It feels acceptable as an occasional indulgence, though probably not something sustainable on a regular basis.

That said, when the cafe is not crowded, the second-level seating area offers a rather relaxing atmosphere. Complimentary ice water is also available, which is a thoughtful touch.

Stopped by Champion Polo Bun after hearing all the buzz and it definitely delivers if you are a fan of Hong Kong style bakery snacks done fresh.

The star of the show is obviously the polo bun. It arrives warm with that signature golden crust on top that is crisp, crumbly and lightly sweet. Bite into it and the inside is soft, fluffy and buttery, which creates that classic contrast that polo bun lovers are always chasing. The shop itself is small and casual, with a steady flow of people popping in for a quick snack or takeaway box. Seating can be a little tight during peak hours but the turnover is quick so it usually moves along. Love the three storey design and also including a very cosy third level as well.

Simple menu, well executed classics and very satisfying if you are craving a good polo bun in the Tanjong Pagar area. Definitely worth the stop.

What a beautiful atmosphere along with spectacular views of Marina Bay and the sites surrounding it.  The staff are are very professional and attend to all your needs, noticing that we were chilled when entering and being seated, we were offered shalls to put on our shoulders.
We decided on the Chef's Spring tasting menu for a sunset dinner, arrive early to get your choices in before 5:55 and take advantage of the dinner promotion.
We all enjoyed our choices and loved everything, the appetizers and meals were all cooked to perfection, followed by dessert for a few of us and 2 complementary trays of small bite options for us all to enjoy.
After dinner, we went to the outside area to enjoy the views of Marina Bay and all the surrounding sites.  The is a must for a special dinner while in Singapore!

Celebrated my birthday at Vue with my husband, the ambience + view + food + service was amazing.

We were given sofa seats side by side so we could appreciate the skyline. Also, their lunch set was value-for-money given the quality of the food. We enjoyed all the dishes ordered (other than the uni risotto which fell a little short of expectations), and will probably be back for more!

We dined here for one of our honeymoon dinners and it was incredible.

The venue, view, food and service was amazing.
We had magnificent fresh oysters, octopus so soft that you could slice with a butter knife and the T-Bone steak that was buttery and delicious paired with a red wine jus.

There was an honest miscommunication with something and we were actually abit rude to the waitress who i believe was actually the floor manager. Even so, she was extremely patient and understanding. We apologised at the time and apologise sincerely again. She did an amazing job servicing us and went above and beyond, so thank you to her.

5 star service, food & view 🌟

I honestly have nothing bad to say about this cheesecake. Everything was so good! The cheesecake was super yummy—the taste was just right. It had the perfect balance of salty, sweet, savory, and creamy.

I also liked the vibe of the place. It's cozy, and you can just enjoy your own little introvert moment even with other people around. The small corner seats are so cute too.

The crew was really nice and accommodating. They greeted us as soon as we walked in, which made us feel welcome right away.

Will definitely come back for more cheesecake! Next time, I'll try the Ube Cloud Cheesecake. If you love ube and taro, I think you'll definitely love it too!

Absolutely loved Queic by Olivia 🧀✨
Tried their Michelin-starred Signature Cheesecake and wow… definitely one of the best cheesecakes I’ve had. Super creamy, rich, and smooth with a perfectly balanced sweetness. The burnt top added such a nice deep caramelized flavor too 🤍

The place itself was quite small, but surprisingly still had plenty of seating space when I visited, so it felt comfortable and not too cramped.
Cozy atmosphere, friendly service, and the cheesecake was honestly 100% worth the hype. Would definitely come back for another slice 😭🫶🏻

Tried cheesecakes in different countries, but Quiec by Olivia (Singapore) is really different—you can actually taste the cheese, not just sweet, which I love. 😍✨

Our favorite is the cheddar burnt cheesecake, super good!!!!👍 The Dubai chocolate is also worth trying if you like something more indulgent.🌟

We also had the classic cheesecake with the Spanish latte with cloud foam—perfect combo. Went to the Kreta Ayer branch, nice and cozy vibe.

Angela was very friendly and nice—she made us feel welcome and gave great recommendations. Service was really good.

Will definitely come back!👌

Ps. Try their Olivia’s Signature Chocolate Cheesecake as well! Wahhhhh so good! 😍🤤✨

We recently held our wedding dinner on May 2026 at Artemis. We highly recommend and are really happy that we chose Artemis as our wedding venue.

We would like to thank the ARTEMIS team and we appreciate all the hard work and support for the dinner! Especially Kai & his team who were very responsive and prompt to reply throughout the planning stage.

They were really understanding and supportive of any last minute changes we had and went beyond in supporting the wedding dinner. His quick responses and suggestions throughout assured us that we were in good hands.

Artemis was also beautifully decorated from the amazing tea ceremony setup in the garden to the overall vibe of the restaurant.

The dinner was really well organised and beautifully executed, the feedback from the guests were really positive!

Of particular note was the tasty food. Many of the guests responded that it was the best tasting wedding dinner they had.

Perched on the 40th floor of the building and surrounded by others, the blocked view of Marina Bay and the Singapore Strait beyond was still quite spectacular. Outdoor dining is available but not recommended if heavy rain threatens. I imagine it would be nice in the evening but at lunch time, we preferred indoors! The large windows managed to filter any harsh sunlight and despite the bustle, it was a very relaxing meal. We had the Executive Lunch ($55 for 2 courses or $62  for 3). I orderd the cod for my main, which had that springy, slightly chewy texture i love. My companions had the pork, lamb and beef and all were not disappointed. Dessert was a satisfying sweet ending to the meal. Kudos to the attentive and efficient service staff who were constantly moving among the tables and making sure our glasses were never empty. From 12pm, the place quickly filled up and all tables were occupied so make reservations! Overall, a very pleasant experience across the menu selection, food quality, service and ambience. Will come back for dinner sometime!

What an experience. I've recently had my wedding dinner held at Artemis just last week on the 3rd of May, and to put it simply it was the proverbial 5-star experience.

I am based overseas and was searching for the right venue for a wedding dinner, so I had to rely solely on online reviews and video journals to research various venues around Singapore. Right from the beginning when I first submitted my enquiry, (Events) Manager Kai and Adrian had been very proactive and informative with their responses. Kai, who was the main coordinator for this journey, deserves special praise for his patience and willingness to really listen and provide solutions for the client.

Based on online research, we found Artemis fulfilled several of our criteria with it's wonderful outdoor sky garden, chic sky bar and classy but intimate dining space. Needless to say, I still had some reservations initially before the actual food tasting and site visit. All it took was one visit during the food tasting session to quell all of my doubts.

Working with Artemis' partner florist and design company, both extremely professional and responsive, they've helped create an evening of quiet magic and perfect ambience, exactly how I've envisioned it.

1. We had our tea ceremony at their assigned room, which was comfortable and had a pleasant backdrop perfect for phototaking. We also really appreciated the beautiful tea set and cups that was provided, something I had not expected.

2. We then had our solemnization at the outdoor sky garden, luckily the unpredictable weather was co-operative and everything went perfectly. We had specifically wanted a venue where an 'ourdoor garden' style solemnization was possible, and Artemis was one of the few places that provided such an option, at level 40 no less. We also really liked the cute tiffany chairs, and partner florist Elin did a beautiful job with the floral decor.

3. The sky bar area was something that (based on everything I've researched) most wedding venues did not provide, so it is rather unique to Artemis I would say. It has spectacular views of MBS and the bay, and many of my guests would say it is a unique experience to enjoy such a stylish space to themselves for a wedding/family event.

4. The dining area, while not the largest, fit my 120 guests perfectly. The ambience was everything I had hoped for, cozy, intimate and romantic, and had enough clear room for a 'stage' area for games and dancing. The star of this space, however, had to be the breathtaking lv40 views of the city, which provided amazing backdrops for phototaking.  One of my biggest regret due to being too busy as the groom, was how I wasn't able to really take in the dusk views, which is something Artemis is known for.

5. The food was everything I had hoped, and almost all the guests I've spoken to gave 5-star reviews. Amongst our favourites were the Black Cod, Burrata starter and the mango sticky rice dessert, even the complimentary mocktail drew huge praise my wife! I will readily admit I'm not usually a fine dining kind of person, but I absolutely look forward to the next time I return to Artemis.

6. Service was good, professional and understated, all feedback was also taken onboard positively and reacted upon quickly. Supervisors and servers were both well trained and handled themselves with a lot of grace.

Lastly, I want to extend my heartfelt thanks once again to Kai, your fantastic support made this all possible and I always felt like no problem couldn't be solved throughout this journey!

One of my favorite underground link Connect to many shopping malls.
Link to Suntec, marina square, capitol and Esplanade from city hall mrt Station. Very convenient... No sweat..

Horrible piped in music with only one song
Drove me mad while dining at Wow Fish!
Pity the people working in the shops here
The surest way to drive away your shoppers

It's been a really long time since I visited this section of downtown Singapore. As I was early for a lunch appointment at nearby Esplanade, I took a slow stroll through the connecting mall, walking from the City Hall MRT Station to my final destination at the Esplanade. The shopfronts have changed hands since I last visited this area several years ago.

Tiong Bahru Bakery - Fort Caninning Park

Rain or sun, you will enjoy your stay here, at the foothills of a beautiful park, surrounded by trees.

FRESHLY DELICIOUS:
The concept and atmosphere unique. They offer great selections of new and classic bakery items. As well as, great hot and iced beverage options.

CLASSICALLY NEW:
I ordered new and classic delicious bakery items.

SALMON:
If you appreciate a good and fresh salmon, may I recommend you try, Smocked Salmon & Cream Cheese Croissant - S$12.

I love a good natural salmon and they offered a great choice here. It tasted fresh and the combination of ingredients was delicious and unique. Be sure to ask them to toast it for you, as they offered it for me.

CHOCOLAT DEVOTION:
Next, if you love a good Chocolat pastry, may I suggest you try, Pain Au Chocolat - S$4.70. Just as delicious as it looks.

SMOOTH MATCHA:
Finally, if you’re a lover of all things Matcha, you should try their, ALL-NEW: Matcha Basque Cheesecake - S$9. This one I’d say was exquisite and very unique.

The texture, the flavor was nothing short of delicious. With each bite it was smooth, soft and rich. Try it out and your taste buds will be on cloud nine.

SEATING:
Good seating options too, both indoor and a large patio. I stayed here for few hours and enjoyed hearing great music through their BOSE speakers. I also enjoyed listening to loud thunder and rain outside, beating against the treetops.

OVERALL:
It’s a laid back and relaxing experience with super friendly and welcoming staff. If you need any assistance to place your order, they’re here to assist with a smile. I’m looking forward returning.

This branch of Tiong Bahru bakery is spacious and had a lot of available seating. They had indoor and open air seats. Of course, the croissants and drinks are great! I ordered pistachio matcha & strawberry lychee rose croissant, both of which I haven't seen at TBB before. Both were really good!

Such a quaint establishment located close to Fort Canning. We had to stand in line for 20 minutes before being able to place our order, but the queue kept moving quickly and the staff were super nice and helpful when I couldn't make my mind up!

The Quign Amann was amazing and so was the mushroom and cheese croissant sandwich I had. Will definitely visit again when I'm in Singapore next.

Try going during non-peak hours so that you can get your food and drink faster and also relax a bit inside the cafe. Pets are allowed in their outdoor area.

An excellent dinner option with a great view. Our server Audrey was very polite and gave information about the dishes. The rest of the staff were professional, quick to attend to our needs, and very helpful when we wanted to transfer tables to the outdoor terrace for dessert. As it was our birthday month, our dessert came with a lit candle and a song from the staff. A free printed photo in a frame was our takeaway memento of excellent service.

The set for two was definitely worth it with great portion sizes. Starters were unique, very well prepared and plated. I would have been very happy to have the starters as a meal by itself. The pasta was well done. Flavors clean and the ingredients top tier. Ordered the extra Wagyu beef which came with a very healthy portion. A bit on the salty side, but the wine just paired perfectly.

Atmosphere wise was very cosy, lightly lit, but with a more modern choice of background music. A little bit on the louder side, but we had no issue speaking.

Would love to visit for their lunch set.

Came here to celebrate our anniversary dinner and we loved it so much.

Firstly, the service is amazing. All the staff are so friendly, helpful and proactive!! Shoutout to Alvin and Audrey who took impeccable care of us the whole time ❤️ we’ve been to many restaurants but they were the most attentive staff we’ve ever had! Thank you for making our anniversary dinner so special!

Secondly, the food is yums and affordable, perfect for a date night out. Highlights were the seafood and the tiramisu for me. We had the couple set but would like to try Ala carte next time.

Lastly, the view was amazing??? I never knew how pretty the SG skyline was until now 😅

Overall a 10/10 experience for service, food and ambience!

Celebrated valentines day here and had an amazing time. The valentines menu was well designed and the portions were very generous. The wine pairing was great and well presented by the sommelier.

The experience was further elevated by service with a personal touch. we were very well taken care of by Gilbert, Audrey, Johnathan and Melvin. They were genuine, warm, and friendly, going out of their way to make our experience a memorable and 6-star one. We are definitely coming back! Great job to the team (:

Our 7-Year Journey: The Good & The Bad at KKH

After 7 years and 3 miscarriages, we finally welcomed our miracle. Our journey had incredible highs and some difficult lows.

The Heroes: Expertise & Care
Dr. Liu Shu Ling (IVF): After years of "normal" results but no baby, Dr. Liu’s logical, step-by-step approach was a game-changer. She was patient with my wife’s past trauma and guided us through a successful IVF PGT-A journey. She is a true expert in recurrent miscarriage.

Dr. Angelina Chua (Delivery): Recommended by Dr. Liu, she was amazing. The C-section was smooth, the stitches were incredibly neat, and the anesthesia team managed the pain perfectly.

The Challenges: Areas for Improvement
Ward 82 Recovery: Following a C-section under Full GA, my wife needed rest. However, we felt pressured and judged by staff regarding breastfeeding and formula use. More empathy is needed for mothers in heavy post-op recovery.

Physiotherapy: We felt pushed into unnecessary treatments for "suspected" Torticollis. The approach felt forceful rather than supportive.

Jaundice Management: We were discharged despite a rising jaundice trend, only to "bounce back" to the NNJ ward a day later. KKH should recalibrate this—starting phototherapy earlier for "high-normal" cases would save exhausted parents from the stress of readmission.

Final Word,
The NNJ Ward staff were a silver lining—comforting and straightforward during a tiring time. Ultimately, we give all the credit to Dr. Liu and Dr. Angelina for finally make our dream come true and we can bringing our baby home in January.

Thank you, KKH, for the medical expertise that made us a family.

I underwent an emergency cesarean section at KKH. The surgery went smoothly. Supported by the gentle comfort and professional skills of the medical staff, I safely gave birth to my baby daughter. I was admitted to the intensive care ward that night, where staff took meticulous care of my postpartum discharge. After moving to the general ward, most medical workers were warm and thoughtful. They helped feed and burp the baby, and patiently taught me breast massage methods to stimulate lactation. I soon mastered basic care skills. Most members of the medical team are professional, patient and kind, for which I am truly thankful.

Nevertheless, a female medical staff member wearing glasses behaved harshly and coldly. Her actions repeatedly upset me, leaving me filled with guilt toward my baby afterwards.

My husband tried feeding the baby for the first time. As new parents, he feared the baby might choke and nervously turned to medical staff for advice. Unexpectedly, she raised her voice and spoke in an impatient, blaming tone, repeatedly questioning whether we knew how to feed the baby and saying they would take charge instead. Without giving us a chance to explain, she took the baby straight to the nursery without a single word of explanation, and did not send the baby back for a long while. Much later, another staff member returned the baby. Seeing my husband looking flustered, I suppressed my discomfort and comforted him to relax.

Later during a routine check-up, the newborn suddenly burst into tears. Newborns cry mostly out of hunger or physical discomfort, so I planned to soothe her first before cooperating with the check. She stopped me abruptly, telling me not to hold the baby in case it developed bad habits. I could not bear to ignore the fragile crying infant. I told her I once thought the same way before becoming a mother, yet all I wanted was to calm my uneasy baby.

I comforted the baby and laid her back gently in the trolley. Yet she completely ignored my will and asked her colleague to push the baby to the nursery without my permission. The nursery was constantly filled with crying sounds. My baby had stayed there alone overnight due to my poor health condition. Though reluctant, I assumed it was only a temporary placement and the baby would come back right after the check, so I did not stop her immediately.

What disappointed me deeply was that she left right after the examination. I waited alone anxiously and felt wronged. It was not until a kind medical worker asked if I wanted my baby back that tears welled up in my eyes. I nodded quickly, and my baby finally returned to my side.

I cannot remember her name, staff ID or clear appearance, but her rude and unfeeling manner is deeply engraved in my mind. Every time I recall this experience, I blame myself bitterly for failing to protect my baby firmly and letting her be taken away. Even though she may have rich work experience, her lack of empathy and tough attitude are unacceptable.

I still trust the medical services of KKH and sincerely appreciate all the caring medical staff. Night-shift workers comforted me constantly and shared happiness when my blood pressure returned stable.

I hope I will never encounter such distressing incidents when giving birth to my second child. I wish all expectant mothers here could be treated gently. I remind myself and all mothers to follow inner feelings. Speak up bravely whenever feeling uncomfortable, and always protect ourselves and our lovely babies.

Time has passed since these incidents. My baby was born prematurely but grows healthy and well now. Whenever I gaze at her pure and cute face, those unpleasant memories haunt me and bring back my remorse. I share my personal experience with other parents staying at KKH, and I believe relevant medical workers will also see these words. I have never filed any complaint about what happened. I only hope every mother and infant can receive considerate and humane care during their hospital stay.

KKH service has been extremely disappointing.

Admission staff, the level of empathy and basic courtesy has been lacking. As parents, we are already physically and emotionally exhausted caring for a sick child. We are not asking to be treated like royalty — we are simply asking to be treated with kindness, patience and respect.

Instead, when we try to explain our situation or ask for help, we are often cut off mid-sentence or spoken to in a dismissive manner. This only adds more stress and frustration to parents who are already going through a very difficult time.

Healthcare is not just about medical treatment. Compassion, empathy and communication are just as important when dealing with patients and their families.

It is deeply disappointing that when feedback is raised, the response often feels like the institution is quick to defend staff rather than acknowledge the experience of patients and their families.

Perhaps it is time for all frontline staff — especially those at admissions — to undergo proper service training or Certified Service Professional courses to improve how they interact with parents and patients. A little empathy, patience and understanding can make a huge difference.

Parents who come to the hospital are already worried and overwhelmed. The least we hope for is to be treated with respect, not dismissal.

Very disappointed with the experience.

Mount Faber Peak, is a popular hilltop destination in Singapore. It is located at 109 Mount Faber Road, Singapore 099203.

Mount Faber, formerly Telok Blangah Hill, is a hill about 308 ft in height, located in the town of Bukit Merah in the Central Region of Singapore.

This placec overlooks the Telok Blangah area and the western parts of the Central Area of Singapore. The summit is accessible by Mount Faber Road or by Mount Faber Loop via Morse Road, but there are many footpaths or trails leading up the hill, like  Marang Trail, which leads from Marang Road at the Harbour Front MRT station (Exit D), and the Southern Ridges Park Connector, which connects from Telok Blangah Hill Park, Kent Ridge Park, and Henderson Waves.

It is a major tourist attraction, as it provides a panoramic view of Singapore's Downtown Core.
It's slope includes a tower that is part of the Singapore cable car system that connects to the Harbour Front and Sentosa. It is accessible from the HarbourFront MRT station.
