단골집이에요. 노미호다이 최고!!

We were super impressed by the quality of the food. Oysters were plump & super fresh and tastes just nice; the grilled prawns were huge and on a special promotion now at $5/stick (was $11) sweet and grilled just right; the stew was good but the price was a tad high at $43. Special mention to Winnie for attending to us patiently and suggested we try their yakitori next (their speciality)!

Really good Izakaya with a good selection of beer and sake food. Especially the Ankimo and Shirako were every well executed. Asides draft beer on tap, the Sake selection is great with many different selection at very reasonable prices. My only gripe is during dinner time, they do get crowded with family diners instead of drinkers. Hence you get the usual kids' noises rather than salary men rants 😆

Great experience at this clinic! Ms Tina explained my health issues clearly and in detail, which really reassured me. Ms Samantha at the counter is always so friendly, greeting everyone with a big smile and patiently attending to all patients even when it’s very busy. Also thankful to the pelvic scan staff for being so gentle and patient. Really appreciate the caring team! Please keep it up🙌

Great service, everything was great from the time we entered till we left. Christine assisted us with everything we need. Staffs were also friendly. Cleanliness was great. Nana who helped me with the ECG test was really professional make sure all checks were done and assured me on my safety before we proceeded with the test. Highly recommended if you need a health check up. 👍

I had a disappointing experience with this clinic regarding their health screening service. If the grade can be lower than zero star, I definitely agreed.

While my own report was ready earlier, my wife has been waiting for more than 2 weeks and still has not received her health screening report. We have tried following up multiple times via WhatsApp, but the responses have been slow, unclear, or sometimes not received at all. It feels like our messages are just being ignored.

We have never experienced such a long delay with other clinics before. What is more frustrating is the lack of proper communication and transparency. Even when looking at Google reviews, the clinic often replies asking patients to contact them directly, but based on our experience, this does not seem to lead to any real follow-up or resolution.

In addition, the overall process feels very manual and outdated. There seems to be a lack of proper system or automation to track and update patients on their report status, which may be contributing to the delays and poor communication.

Health reports are important, and patients should not have to keep chasing for updates. We hope the clinic can improve their turnaround time, communication, and consider adopting better systems to manage patient reports more efficiently.

Nurse Lu Yen Ling did the procedure for my health screening. Very patient and reassuring, explained the process clearly and addressed my queries. Excellent service made my day. But there was only 1 staff at ground floor helping those who were unable to self-register, resulting in queue. I was there before 10am.

We had a very pleasant experience with Dr Marcus Tan. Although our consultation was mainly for an eye concern, He was very attentive and also noticed my child’s blocked nose during the visit.

We really appreciate how thorough and caring the doctor was, taking the time to look beyond the main issue and advise us accordingly. It made us feel very reassured and well taken care of.

Thank you, Dr Marcus, for your patience, professionalism, and genuine care.

Managed to book a 10:40am appointment here through HealthHub. Arrived and the kiosk was easy to use. Went up to lvl 3 for BP and eventually rebooked me to lvl 2 :) shorter waiting time I supposed. Dr Jonathan was super professional from room 27, I feel like he addressed all my concerns and make me feel better in general, despite unable to further his assessment but assisted me in referrals to specialists. I’m very happy with my polyclinic visit today.
Large and beautiful covered shopping center. There is an abundance of shops, restaurants, coffee shops, and much more. There is also an attraction that mimics Venice a bit.

​This station is clearly destined to be an important transit hub, even if it feels a little disjointed at the moment. Given the many establishments pipelined for the area, it sets a robust foundation for Singapore’s connectivity. It’s a great example of forward-thinking urban planning that will truly shine in the years to come.

Marina Bay in Singapore is a stunning example of modern urban planning and architectural brilliance. Located at the heart of Singapore's downtown, it is a vibrant hub that perfectly encapsulates the city-state's blend of innovation, luxury, and cultural diversity.

One of the most iconic features of Marina Bay is the Marina Bay Sands, a massive integrated resort that dominates the skyline with its three towering structures connected by a unique rooftop SkyPark. The SkyPark offers breathtaking panoramic views of the city, especially at sunset when the skyline is bathed in a golden glow. The infinity pool at the top is also a must-visit, offering a surreal experience of swimming with the city at your feet.

The area around Marina Bay is equally impressive. The Marina Bay Promenade is a beautifully designed waterfront walk that provides scenic views of the bay and is a perfect spot for an evening stroll. The Merlion Park, featuring Singapore's iconic Merlion statue, is another highlight, drawing tourists and locals alike for photo opportunities and to enjoy the atmosphere.

For those interested in culture and the arts, the ArtScience Museum, with its lotus-inspired design, offers a range of exhibitions that blend art, science, and technology. The Marina Bay Sands itself houses numerous high-end shops, restaurants, and a world-class casino, catering to every kind of luxury experience.

The Gardens by the Bay, located just a short walk away, is a futuristic garden space with towering Supertree structures that light up beautifully at night. The Cloud Forest and Flower Dome within the gardens are also spectacular, offering a unique blend of nature and technology.

Transportation in and around Marina Bay is seamless, with excellent connectivity via the MRT and buses. The area is also pedestrian-friendly, making it easy to explore on foot.

Overall, Marina Bay is a must-visit destination in Singapore, offering a mix of luxury, culture, and breathtaking views that make it one of the most memorable places in the city. Whether you're there for shopping, dining, sightseeing, or just soaking in the vibrant atmosphere, Marina Bay has something for everyone.

One of those bars where the cocktail menu genuinely surprises. Inventive drinks without being gimmicky, a beautiful space, and staff who are warm and clearly know their craft. The menu has real innovation to it — enough to bring you back. Two small notes: the music can be a touch loud, and Fridays get busy. Neither is a dealbreaker. Confident recommendation.

Had a wonderful experience here! Went by without a reservation, they squeezes us in at the standing spaces and were moved over to the bar afterwards.
Soooo many good drinks to choose from, we went for the Nighthawks (below) and the Dependable Expandable. Both very delicious! Would definitely come back again!

Night Hawk is a proper bar with creative drinks that caters to the more adventurous in terms of cocktail palatte.

The place is exudes a classic American diner vibe with Art Deco thrown into the mix which is very much in-line and well thought out with the artwork that inspires the place; Nighthawks by Edward Hopper.

If you know your classic cocktails, you can order them as well even though its not listed on the menu so just give them a go as well, don't be shy. I loved the Rusty Nail I got.

Overall a wonderful experience, but do prepare for a bit of a wait as reservations are not possible and best to call 15 mins ahead to check if the place has place for you and your date :)

Cheers!

Efficient system, but the doctor I saw today also efficient like robot and nothing more. She's like in a hurry to give me the main findings and recommendations and that's it. Hardly any advice. Questions were simple one-liners and I was quickly dispatached. I get it. Lots of patients are waiting outside. I'll get more comprehensive answers from AI after it has read my scanned report. Overall, not good.

I’m not surprised that the National Heart Centre is a world-class facility. The environment is modern, clean, and uncrowded, with spacious interiors and clear, prominently displayed signage that makes navigation easy.

Reception and medical staff are prompt and professional in both service and response. While waiting for test results, there are plenty of options for a quick meal or coffee at Level 2.
There is also 20 mins interval shuttle bus service to Outram MRT.

The presence of subtle art displays in various corners adds a nice touch to the atmosphere. Overall, it's a fantastic healthcare facility that Singaporeans can truly be proud of.

I would like to especially shout out to Ms Shi Hui and Genevieve Wong from Medical Social SVcs Dept Rm 6B who I had passed along on 22May26 when I was visiting to make payment arrangements for my sister who is a patient.
It was Friday and prayer time and was looking out for a spot to say my prayers. There is no prayer room per se for the Muslims and as I can't sit on the floor for my prayers I could not settle to pray in the stairwelll where most muslims go off to pray for that short 15-20 mins.
When I approached them, they were kind enough to not only allow me to use one of the meeting rooms but also requested another colleague to put a 'Do not disturb' sign. This whole gesture meant alot and would like to say a very big 'Thank You'.
I'm thinking if they were so sensitive  in this instance, then their care for patients would be 'many folds over'. KUDOS!!!

It has been a while since I last visited a cinema. Seats r wider with a lot of legroom. Not crowded so it's comfy.

-1* as ticket is pricey. $16 for a ticket on Sun is shocking.

Had a pleasant time watching a movie. Not too overcrowded; all was in order. Downside was the theatre only opens 5min before showtime; it used to be 10-15min prior.

Good seats; arm rests could be lifted up. Clean.

They should make movies a bit more affordable. $100 for a family of 4 with snacks for a weekend is not something everyone can afford.

Modern and sleek movie theater, purchasing tickets was a smooth and easy process and the staff were relatively friendly. Aside from that, the seats are quite large and have plenty of leg room. One thing to note is that the theaters are extremely chilly, it is suggested to bring a jacket if you aren't good with the cold. Overall it's a pretty good movie theater and I would go again, rates are also not bad especially with discounts.

At Singapore General Hospital. The area appears to be well-signed with information in multiple languages. The presence of a registration counter suggests a structured process for patients. Inside, there are waiting areas and indications for different types of scans like CT and MRI. However, these are just observations based on the visuals. Currently, after a week where my parents bring my brother here for his additional upcoming appointments for his return to visit to the Diagnostic Radiology department at Block 2 of Singapore General Hospital, Gastroenterology & Hepatology, with Dr. Steven Mesenas. Also, he has additional upcoming appointments that after a five-day period, which is on Monday, May 19, 2025, at SGH. The CT Enterography procedure, such as fasting for 4 hours beforehand and following a low-residue diet the day before, my brother indicated, "Signs of Crohn's disease and iron deficiency anemia." This information, along with the upcoming CT Enterography, suggests he is undergoing tests and treatment for these conditions. The test was performed on November 5, 2024. The levels > 100-200 may indicate the presence of intestinal inflammation. The managing physician should correlate the patient's clinical status with this test result and determine if further laboratory, radiological, and endoscopic tests are needed. The test was performed using Quantum Blue Calprotectin Extended Buhlmann.

Currently, since earlier over the past five days, when my parents have brought my brother here once again undergo for additional checkup, it seems my brother Raymond has had additional appointments and a CT Enterography procedure at SGH, specifically within the Gastroenterology & Hepatology department and the Diagnostic Radiology, with Dr. Steven Mesenas, Clinic M, department located in BLK 3 L1 (Yellow Zone). This day he be able to self-collecting his consultation and services medications there. In addition, the doctor has prescribed him for Ferrous Gluconate Compound Cap (180 QTY), which is used in the prevention and treatment of iron-deficiency anemia. OMEprazole 20mg Cap (91 QTY) is used to treat certain conditions where there is too much acid in the stomach after done seeing his latest Gastroenterology & Hepatology test result.

The final tax invoice indicates that the CT Enterography procedure costs $1,974.75, which was covered by the MINDEF CMPB (PRE-ENLISTEE) scheme.

My appointment scheduled at 3:15pm but until 4pm not yet my turn to see doctor.when I came early around 2pm to register and nobody informed me it will be delayed until so late , things should be arranged earlier, if not why give patients appointment hour , my appointment became meaningless because of your fault. Very bad experience.

Next January would be a year I first stepped into SGH on our 15 years of stay in Singapore, all this while we have heard about this biggest hospital in Singapore with worldwide fame, okay the Urology department's public toilet needs a little renovation. Jokes apart, our destination was the Urology department, I was the patient who is a fear monger to the power of infinity, joke was least on my mind! Then I met my prescribed doctor, in fact his assistant or junior, whatever. I was in dilemma not knowing the system, the name says doctor is male, I am talking to a female. I saw one gentleman continuously moving to & fro from one room to the adjoining, I asked if he is Dr.Henry Ho, he finally was kind enough to look at the screen and speak to me. He didn't rebuke me for being suspicious about his doctor title, but his broad smile & comforting words eased me in such a manner that those few words spoken & his gestures would forever remain etched in my heart & memory! I met him one more time thereafter, the scheduled third meet did not happen, he redirected me to his junior colleague! May be he was busy with serious patients given I wasn’t diagnosed with anything serious! But I firmly believe he is not only excellent in his job but knows the way to a patient's heart, how to ease scared patients in discomfort! Definitely a medical college may not teach this in details, it comes from within! I believe he has as beautiful a heart as seen through a patient’s eyes in that brief encounter, besides the varied degrees & chairs he holds. I wholehearted recommend Dr.Henry Ho for your related issues! I wish him health, happiness, success throughout his life! By the way, SGH houses excellent food arenas at subsidised prices, you may try!

I recently attended the Nanyang Institute of Management in Singapore, and I couldn't be happier with my experience! The faculty is incredibly knowledgeable and supportive, always willing to go the extra mile to help students succeed.

The curriculum is well-structured, blending theory with practical applications, which has really enhanced my understanding of the subject matter. The facilities are modern and well-maintained, providing a conducive environment for learning.

Additionally, the institute offers a great sense of community, with plenty of opportunities for networking and collaboration. I've made lasting connections with both peers and professors.

Overall, I highly recommend the Nanyang Institute of Management to anyone looking to further their education in a vibrant and dynamic setting. It’s truly an institution that prioritizes student success!

Nanyang Institute of Management is one of the PEI that I know of that creates plenty of events for students, creating a home atmosphere for them. Would really recommend it for students who are looking for something different!
Good environment learning for Vietnamese students. Helpful and friendly teachers as well as good supporting services. One of good schools for foreign students to study in Singapore.

This restaurant is best known for its briyani, the true signature dish of the house. The rice was soft, light, and fragrant, while the meat, well-marinated, delivered rich and balanced flavors. The accompanying sauce was also well executed, although it felt slightly too salty for my taste.

The service stands out for its speed and the friendliness of the staff, making the overall welcome pleasant. However, the cleanliness of the dining area in the street food center leaves room for improvement, and additional staff dedicated to cleaning would probably be beneficial.

In the end, despite the quality of the briyani, the overall experience did not fully live up to expectations.

Excellent mutton biryani. The mutton is well cook, tender and soft. The biryani rice is fluffy and flavourful. Is too much for me despite asking for less portion. The curry is not too spicy. My kid like it too. For $7 including a hard boiled egg, this is very value for money mutton biryani. Highly recommend for those who prefer less spicy biryani.

Actually this is my first time eat at this place. What i can say its above my expectation , it was good , flavourful, big portion, the vege also fresh and crunchy. Chicken tender. Rice is aromatic and flavourful, dhal curry also thick and great combination with the rice overall 4.5/5
Only the place is very crowded during peak hours. And hard to find empty tables, if u alone is ok, if u with family not recommended. So many people and also hard for you to passing thru because of so many people. Overall good and other shops also have a lot of makan things

Great hotel! I was able to ask inquiries about the room (to ensure I got a window) & book over email, which I greatly appreciated! Check in was smooth & easy, and the room was great! - exactly what I needed for a solo week stay in Singapore. The location was amazing - very safe at night, and close to Outram Park MRT stop. Despite being surrounded by bars, it was extremely quiet. Having free laundry on site was a huge plus. Attendants were very helpful, and the complimentary beverages were a nice touch.

Solid boutique hotel with a clean, modern, well-designed interior. Definitely on the smaller side (at least for their lower priced rooms). I was solo traveling and had enough space. But if I had been traveling with my partner, their double room would not have been large enough for multiple suitcases without having to put them right in the middle of the floor/tripping hazard.

But the room was very clean, aesthetically pleasing, comfortable bed, and nice shower with good pressure. A good place to come back, relax, and sleep after a day exploring the city. The hotel is right across from a bar, so there is some of that noise (I advise earplugs if you’re a light sleeper) or ask to stay in the interior side of the hotel. The higher rooms are their more expensive rooms, too, which could potentially cut down on the noise.

The location is AMAZING! 10/10 on location. Right in the heart of Chinatown with quick walks to two great hawker stall centers: Chinatown Complex and Maxwell Center, with both the Chinatown MRT and Maxwell MRT very close to walk to (use Singapore’s MRT system – it’s great: inexpensive, convenient, takes you all over the city).

Would give this hotel a 4.5 if I could. It is reasonably priced compared to a lot of other options in Singapore and feels newer and very well-maintained.

I had a really pleasant stay at this boutique hotel. The space is super clean, well-maintained, and has a beautiful minimalist design that makes it feel calm and cozy. You can tell that a lot of thought has been put into keeping everything neat and aesthetically pleasing. The overall atmosphere is relaxing and perfect if you’re looking for a simple yet comfortable place to stay.

The only minor downside is that the toilet is quite small, which might feel a bit tight for some guests. Aside from that, everything else was great. Overall, I’d still highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a well-kept boutique hotel with a nice, modern vibe.

Really good coffee. They have 2 types of beans, one more classic, one funkier. It was perfect for us. The quality of the coffee was really high, we tried both warm and iced and it was very well balanced. We didn't get a chance to try it again because we were only shortly in Singapore, but I would have tried it again.

Staff is very friendly and helpful.

Seriously good coffee! Best one I’ve ever had in Singapore. Highly recommended, my honest review 👍
Meticulously made from roasting, brewing, and choosing the quality  coffee bean.
I’m a coffee lover, and been trying coffees around  the world including in Sydney, Melbourne.

We visited as a party of two and ordered an espresso, which was very well balanced with a nice body.

The staff was very friendly and attentive, which we appreciated.

Since the café is located inside a mall, it was quite loud and didn’t really feel like a place to slow down and enjoy a calm coffee.

The tables were a bit run down, which took away slightly from the overall experience.

We didn’t try any food or pastries and didn’t check for Wi-Fi or power outlets.

A/prof Gavin Tan is an exceptionally good and thorough doctor. My friend got his choroidal melanoma surgery done under his supervision and the treatment was done very well indeed. The staff, nurses, esp Rachel at the pre-surgery centre, Level 1, lobby B was extremely warm, professional and very very kind. She kept me calm while I waited for the surgery to finish and offered me tea and coffee throughout the whole time. I highly recommend this eye centre as it has the very best opthalmologists and care staff.

Uncoordinated between ATU, registration and screening. Our appointment is at 12pm, but postponed to 4pm because of all the delays in the systems and ops. The building is nice but service is inconsistent. Filipino staff at counter in ATU suite B is very blur.

I visited NCCS Oncologic Imaging on 19 Mar 145pm for a MRI scan and suddenly had a fainting spell right before my scan. Luckily 3-4 nurses came to my rescue and immediately lifted me to rest on one of the available beds. They kept checking in on me and made sure I was ok. Doctor Tang who checked in with me pre scan was also v nice and reassuring. I didn't have a chance to properly thank them in person so would like to shout out my appreciation here. Thank you so much for your kindness and care. Everybody at the hospital was very patient and friendly too

My first ever time visiting OCH, both times this month. It was a very good experience, probably my best experience at any community hospital so far as a visitor. The beds are spaced apart well so patients do not feel too constrained. The visiting hours are fantastic, accommodating a wide range 8am to 10pm. Pre-registration makes it seamless for easy entry and exit. Staff especially the nurses but also the ground level staff are all so professional, patient, and family. Thank you for making a positive difference 🙏🏻

My family would like to express our sincere gratitude to the team at Outram Community Hospital for the excellent care provided to my mother during her three-weeks stay.

From admission to discharge, the doctors, nurses, therapists, and support staff demonstrated professionalism, compassion, and patience. The medical team took the time to explain her condition and recovery plan clearly, giving our family confidence and peace of mind throughout the rehabilitation process.

The ward was clean, comfortable, and well-maintained, creating a positive environment for recovery. Most importantly, my mother felt respected, safe, and well taken care of during her stay.

Highly recommended.

I visited a loved one at Outram Community Hospital and was very impressed by the overall environment and care provided. The hospital is clean, modern, and thoughtfully designed, creating a calm and welcoming space for both patients and visitors. Carpark is also well organized with sufficient parking lots.

What stood out most was the professionalism and warmth of the staff — from nurses to therapists to admin personnel. Everyone was patient, respectful, and genuinely caring in how they interacted with the patients. It gave me a lot of reassurance seeing my loved one so well looked after.

Facilities were well-maintained given its newly opened as well and visiting hours were managed smoothly. There are also great amenities - Koufu food court, POSB ATM, AXS machine, starbucks, Koi, and a pharmacy. Pretty decent for a community hospital.

A great example of community healthcare done right unlike some others i have visited. Thank you to the team at Outram Community Hospital for your dedication and compassion.

What a market! Clothing, food, drinks, souvenirs, toys, electricals, shoes & much much more. Stalls are right next to each other & there must have been over 500! We also bought some fresh jackfruit from a stall at the rear of the market & they cut the fruit & packaged it whilst you were ordering . Fantastic.

Bugis Market @ Bugis Street is a vibrant and bustling spot packed with a huge selection of shops.
It’s very popular with both tourists and locals.
You’ll find fruit stalls, souvenirs, street food, mobile phone services, chocolates, sweets, T-shirts, trinkets, beauty services, bags, pharmacy and plenty more.
It’s always busy and crowded, but over the years, the place feels cleaner and less stuffy, with better air circulation now.
Worth a visit to browse around and soak in the lively atmosphere.

A vibrant and lively shopping destination in the heart of Singapore. Bugis Market offers a wide variety of affordable clothing, accessories, souvenirs, snacks, and local products. It is a great place to explore, shop, and experience the bustling atmosphere of Singapore.
The market is well connected by public transport, and there are plenty of food options nearby. A must-visit destination for both tourists and locals looking for good bargains and a unique shopping experience.
Highly recommended!
Love this place! Warm welcome and good vibe. Easy to go anywhere in downtown. I can took a pictures around here.
Great for a mooch about on a rainy day
Nice square for relaxing, sitting during the hot day ❤️

Through my personal taste this one of the top fishball noodle in Singapore.  Fishball quality are old generation like me in the 60’s who appreciate what is the traditional good fishball tastes like.  Always long Q but worth it. Chilli sauce and they’re also their highlights. Very 古早味。Highly recommended.

Went over to check out Albert Centre behind our hotel. The queue for this stall was long so I had to try it.

Noodles are springy and Fishball are quite nice. Overall a good meal.

Friendly ladyboss.

Always wanted to try as it’s closed by noon. Was in luck when after 12pm and there was no queue, gestured to the aunty whether there was still any available and decided to place my order. Kway teow with chilli and vinegar, ala the old school type and the fish balls 8 of them to be exact, in odd shaped reflecting they were handmade had great texture and possessed that bounce.

Pocket Rocket is a splendid reminder that true hospitality has very little to do with extravagance and everything to do with the people behind the bar.

The venue embraces its dive bar identity with confidence—unpretentious, full of character, and effortlessly welcoming. It strikes a rare balance between relaxed charm and genuine warmth, making it somewhere you find yourself returning to without hesitation.

A particular mention must go to Ganesh, whose hospitality is nothing short of exemplary. Attentive without ever being intrusive, personable without feeling rehearsed, he has a remarkable ability to make every guest feel genuinely welcome. It is, quite simply, hospitality at its finest.

If you’re after polished cocktails, authentic conversation and an atmosphere that values substance over spectacle, Pocket Rocket is well worth a visit. A proper hidden gem. Highly recommended.

One of my favorite neighborhood spots in Singapore.

Pocket Rocket is about as casual as it gets—in the best possible way.  Nestled among the shophouses on Keong Saik Road, it’s the kind of place that’s perfect for bringing out-of-town guests for a taste of local flavor, or winding down after a long day in the CBD.

The team genuinely cares about the people who walk through the door, remembers your name, plays great music (with the occasional nostalgic 2000s emo/punk throwback 🎸), and creates the kind of atmosphere where it’s just as comfortable to come with friends as it is to rock up solo and strike up a conversation.

Don’t come expecting luxury or pristine amenities — that’s not the point.  Come for a cold beer, good company, and a team that works hard to make everyone feel welcome.

A rare gem.

When I came in, I was greeted with such friendly service from staffs Issak Chua, Kenny, Levi, Ganesh, and Prasanth. The drinks were exceptional and the bar Captain Issak explained every ingredient that was used to craft my cocktail - Gin and Tonic. Definitely a place to try!

Stopped by here for a late lunch. I had the Kopi O Kosong and Mee Siam. The place was relatively quiet when I went, which was nice for a relaxed meal. The staff was genuinely friendly, and the lady boss even came by to ask how the food was – you can really tell they're putting in the effort to get things right as a new shop. The Kopi O Kosong was robust and flavourful, exactly how a good Kopi O Kosong should be, and the Mee Siam had that perfect balance of tartness and sweetness without being too heavy.

If I had to nitpick, a few minor things could be polished, which is expected for any new place, but the attention to detail and their food recommendations really shone through. It's clear they care about what they serve. If you're in the area (Icon Village / Altez), I'd say give them a shot – new spots need support, and the team here is genuinely trying their best. I'll definitely be back soon. Worth a visit for sure!
Cozy Coffee Place. Newly opened this month! Clean and comfortable. Nice ambience. Friendly staff. Good food. Reasonable price.

We love coming to the Coffee Hive here after my daughter’s enrichment lessons. They are open on Saturday and even Sunday which we really appreciated it as we can have our breakfast here with our cat and our girl. They are both pet friendly and child friendly which is really a rare find in Tanjong Pagar area. The price of the food and drinks are also really affordable. One of our favourite food is the Ipoh Hor Fan!

If you are a World Cup fan, you can even catch World Cup while having your breakfast here!

I am not sure why people keep raving about this stall.

I tried the goat intestines recently but the masala doesn't seem to have seeped into the meat, it was almost tasteless.

Not worth the price, maybe their other non veg dishes fare better

For the price of the goat intestines + rice, I can get an entire non veg biryani elsewhere.

😊 Bringing your work colleagues and friends to Zham Zham Muslim Food sounds like a great idea! They'll probably love the food just as much as you did. The friendly service will definitely make the experience even better. Can't wait to hear what they think!

While most stalls are closed in the food centre and wet market - this stall is where you can find nasi Padang!! Possibly once Zam Zam and today is ZHAM ZHAM MUSLIM FOOD. For nose to tail lovers , enjoy the mutton innards and liver here - I would just take away the dishes, very delicious and tender. You can call in to pre-order, phone number updated or check out the photo 👇🏻

💋 “Where cocktails flirt with class — and every sip tells her story.”

Step into Madame, the sultry new cocktail lounge along 69 Tras Street, where Parisian boudoir elegance meets modern Tanjong Pagar charm. 🌹✨

It’s not just a bar — it’s an experience. From dimly lit interiors and jazz-kissed ambiance to signature cocktails inspired by iconic women like “Marilyn” (high-proof bourbon with maple foam) and “Grace” (Jamaican rum with dashi) — every drink feels like a whisper of indulgence. 🍸

Pair your drink with Mediterranean-inspired small plates that impress:
🥗 Burrata & Tomato — silky, tangy, with kaffir lime oil and longan that awaken the senses.
🐟 Tuna Salad — cured tuna with kaffir lime dressing and pickled papaya; refreshing, addictive, and oh-so-balanced.
🍗 Hua Diao Brine Poulet — tender chicken with carrot purée that melts in your mouth.
🥩 Beef Bourguignon — slow-cooked perfection with leek purée — rich, comforting, and sophisticated.
🍰 Burnt Cheesecake with Dark Rum — boozy, bold, and unforgettable (a must-try!).

Whether it’s an intimate date night, a catch-up over cocktails, or a chic evening out with friends, Madame knows how to charm. 🖤

📍 Madame, 69 Tras Street, Singapore
🕰 Perfect for evenings filled with laughter, flavor, and a touch of French mystery.

Ready to sip, savour, and be seduced by Madame?
Book your table or drop by for a night of Parisian indulgence — because every woman (and man) deserves a little magic. 💃

Had such a lovely time at this bar in Singapore. The food was really good, well-flavoured and nicely presented and the service was warm, and friendly made the whole experience even better. The mocktails and cocktails were a standout: not just delicious but also beautifully crafted, making them perfect for both sipping and photos. Overall, a great spot for good vibes, good drinks, and a relaxed night out. Definitely worth a visit! 🍸✨

Had such a lovely dining experience here! Every dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented.

The Beef Tartare was one of my favourites, hand-chopped and perfectly seasoned with pickled shallots and mustard, paired with crisp toasted brioche for the perfect bite. The K.P.T Cocktail was a fun starter, crispy tart shells filled with creamy prawn cocktail salad, light yet flavourful.

For mains, the Hua Diao Brine Poulet really surprised me! The poached chicken was unbelievably tender and juicy, complemented by a smooth carrot purée that tied everything together. The Flame-Grilled Scallops were plump and smoky, each bite bursting with natural sweetness.

Desserts were a perfect ending, the Burnt Cheesecake with a hint of dark rum was rich and indulgent, while the Bread Pudding felt warm, homey, and comforting.

Their cocktails were another highlight! I especially loved Amy, a sweet and refreshing mix that instantly won me over. Grace was just as delightful, balanced and elegant.

Overall, an amazing spot for great food, drinks, and a cozy, refined atmosphere. Would definitely come back to try more!

This MRT Station is probably one of the busiest in Singapore in terms of usage and between its many exits footfall as it is right in the heart of Singapore's Chinatown - the latter, because this MRT Station connects to a number of nearby shopping malls, either via their basement levels (for example Chinatown Point) or ground entrances (again for example Chinatown Point). However, because of its heavy usage, the public toilets at this MRT Station is often not at its cleanest.

Chinatown MRT station is recognized as one of the busiest stations in Singapore and is a significant point of interest for tourists. It offers diverse dining options, from local eateries to vibrant street vendors. Visitors can easily explore nearby attractions such as Little India, Chinatown Complex, Chinatown Point, the Chinatown Street Market, and the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, all within a short distance. Positioned at the intersection of Eu Tong Sen Street, New Bridge Road, and Upper Cross Street, this station provides essential rail connections to the bustling Chinatown district, where the harmonious blend of modern architecture and distinct Chinese cultural elements creates a unique urban landscape.

Chinatown Singapore.
This is a must visit location in Singapore especially during the Chinese New Year festival.
There are many stores popped up along the streets during the this period and in the evening the whole Chinatown will be so busy with the locals doing the usual New Year shopping.
It's so colorful and foods are on every street.
The wet market at basement of Chinatown complex is one of the busiest market in Singapore.
Many Dim Sum restaurant here in chinatown.
The tooth relic temple in Chinatown is the new landmark and you will never miss the temple when you are in Chinatown.

A tranquil MRT station with little people, I passed by here to take a bus. There are a few exits, so do know which one you are exiting from to prevent any unnecessary U-turns or walking more than needed.

Station is immaculate as always, and it is very spacious, which can accommodate a large crowd when walking across the various underground paths. Overall, a tranquil environment and a nice MRT station.

If you wanted to visit Gardens by the Bay, Marina Bay Sands, ArtScience Museum and the Helix Bridge, this is NOT the MRT station to go. Instead, Bayfront MRT Station (CE1/DT16) should be the designated station. Don't worry, luckily this is an interchange station and Bayfront Station is just 1 station away. You just need to head to the Circle Line (CCL), going towards CE1 direction.

This is a huge interchange station, from one line to another takes a few minutes walk. I like that the station is spacious, clean and less crowded, but the elevator speed is really fast, you really need to pay attention when getting onto the elevator.

Marina Bay MRT station is an underground Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) interchange station on the North South (NSL), Circle (CCL) and Thomson–East Coast (TEL) lines in Singapore. Located in the Downtown Core district near Marina Bay, the station serves the Marina One Residences, Marina Bay Suites and the Marina Bay Financial Centre.
It was a shopping mall with a very large space and a lot of people. With the lighting, the interior is very well done and there were many sale products.

Singapore Garden Festival 2022 is ON, and for this year, Civic Plaza Ngee Ann City has become one of the venues for this festival.

From 30 July to 7 August 2022, the public is welcome to visit, view, and enjoy the showcase of several garden festivals for free.

All the garden displays are so beautiful, and it is hard to pick the best or favorite because each display has its angle and style.

It's a surprise to see this festival create a mini pond display with lotus flowers, different types of beautiful orchids, picnic garden inspiration, and a hanging bird nest.
The worst information staff ever, i stand infront of her, not even saying hi or what. Ignoring me, arrogant human
It's suitable for a cruise, and the mood is very relaxed and comfortable.😃
This is a very beautiful place to walk, run, ride your bike, have a picnic or just sit and enjoy yourself. There is also wildlife and tranquility.
Very busy area we visited in February it was hot in the day. Sunglasses, sunscreen and hat is a must to talk around this area. You can easily find nice breeze as long as you are covered.
So nice to see a little farms in raffles place. Decent selection of groceries, deli food and wine. Friendly staff as well, especially Yi San, good recommendations from her.
Great food here! Everyone should come and give it a try. The service is very good as well.

Have been getting my afternoon coffee here almost daily since this place opened in mid-July.

Excellent service and concoctions from Khristine and team. They constantly strive to improve and come up with new offerings, and their effort shines through. My go-to drink was their Mont Blanc, but I’ve been getting their Dirty London Fog every single time since they launched their monthly specials.

Looking forward to the future interesting creations they have in store!
I have tried the coffee at Bendemeer, Hong Lim and Tanjong Pagar, it taste great. The coffee has a smooth body and comforting flavour notes. I have also gotten a cool tshirt from their online store.

Good coffee, serve both modern menu (latte, flat white) and traditional coffee menu. I ordered Kopi C Kosong for dine in. Since it’s in hawker area, you don’t have to worry about the seats. You can seat at any vacant table or join with others guests. Put your used cup into available shelf in the corner and done.

Very crowded coffee place in Tanjong Pagar Hawker Center, run by a very friendly lady boss. I had the spanish latte which has a very strong and rich flavour while still being very smooth.

Overall would definitely come back to give their other coffees a try

My favourite kway chap! I really love, love the large intestines here - it’s so chewy and has a nice roasted taste to it too! I also like that the meat is not fatty at all~

The kway can be inconsistent - but on a good day, it will be the smoothest and softest kway that you’ve ever tried!!

Highly recommend!

Chuan Seng Kway Chap is one of those always long-queue stalls at Albert Centre Food Centre, Bugis.

Skip the standard one pax platter, go straight for a pick & mix instead.

Paid S$15.70 for a decent spread of large fatty intestines/大肠头, small powder intestines粉肠, pig stomach/猪肚, fish cake, & egg, plus a bowl of kway/flat noodles.

The offal is the highligh - clean, no gamey smell, nice chewy bite but still tender, & well soaked in that savoury, slightly herbal braised gravy.

The kway is silky smooth & breaks apart easily with a spoon, super easy to eat (my kind of texture).

Gravy looks dark but flavour is well balanced - not too salty, not too bland.

Only thing is the chili not really my type.

Little India, Singapore

Little India (Tamil: லிட்டில் இந்தியா) is an ethnic district in Singapore. It is located east of the Singapore River—across from Chinatown, located west of the river—and north of Kampong Glam. Both areas are part of the urban planning area of Rochor. Little India is commonly known as Tekka in the Indian Singaporean community.

Little India MRT station is an underground Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) interchange station on the North East (NEL) and Downtown (DTL) lines. The station is located at the junction of Bukit Timah Road and Race Course Road, and serves the ethnic neighbourhood of Little India. Several landmarks surrounding the station include KK Women's and Children's Hospital, Tekka Market, etc.

Little India is a lively and colorful neighborhood that is a fantastic place to visit. It's known for its rich Indian culture, delicious food, and unique shopping. You'll find beautiful temples like Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple, vibrant street art, and the famous 24-hour Mustafa Centre where you can buy almost anything. The air is often filled with the smells of spices and flowers from the shops. The Tekka Centre is a great spot to try authentic Indian food at a hawker centre. Little India is a fun and exciting place to explore.

5 stars for Koffee Kollective at Tanjong Pagar! Honestly one of the best little coffee finds in Singapore, a charming, cozy coffee house tucked away in the corner at #02-51, Tanjong Pagar Food Market.

What I love most is that it feels so personal and heartfelt. The founders are lovely, and you can really tell they put a lot of care into what they do. It is the kind of small local business that makes you want to come back, not just for the drinks, but also for the warm service and good vibes.

Their drink options are great too. Whether you want a classic kopi, an espresso-based coffee, an iced latte, or something more fun and creative, there is something for everyone. They also have matcha options, hojicha, Milo-style drinks, and special flavours like strawberry matcha, dirty matcha, honey oat latte, and even more indulgent choices like banana pudding matcha. Perfect for coffee lovers, matcha fans, or anyone who just wants a nice drink to brighten the day.

They also have another outlet in Bedok, so do check them out there too.

Please come support Koffee Kollective if you are around Tanjong Pagar! It is a hidden gem, run by lovely people, with solid drinks and lots of heart. Highly recommended.

personally i feel that their quality, quantity and price point is really hard to beat compared to the myriad of matcha brands around the area. plus you get to use your cdc voucher!!

when ordering, you get a choice of:
/niko neko matcha/
• yuri - entry-level artisanal matcha. described as clean and grassy with vegetal umami taste profile.
• ajisai - a more premium ceremonial-grade matcha  with subtle nuttiness and hints of bitterness.

/niko neko houjicha/
• akane - dark roast with soy milk chocolate taste profile and intense roastiness.
• tsubaki - medium roast with hazelnut nuttiness and moderate smokey roastiness.

/regular or large size/
• specialty coffee - hot is 8oz, iced is 12oz
• matcha & houjicha - regular is 12oz, large is 16oz
*info gathered from their website

they're located around a corner area, facing a traffic light below~

personally found their matcha latte rather underwhelming 😭 since they claimed to use niko neko matcha powder, i was really excited and upsized my matcha latte ($6.20 for large, $4.90 for small). i also went for the large cup bc they mentioned it comes with 7g of matcha, compared to just 4g in the small cup. sadly, the matcha ratio was pretty off and the milk was pretty much all i could taste :( would’ve loved a stronger matcha flavour, especially since i ordered it unsweetened.

that said, i might still go back to try other matcha renditions (like their strawberry/mango matcha!) or their coffee. sincerely hope that it was just a one off poor experience on my end!

ION Orchard delivers a high-end shopping experience right in the heart of Orchard Road. The architecture is striking, and the mall houses a wide range of luxury brands alongside stylish dining spots. It’s always lively and well-maintained, though it can feel overwhelming due to its size. Still, one of the most iconic retail destinations in Singapore.

It wasn't a goal on my list. I visited it only because through it you have access to ION Sky, an observation deck. What I liked is the absolutely unique architecture, very beautiful. Otherwise, it has nothing extra compared to other malls.

A huge, modern, expensive shrine to consumerism. If you have the money, and yoy need lots,  you can find anything here. We did however have the best lunch date at Twinings much to my surprise and delight. I would absolutely go there again.

Our stay at Shangri-La Singapore was overall a lovely experience, especially as a family traveling with kids. The hotel is very well set up for families, and it truly shows in the thoughtful facilities and attentive service from the staff throughout our stay.

One of the highlights was definitely the Asian breakfast buffet. The selection is generous and well-executed, with plenty of local flavors to enjoy. However, if you’re staying longer than three days, you might notice that the menu doesn’t vary much, which can make it feel a bit repetitive over time.

That said, the other restaurants within the hotel are excellent and maintain a high standard, offering good alternatives when you want a change from the buffet.

For families, Buds by Shangri-La is a fantastic play area—our kids absolutely loved it. Just keep in mind that access isn’t included in all room bookings, and you’ll need to reserve sessions in advance during your stay.

Another great feature is Splash Zone Shangri-La, which adds a lot of fun for children. However, being outdoors, it can be affected by the tropical weather, and I do wish it opened a bit earlier than 9 AM to make the most of the day.

Overall, despite a few minor points, our stay was very enjoyable. The staff were warm, helpful, and consistently supportive, which made the experience even more memorable.

Had a great stay at Shangri-La Singapore. The room was great, clean and welcoming. The view was nice. The bed is very comfortable. The hotel is situated in a great location, they have a shuttle to ION Orchard which makes everything much easier since you can take the MRT basically anywhere from ION Orchard. Beautiful hotel and location. The gym was great and the Spa as well.

A superbly clean hotel in a quiet part of the city. The complex's huge size (900+ rooms) made for quite an impersonal ambiance. The overall decor is looking a little dated although all perfectly functional.
Gym is well equipped and maintained.
A solid choice for a lively, family-oriented experience.

I visited here for a morning walk. The park is quite large, so you'll definitely work up a sweat walking around. I highly recommend bringing a water bottle. It's full of nature, and spotting a wild chicken was a fun experience.

Relaxing spot, perfect for a nature retreat while in the city. A lot less crowded than you'd expect, considering it's central spot.

It's a collection of spots really, rather than a single destination, with lifestyle dining, museums, educational spice gardens, wedding photo destinations, or just a plain picnic spot. It's much less of a climb than you'd think, is great all around.

View from the top is a comforting one, nice to see the cityscape.

One interesting thing is how it's occupied mainly by maids, foreign workers, and tourists. As an aside, Chinese tourists and their themed outfits are kinda fun! Maybe we should look into that. Under-utilized by Singaporeans - thats your tax dollars at work you know, might as well use it.

We also appreciated the condiment and sauce stations, which allowed us to customize our meals with different flavours.

One thing that puzzled us was the nasi lemak at the salad bar. It came with sambal chili, but it felt incomplete without essentials like ikan bilis. As a result, the rice didn’t pair particularly well with the other items available at the salad bar.

Overall, it was a very satisfying lunch with plenty of variety and good value. The only limitation was the 90-minute dining time, but it was still more than enough for us to enjoy the meal at a comfortable pace.

Thanks also to Ms Tan Chin Hean from customer service for the great assistance rendered to the receipt points redemption.

Cheers!

TANGS at Tang Plaza is one of the oldest surviving and longest running  department stores in Singapore, and the main Orchard Road store feels like it has been around forever. I’ve been seeing it since I was little, so there’s definitely a sense of nostalgia attached to it.

One of my favourite restaurants, Sinpopo, is located inside the department store. However, the fourth floor, which used to house places like Dancing Fish and Justin’s Gastro Café-Bar, has since been repurposed. The basement has now been transformed into a large food hall featuring the Hawker Street food court and various other restaurants and eateries.

I really hope TANGS continues to thrive, as it remains such an iconic part of Orchard Road. Since they own the freehold land the building sits on, I’m optimistic that the business will continue for decades to come.

This branch is crowded at weekends due to its locality within Orchard shopping core. Best to book tables if you really want to be sure. Service is pleasant, though somewhat harried during peak dinner times! Queues form for those without reservations.

I recently dined at PS.Cafe at Raffles City and had a pleasant overall experience. The ambience was as expected—stylish, relaxed, and perfect for a casual catch-up or a quiet meal in the city.

For mains, I ordered the king prawn aglio olio. The prawns were fresh and reasonably juicy, and the pasta was cooked al dente. The garlic and olive oil combination was fragrant, though I felt it could have had a bit more depth or spice to elevate the flavors further.

The Caesar salad was disappointing. The dressing  seemed odd, but the ingredients tasted fresh.

Dessert was the highlight of the meal—the marshmallow brownie with vanilla ice cream. The brownie was rich, warm, and gooey, paired perfectly with the cold, creamy ice cream. The toasted marshmallow added a nice sweetness and texture contrast, making it a satisfying end to the meal.

Service was attentive and efficient, though the restaurant can get quite busy during peak hours. Overall, a reliable spot for comforting Western dishes in a chic setting.

Had a wonderful dining experience at PS.Cafe Raffles City! The food was delicious with a great variety, and every dish was beautifully presented. The ambiance was warm and cozy—perfect for a relaxed meal with family and friends.

What truly stood out was the exceptional service, especially from Glaiza—friendly, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. Her thoughtful touch made the celebration feel extra special and memorable.

Highly recommended for great food, a lovely ambiance, and outstanding service at Raffles City Singapore!

13/1/26 at 11:20am - To my great surprise, I was customer #2 today🤔

As a creature of habit, Nam Nam has been my lunch venue for almost EVERY visit to Raffles City in the past 10 years. But after today, I will NOT be returning here for lunch ever again. Because prices are now higher, portions are smaller and food quality is down.

👎 no more lunch sets of a bowl of noodle with protein, side dish & drink. Now I pay more for the bowl of noodle.
👎 today my hot lotus tea is $5.50😱 which is unbelievable for a hot drink with some flavour.
👎 the soup standard has slipped throughout the years. Today’s version was weakest. It’s just a bowl of brownish liquid that looks like soup but the robust flavours of the version I loved at first slurp from years ago are gone. For good.
👎 the beef slices came clumped together and the texture was not appetising. I don’t believe the higher price was justified for a REGULAR portion that didn’t even fill me up properly. There was a serving of basil leaves and bean sprouts but these looked like visual distractions to make up for the lack of a free side dish 🙄
👍 service staff was cordial and attentive but their readiness to serve means nothing when there are only one or two diners. By 12pm, the only people who came in were a handful of tourists. Then some office workers came but the scenes of long queues and packed restaurants are no more.

Today’s lunch here cost $23 but I was still hungry and had to buy a bun from a bakery, which meant total spent was about $26.

For that amount, the next time I come to Raffles City, I will find a new lunch venue that gives me more value. Bye bye Nam Nam 👋 it’s not me, it’s you!

Been a fan of Nam Nam since its opening but I honestly haven’t had it in the last few years since the menu change and there isn’t crab noodles or seafood pork noodles anymore. Still tastes decent but I have to say it’s unlike before. Still find it tastier in the past. Pho used to be served with a small plate of herbs (mint leaves, basil, bean sprouts, chilli and lime wedge) but seems like they don’t anymore — you have to request for it and even then they don’t give you everything. There is a limit of 45mins eating time (to ease the queue), though it’s not strictly enforced but it’s quite stressful. I can’t enjoy to the fullest because I feel like I’m being watched when I’m done with my food and they want me to leave. I would say there are greater Vietnamese options out there but if you do have some cravings and Nam Nam is close by, give it a go.

NamNam at Raffles City is located at Basement 1. Always having long queues during peak hours. The value set meal was a good touch. Bánh mì was average / nothing special, the side fries were served cold. The coffee with milk was normal but in a small cup to recuperate the value meal set cost.

The cashier and staff (supposedly to usher customers to their assigned tables) were distracted. Both of them were chatting/gossiping with each other during peak hours. The cashier was loudly complaining and unhappy about customers most of the time (in front of other customers). The whole experience was bad.

Every dish we ordered was full of flavor.
The food was absolutely delicious and authentic flavors, perfectly balanced spices.
The ambiance was cozy and clean, with a relaxed vibe that made it easy to enjoy our meal.

What really made our visit special was their customer service. Kimberley was friendly, attentive, and making sure everything was perfect throughout our meal. Her welcoming attitude made us feel warm.

Highly recommended for anyone craving authentic Thai food with pleasant service. I’ll definitely be coming back!
Very flavourful food! Great service, Kimberly is friendly and warm :)

Kimberly was amazing! She greeted us with a warm smile, checked on us at just the right moments, and patiently answered our questions about the menu. Her service was efficient and thoughtful, and it truly elevated our overall dining experience.

Lighting is bad
Alcohol is super expensive
There was also cover charge per pax.
Ordered food from them which they ordered from a nearby restaurant and marked up the price.
11 of us spent $1500+, drinking only 2 bottles of glenfiddich 12 years and food like fried noodles fried rice, fried egg, veg, mala chicken, mala frog legs, tofu, potato and a seafood platter which was supposed to be $128 but they marked up too.
Saw their TikTok video but unfortunately the food dont looked like it was shown on the video.
They came in plastic containers, except for the seafood platter.
Service from staffs are great however too expensive to come again.
Unless purely for singing.
Cant adjust the dim the light. Its total off or bright. Microphone was flat like u are n emcee, we end up using the room to listen to song and chitchat. Food was so so. Not coming back ever again.

Spent 5hrs here on 17/7/24, was a good experience. Staff was polite and friendly. Beer/Stout charged at $15.90++ per bottle was expensive in my humble opinion. Sound system was good, room was clean and nice. Only 1 common toilet on level 3.

Fusion western restaurant that infuses  local flavors into standard western cruisine framework. I have had their pasta in the past, and the Cincalok steak, and have returned for the steak this time around. I consider their rendition a successful and adventurous mix, such that I would be back for theiress conventional steak, to say the least. The cincalok is an unexpectedly exciting partner to their decently done steak, sauce and all. There is no mistake for if you are after a higher tier pristine steak experience, this may not be it. For anything else, this has been on my mind for awhile, for that strong unami kick is unforgettable. It can get a little too salty though, considering the use of cincalok is a matter of dealing with an item of very high salt content in its native form. Present as well is the lemon grass chicken which is crispy and drench in the aforementioned sauce and respectably satisfies my crave for protein. The soup of the day is Spicy Sour soup and is also done properly with the appropriate amount of thickening. The execution of the dishes does well to continue my faith in this fusion menu, which has taken care and consideration for use of Asian/Singaporean flavor profile to thoughtfully pair with their western counterpart. This shine through amongst the many others which may fall short, sometimes by an appalling margin.

Very good services!
Waitress saw that I was bringing my folding bike, quickly showed me a place to place my bike out of the way.
Ordering thru the QR code but waiter still came to check if we got our food. Only then we realized we didn’t place one order. Water was free flow, and waiter constantly checked on us if we needed anything.
Paying time was fast, didn’t have to wait too long. Price is acceptable for this location.

Tried the impossible burger - not bad at all. However fries were quite salty and accompany salad was underwhelming.

Mushroom soup portion size was huge and best for sharing. Otherwise it will be helpful if the restaurant offered a small and cheaper alternative - S / L choice for customers.

When ordering via their online link, it will be extremely useful if they indicated the ingredients / alternatives for vegeterians. Did not know what to expect in the pasta / sauces in the burgers without troubling the waiter to check with the kitchen.

Service was great though, nice personality and warmth.

Takashimaya Hegan- The Hunny Days pop up event.

Gotta admit that coming to Taka to get the hegan bottles is good marketing cos families will end up shopping more than usual, eating and walking around since “we’re in town”

If you have young children, the little ones will love the fountain at Taka, the aircon is cool enough for their naps. Plus if you’re feeling $$$ enough, take a walk at level 4 Taka cos after all it’s the children’s level.

The concourse always have events that you can walk around. Not forgetting the food, coffee, bubble tea.

The best part? It’s sheltered all the way from orchard MRT. That means if the weather is bad and it suddenly pours, you know you’re well sheltered.

Accessibility, great! Cos it’s now linked to NS and TEL line

Would I come again just to take a walk? Why not!?! But I might also wanna devise a plan that I can really sit, rest and relax.

Wonderful experience at the kids department at Takashimaya! We came by on a weekday morning (20 Jan) and was served by Michelle who was also the cashier.

She was friendly, patient and very service oriented which is a really a rarity nowadays.

She was knowledgeable and took the effort to demonstrate to us all the different products while also managing to explain each and every one of its functions.

When our preferred cot color was out of stock, she even went out of the way and arranged a delivery for us (which we were not aware was an available option)

Keep it up Michelle! Always appreciate excellent service👍🏻

The Gold Standard of Premium Shopping in Orchard! 🛍️✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
If you are looking for a world-class shopping experience in Singapore, Takashimaya is the ultimate destination. Located in the heart of Orchard Road, this Japanese department store combines luxury with incredible variety.
What makes it special:
• Everything Under One Roof: From high-end luxury brands like Chanel and Louis Vuitton to premium Japanese skincare and household goods, it truly has it all.
• The Food Hall (B2): A paradise for foodies! The basement level is famous for its incredible Japanese snacks, gourmet groceries, and the legendary annual mooncake or food fairs.
• Customer Service: True to its Japanese roots, the service here is impeccable—polite, efficient, and professional.
• Branded Children's Section: One of the best places in Singapore for high-quality kids' clothes and toys.
My Tip: Don't miss the Takashimaya Square on the basement level. There is almost always a massive sale or an interesting themed fair happening there. Also, if you are a tourist, remember to bring your passport to the customer service counter for tax refund forms!

Feels very China /HK vibe and decor but it’s really the love of Chinese and local Singaporean cuisine.

Love the familiarity yet fusion presentation of old local delights that are deconstructed and reimagined in very interesting culinary way

The food brings about familiarity and yet interesting textures and flavours brought together

Was a feast and enjoyable moment for my parents.

The staff was also attentive and very kind to help me get two candles on the desserts and sang Happy Birthday to my parents as well

We got the communal set ,though some items were not available but the chef was kind enuff to replace some of the items and let us have the communal set and it was great as I no need to rack my head on what to order but being able to taste test all the recommended dishes of the restaurant 🤤

Support local!

My partner and I came for dinner as we really wanted to try authentic Singaporean food that was safe to eat. Initially some of the reviews gave me doubts, but I’m so glad I trusted my intuition and the many positive reviews because Choon Hoy Parlor was fantastic!
The service was wonderful - both servers we encountered were super helpful and knowledgeable in recommending dishes to us, which didn’t disappoint!
The food was glorious - not too heavy or greasy, cooked to perfection.
Fairly priced and food came quickly.
We would definitely recommend coming here!

Very pleased with this find at Capitol! “Singapore soul food” - what that means I’m not sure, but the dishes we had were great. We ordered their Kueh Pie Tee, Bah Ku Teh, Dry Laksa, Assam Stringray, Duck, some pork ribs I think and a soup. Didn’t really touch the meats but I enjoyed the Laksa and Kueh Pie Tee was delicious. I had their Trio Orh Ni for dessert which I think might have been for sharing since it’s huge but I finished it all. Nice place and vibes. Service was a mixed bag but food made up for it.

Had a fantastic lunch experience trying out the limited-time menu at Twyst (Raffles Place MRT). The Butter Tandoori Pasta is excellent—very flavorful, creamy, and packed with a generous amount of chicken. If you can't make it to the CBD, glad to know this particular pasta is actually available islandwide!
However, if you are at the Raffles Place outlet, you definitely want to check out their exclusive Toasted Sandwich Stacks which are only available here for a short time. They are perfect for a fast grab-and-go lunch or to take away for a hassle-free dinner later.
Service was efficient, the food came out hot, and it’s a great addition to the daily lunch rotation. Will definitely be back!

First time here.

The food taste just average.  A bit pricey for the small portion served.  The mushroom soup was very diluted.

Only the fried chicken mid wings was delicious and memorable.

The air-conditioning is like not working at all.  The whole restaurant is very warm and the air is filled with fried food smell.  The smell sticks to our clothes when we exited.

A very disappointed dining experience.

It is often packed with office people working in Raffles Place. They have the build your pasta options as well as their signatures. They often launch limited edition pasta. I have always liked their pastas and tried their tomato pomodoro which comes with spinach, chicken and cherry tomatoes. Some colleagues like their aglio olio, smoked duck pasta, and creamy Alfredo. However, their pasta is on the oilier side and when I tried their miso butter smoked duck pasta, I knew it was a really bad choice. The whole bowl was drenched in butter and oil, and they were pretty stingy on the toppings like spinach. I could barely see much vegetables in the pasta. For 11.90 and a 30-45mins wait, it is definitely not one of my top choices for lunch on a typical weekday.
Very nearby to the hotel that we stayed, Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel. Travelling to Orchard Road or Gardens by the Bay was smooth.
It’s a long walk with a staircase to the exit, so it may not be ideal for elderly visitors. However, the lift tends to get very crowded, so please be considerate of their needs.

I was using this MRT to commute to work since the opening. This MRT is located near to many hotels. Many tourists use this MRT station everyday.

Although mrt station itself is clean, there is nothing improved or changed since the opening. There is no ATM, no convenience store, no money changer and feel very isolated mrt station.

But I gave 1 star review mostly because of the attitude of station staffs here. They aren't helpful to people at all. Every few week, I see lost tourists seeking help from them but they do not care to help them. I see people having heated arguments with station staffs.

Sometime, they have security check system at the gantry. But I have no idea what they are checking, but I got asked to go through security check every morning when I go to work. But my wife was never asked to. She was only asked once when she was with me. The station staffs here are so free and crazy; they want to stop and disturb the people who is going to work every morning.

The nearest Tiong Bahru mrt station is way better with friendlier station staffs and lots of atms and stores. Every year, after a week of going through those security check everyday, I walk a bit further from my house to Tiong Bahru mrt just to avoid those untrained security check. Ain't nobody got time to go through like airport security every morning just to go to work.

To my extended disappointment the food choose in pic were served cold. Except for the rice which was mildly warm. To me this is just local economical rice revamp to bento modern  concept. Nothing uniquely worthy for the price of $11.80. Most of the dishes I had were just flavoured with mala ingredients and nothing distinctive flavours.
To me the least for quick Chinese lunch the food should be honourably served warm even neighbourhood coffee shop economical rice is warmer than this.
Very nice Chinese style bento near my office. Worth trying！！
Bento box selection. Simple classic, ma tasting Sichuan dishes. Rice is fluffy good. Taste is accurate. We are in a aircon Cafe setting for consumption.

Super worth-the-money Japanese food at Bugis!

The truffle ramen had a super rich and comforting broth that came with a spoonful of truffle paste, and tender chashu pieces that was cooked so well 🔥 My fav dish of the night!

The sashimi platter had a good variety of fish, they were very fresh and had thick pieces. Beautiful presentation as well. Would definitely get this again!

The mentaiyaki kaisendon was the best kaisendon I had in sg. The torched mentaiko sauce was so good, heard from the owner that it’s house-made, not too jelak mentaiko. Sashimi pieces were also fresh and good with fluffy rice.

Tried the sparkling yuzu sake, surprisingly very good and was a hit amongst my group.

Overall, service was excellent, very attentive staff. Free miso soup as well, every main also came with a free side dish for their opening promo. Will definitely visit this jap spot again whenever i’m in the area.
Really enjoyed our meal, every item is amazing. The sashimi is really fresh. Lovely pairing with the sparkling yuzu sake. Highly recommended!

I had the ramen here and really enjoyed it! The broth was rich and comforting, the ingredients were great, and the portion was satisfying. The owners were super friendly and warm. Definitely one of those places I’ll be coming back to. Highly recommend!
